recent_reviews.text: I registered with Dr Ngan and Partners. I found my airway became allergic to dustmites from the carpets and oil smoke from kitchen . I am really confused about the diagnosis, and I hope my GP can help me clarify what is my symptoms.

recent_reviews.author: lisa mulligan
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this gp since I was 5 im now 22, it used to be good but recently I have been appalled by their actions, I had a cough for about a month and a doctor sent me to the hospital for a chest xray I then had to wait three weeks for that to go back to my doctors. In which time I went back and told a different doctor that it was getting worse he said and I quote "it will go, iv been a doctor for 25 years with people coughing and sneezing on me and I dont get sick, you dont need medicine". So I asked to see another doctor because I wasnt taking his word after what he said I then seen another doctor on the same day and she said my chest sounds crackly, my blood pressure was up and my temp was low, she sent me straight to the ACU ward at the hospital where they did blood and the doctor said there that oh you're fine you can go home. I said to them I dont feel fine its hard to breath and I have asthma at this point im now coughing, fever, sickness, sharp pain in my arm and dizzy. I went home like they said and now on christmas eve all this things have gotten worse and I have collapsed 3 times in 24 hours and I have had an asthma attack. Iv been dealing with this for over three months now and I have been given 2 sets of antibiotics and then taken off them half way through the course. its got to the point everytime I cough I need my inhaler other I will stop breathing its ridiculous and im fuming. recent_reviews.author: Rehab Sherif
recent_reviews.text: I had an extremely disappointing experience with this dentist. My appointment was 25 minutes long and I arrived 7 minutes late, due to the car park being full, having to find and pay for on-street parking, and arranging (and paying for) a babysitter to attend the appointment. I explained the situation clearly to the receptionist and asked for it to be relayed to the dentist. Despite this, the dentist showed no empathy or flexibility. After waiting six years to finally register with an NHS dentist since moving to Manchester, I was shocked to be told I would be taken off the register for being late once — something that, having worked in two dental practices myself, I have never known to be standard policy. What made the situation worse was the dentist’s behaviour: instead of speaking to me directly like a professional, he avoided the conversation entirely and hid behind a wall, while incorrectly claiming I was “over 10 minutes late.” This felt dismissive, unprofessional, and frankly inhumane. After such a long wait to access NHS dental care, this experience was incredibly upsetting. Patients deserve understanding, honesty, and basic respect — none of which were shown here.

recent_reviews.author: A A
recent_reviews.text: I cannot recommend the Vallance Dental Centre enough! Their professionalism and quality of service is second to none. I wanted to whiten my teeth and my dentist, Dr. George Cheesman, went through all the options with me and gave me the pros and cons of each program. In the end, I went for the Enlighten Teeth Whitening program and the results were spectacular. My teeth were noticeably whiter within just a few days and I had minimal sensitivity. In my final surgery appointment, I forgot to bring my trays, but Dr. George allowed me to go back home to get them and worked through his lunch break to allow me to finish the appointment today. Honestly, I can’t recommend him enough! Also, special thanks to Pauline and Abida for assisting with the final surgery appointment today. I would highly recommend the Vallance centre and Dr. George to everyone.

recent_reviews.author: lisa mulligan
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this gp since I was 5 im now 22, it used to be good but recently I have been appalled by their actions, I had a cough for about a month and a doctor sent me to the hospital for a chest xray I then had to wait three weeks for that to go back to my doctors. In which time I went back and told a different doctor that it was getting worse he said and I quote "it will go, iv been a doctor for 25 years with people coughing and sneezing on me and I dont get sick, you dont need medicine". So I asked to see another doctor because I wasnt taking his word after what he said I then seen another doctor on the same day and she said my chest sounds crackly, my blood pressure was up and my temp was low, she sent me straight to the ACU ward at the hospital where they did blood and the doctor said there that oh you're fine you can go home. I said to them I dont feel fine its hard to breath and I have asthma at this point im now coughing, fever, sickness, sharp pain in my arm and dizzy. I went home like they said and now on christmas eve all this things have gotten worse and I have collapsed 3 times in 24 hours and I have had an asthma attack. Iv been dealing with this for over three months now and I have been given 2 sets of antibiotics and then taken off them half way through the course. its got to the point everytime I cough I need my inhaler other I will stop breathing its ridiculous and im fuming. The hospital and the doctors say the same thing I dont know what to do im concentrating on making it through a day it feels like they dont care about their patients or what happens to them im seriously disappointed if it turns out that something bigger is going on with me im going to make a complaint and leave.

recent_reviews.author: Maria Wren Conyers
recent_reviews.text: Having moved from Essex to Manchester, I’ve done my due diligence to find a highly rated GP service, I signed onto Vallance Medical, and I believe in giving praise when it’s due. I have never come across a surgery so helpful and efficient whilst remaining highly professional. If you ring up to speak to a doctor, they usually ring you back within 30 minutes. They are warm and caring in their approach and if needed, offer you a same day face to face appointment. Where necessary, doctors will phone you with results from tests too. Since moving to Manchester, I have had to ask for a referral to the wheelchair service, which was done immediately - nothing is too much trouble for them. I think this can-do attitude filters from the top down. The courteous receptionists are not like Dragons trying to block your path from seeking medical attention, in fact it is the reverse, they are always trying to help you connect with whatever service you need and have good communications with the in-house pharmacy. In conclusion, I know I will be leaving Manchester within a year and if one could (which I know you can’t) I would travel from Essex to Manchester just to see this medical practice - they are without doubt, the best practice and as a professional who has worked in the NHS for over thirty years, I cannot praise them enough. Maria Conyers

recent_reviews.author: samrita shankar
recent_reviews.text: MEDICAL NEGLIGENCE! After having a horrible experience with Robert Darbishire Practice, I registered with Dr. Ngan and Partners in February 2023. At first, I was very impressed with how quickly I was able to get appointments with the doctors. However, things quickly took a turn for the worse. 1. A severe and persistent headache started on 2nd February 2023 and lasted for the whole of the month. This headache did not subside with any medications, even those for migraines. I then had two telephonic consultations with Dr. Ngan and Partners during which time the doctor agreed that it was probably a sinus headache and not a migraine. He prescribed sinus related medications both times, but the pain did not reduce. By this time three weeks had passed since the headache had started. I informed the doctor that the pain was excruciating and had me bedridden most of the time. I also requested the doctor for an MRI or CT scan during the second consultation but this request was denied. I was also not referred to a neurologist or an ENT specialist despite the nature, duration and intensity of the headache. 2. I also informed the doctor that I had visited the ER earlier in the month as the pain worsened but could not see the doctor due to the long waiting time, hoping this would convey how severe the headache gets sometimes. 3. I contacted Dr. Ngan and Partners for the third time on 24th February and got an in-person appointment for the same day. After conducting physical examinations, the doctor diagnosed it as a migraine and prescribed a migraine medication AGAIN, even after I told her that literally no medications were working. I requested for an MRI or CT scan referral twice during the consultation but my request was denied for the third time! She said "there is nothing specific that we are looking for that would turn up in the scans". Instead, she said she would refer me to a neurologist if the headache persisted for a few more days. By this time, it was the start of the 4th week since the headache had started. 4. On 26th February 2023, I had to call an ambulance as the pain exponentially increased, so much so that I felt like my right eye was about to pop out! I had fever and vomiting. I was told that because my vitals, etc., were normal, they will not be able to take me to the ER. I called Dr. Ngan on 27th hysterically crying and explained my situation. I requested for an urgent consultation with the doctor but was told that there was no possibility of getting an appointment that day or the next as all slots were full. 5. I told the doctors that I was first on Co-codamol as prescribed by the previous GP but the intensity reduced. I was then asked to use Ibuprofen during first consultation with Dr. Ngan. During the last consultation I told the doctor that I had been on Ibuprofen for 10 days straight but she still asked me to use it to control pain. 5. Having felt completely and utterly abandoned by the GP, I had to fly home, to India, on 28th to receive urgent medical treatment. It was a gruelling 22 hours of travel during which the pain almost killed me! Upon investigation after getting admitted in India, it was found that I had a rare and an extremely severe infection in the Sphenoid sinus. The scans revealed that the infection had progressed so much that if I had waited for a few more days to get treated, I would have lost vision in my right eye or suffered brain damage! The infection had broken down the wall between the sinus and the brain and had started seeping into the brain, and the only way out was to have an immediate surgery. I was also told that the constant use of the painkillers prescribed by the GP was the reason why I had started puking blood on 28th February. 6. PATIENT HISTORY MATTERS! I had told the GP that I had suffered a scuba diving injury in 2020 after which I suffered similar headaches. However, this was completely ignored. The doctors in India found out through scans that this infection had likely started after this incident, with its final trigger starting in 2023.

recent_reviews.author: M Mariah
recent_reviews.text: Had a very bad experience with dr elamin last summer , gave negative feedback through the website last year and no one has bothered to contact me . This dr prescribed me multiple rounds of flucanzole . Even though I had taken 6 months worth of this drug and it did not get rid of this thrush. Instead of referring me to a specialist straight away or doing a sensitivity swab, this dr decides to scream at me down the phone blaming this thrush on my lifestyle choices . There was one point where she prescribed me metronidazole gel and tells me this treats the bacteria that causes thrush. This is false . Metronidazole treats BV or trichomoniasis .i did not have either of these. No where on the NICE guidelines does it say metronidazole gel is second line or is treatment for thrush. I book tons of appointments in the summer and had put down in the e consult form that I wasn’t being taken seriously and then dr elamin finally refers me to gynaecology and gives me more flucanazole. I was then given a sensitivity swab by a different doctor. Come to find out this thrush strain is actually resistant to flucanzole.thats why it wasn’t going away I’m still experiencing this thrush and it has drastically impacted my quality of life. It baffles me that this practise hires doctors who are meant to “specialise in women’s health” but actually know nothing about it at all.

recent_reviews.author: Im Me
recent_reviews.text: My appointment was with Nurse Ozaz, and I originally attended just to have my bloods done. However, upon my arrival, she took the time to gather all the necessary information and carried out a full check including my weight, height, blood tests, and blood pressure. Although I only expected a simple blood test, she went above and beyond, and I’m truly grateful that she did. Her thoroughness allowed her to pick up on an issue that would have been missed if she had only carried out the blood test. I cannot thank her enough. This was my first time meeting her, but she made me feel completely comfortable and at ease. Professionals like her show how passionate they are about their work and how much they genuinely care for their patients. If everyone received the level of care I experienced today, the world would be a much better place. I wish there were a thousand more individuals like her. Her mannerism, politeness, caring approach, and positive attitude truly made me smile. I would like to say a very big thank you to her for going above and beyond. Never change, and always stay the wonderful person you are. You are a star, Nurse Ozaz.

recent_reviews.author: Ian Shelmerdine
recent_reviews.text: Feedback for Dr Bahemia I found the appointment a benefit since it was unexpected. My doctor was attentive, listened to my talk about my symptoms and concerns and shared their own options with a colleague to ensure they were giving me the best treatment. I was also impressed with the length of time for my appointment which ensured I did not feel rushed or stressed. However my one concern is that, because I am still having the symptoms and chest pain, no further investigation, apart from an echocardiogram, was agreed on to diagnose my problem and treat it. I have kept this feedback in the link reply since the review box was not blank when I opened the current link for Dr Shafiq. 5 star Dr Shafiq was very focused with the examination and ensured that the urgent nature of my consultation, due to 24 AmbBP results, was in no way something to worry about. He was receptive to the answers I gave during the consultation and made sure that the results of the AmbBP and ECG taken at the practice were explained in detail. His concern and subsequent decision based on the ECG and chest pain observed during my examination were explained and the need for further cardiac tests at the MRI understood. He was also firm in his insistence in my not walking or getting public transport to a and e. The correct decision which his persuasion got over to me. Once again I have been impressed by the care and service given by the practice and it's staff. I must also put a word in for the person who took the ECG readings and their professionalism and approach.

recent_reviews.author: Junaid Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: As a long-term patient (diagnosed with a life time illness since 2005) receiving continuous prescriptions and specialized care, I requested a paid private letter confirming the simple, medically accepted fact that chronic stress and hardship trigger flare-ups to my condition. The practice refused the request, claiming "insufficient evidence" a shocking statement considering my two decades as a patient for whom they have continuously prescribed, medication, are informed of my hospital ongoing treatment for years (Vedolizumab, etc.) and liaised with the hospital IBD team. This refusal demonstrates a failure to understand the patient they are treating. Crucially, this contradiction occurred even though I attached an older letter from my specialist consultant where this clinical fact was already written and acknowledged. This extreme administrative obstacle wasted significant time and energy, forcing me to change GPs due to their unwillingness to support a chronic patient.

recent_reviews.author: JUNAID AHMED
recent_reviews.text: I was a long-term patient with multiple chronic conditions, including ulcerative colitis, arthritis, and migraines — all of which were regularly managed through prescriptions and hospital treatments. I requested a simple private letter confirming my diagnosis and how stress can affect my condition — something a hospital consultant had previously provided. Despite being willing to pay the £35 fee, the practice refused to provide the letter and didn’t offer an appointment to discuss it. As someone managing serious long-term health issues, I found this response dismissive and lacking in basic patient support. I’ve since moved to a new GP who I hope will be more patient-focused. I’m sharing this to help others understand what kind of support they might — or might not — receive here if they have complex or ongoing health needs. To the management: the decline in care became noticeable after COVID. If you’re genuinely reviewing patient experiences, it may be worth examining the internal changes made during and after the pandemic — because that’s when the ship started sinking.

recent_reviews.author: Carla
recent_reviews.text: I wish my first experience with a GP here in England would have been a better one, but this practice is appalling in all its aspects. To start with, somehow they never received my NHS number. It took me eight months of endless phone calls to convince a secretary to call the authorities. One of the secretaries I spoke with even gave me a number to call myself in order to ask for my NHS number. The lady that replied at the phone was shicked that I had been given this number, as the only people they speak with are surgery employees and not patients. As a result of this I couldn't get any type of referral for almost a entire year. Even when I finally did get my NHS number and asked for a referral, it never arrived. The doctor that sees me is incompetent at best. The few times I went in, she almost tried to convince me I was fine. Her behaviour was so dismissive that I almost felt like I had to justify myself for being sick. I started dreading getting ill and postponing the time I had to see a doctor because their uselessness almost started to scare me. Needless to say, it is impossible to get an appointment on the same day (or on the following days, for what it is worth) and if you do have something serious you might as well stay sick, or go directly to the hospital, because I doubt anything ever gets done here. I am sorry that such a surgery it is even allowed to stay open. They are an example of medicine at its worst.

We do offer same-day appointments, and although the vast majority of our patients are seen on the day they contact us, very occasionally, appointments can run over, or patients may need to be scheduled for the following day if it is safe to do so - which was likely the case here. Please be reassured that if your condition had been critical, urgent treatment would have been arranged immediately. The fact that your appointment could be scheduled for the next day indicates your condition was stable and it was safe to do so. We also want to gently remind patients that if a condition feels critical, emergency services such as A&E should be contacted instead of the GP practice as we are not an emergency service that can deal with critical conditions. We know how frustrating it is to sit and wait in a phone queue in the morning. If you are able to, you can use our online form system which is available 24/7. I hope you will find this easier. We appreciate your feedback and hope you continue to feel supported by our practice as we strive to provide safe, compassionate care for all our patients. Kind Regards, Lauren, Engagement & Communications Officer

recent_reviews.author: BobShawBirch
recent_reviews.text: I have used Robert Darbishire Practice for a number of years. In recent years their triage arrangements have become very efficient, prompt and reassuring in the light of what I learn in the press about other practices. My online enquiries are dealt with on the same day by pre-arranged phone appointment (notified by email or text) from a relevant health practitioner - usually a GP - and advice provided by phone or by surgery visit. Their monitoring of my health conditions (annual health checks) have always been prompt. Data emerging from, for example, blood tests, are provided within one week and, where issues emerge (either from me or the GP) are dealt with by further telephone appointment. I feel fortunate to be a registered patient at this practice.

recent_reviews.author: Saqib Javed
recent_reviews.text: I am having a horrible experience with this surgery for some time now. In order to get a simple blood test done, I had two appointments cancelled by the surgery with a text message sent a couple of hours before the appointments citing staff absences/shortages. Finally, the test went ahead on the third occasion. On another occasion my 7 year old son was given appointment almost a month after I rang them to get a simple blood test. Finally, on the day of his appointment we were just 2 min late and the receptionists turned us away saying you are late and the nurse is very busy today. I asked her to speak to the nurse and she refused to do so saying "I know her answer already she wont see you". I am registered with this surgery for more than 10 years and never in my experience I was seen on time. The surgery is always running between 10 to 30 mins late into each appointment and the patients are supposed to wait until finally seen by someone. This is not fair on patients as the surgery expects them to wait for the doctor or the nurse when they are running late whereas if the patient is one minute late they don't bother to see us even if we are willing to wait. I don't see the logic in it. If I am two minutes late with a child that means someone else must be seen during my time slot then why can't I wait and be seen in the slot of the patient who is seen before his/her appointment. Technically speaking, from the 10 mins slot allocated to me I still had 8 minutes remaining and I know the blood tests only take 5 mins.

recent_reviews.text: I have been having issues with this GP for the last few months however yesterday I was experiencing intense pain in my lower back and even had to come home from my shift due to the pain. Today morning I woke up early to book an appointment and was told to come in at 3:00pm I arrived there at 2:40pm and checked in but I was forced to sit there until 4:00pm. I then went to ask about my appointment and I was told that the doctor had gone home. After waiting for more than an hour with severe pain and with no one even acknowledging my existence then they told me to book another appointment for the following day I was infuriated as I have never felt so helpless . I then asked to speak to the manager who was then able to fit me in to see a doctor but I was so overwhelmed by the terrible treatment that I couldn't even explain myself properly to the doctor and have now been sent home with painkillers. and I will be transferring to a different GP ASAP after months of them getting my hopes up and cancelling my appointments last minute. I hope people find this review helpful

recent_reviews.text: This surgery has been deteriorating rapidly over recent years. I have been registered for over 30 years and used to have confidence in the service offered. recent_reviews.author: Mia Smith
recent_reviews.text: Some really nice staff but on the whole this is the most incompetent and negligent GP practice's I have ever been to. They messed up my registration which they did admit fault and apologies for but it caused me to miss 2 weeks of prescription. Got a call back to book a blood test- get to the day of my appointment it was never put into the system. Got the blood test at a later date but get very conflicting information about the results. -Used the online system to requested a GP appointment regarding blood test- I get an email saying literally just "your results are normal" and no offer of appointment. When I rung up to get some detail I found out some things couldn't be tested because the sample spoiled and they want a retest- that's fair enough it happens- but there was no mention of that on the email. recent_reviews.author: Νεφέλη Πάσχου
recent_reviews.text: Extremely uncaring reception staff - aside from frequently experiencing issues with them being full (even if forms are filled in the morning), if you receive a phone call that you cannot take right then, chances are that you will miss your appointment entirely. The "doctors will call back" response I have received from reception if I call them directly is often a lie as well, as I have had to personally ring them back again due to not receiving a call back. I appreciate that the demand might be high and something might get overlooked, but giving misleading expectations should not be acceptable, and should at least be met with an apology when it happens. An example of missing an appointment was when I was in the toilet (due to the pain I was experiencing from my issue), called back within 10 mins, and was met with a rude response and no alternative, just a "try again tomorrow". I almost always receive calls after 5pm no matter how early I fill in the form as well, which as you can imagine, makes scheduling hell and it is extremely difficult to ever be seen. It's at the very least disappointing to experience no sympathy or understanding from staff. Effort to help patients/introduce alternative appointment methods should be higher, especially since the form system clearly has tons of issues, and reliance on GP services is very high right now.

recent_reviews.text: Worst surgery ever! I dont even know where to begin. Needed urgent blood test done of my children. After 13 cancellations and 2 times they lost the blood sample we finally got the result and the doctor wanted to repeat the test. We took time of work on many occasions but they just cancel the appointment last minute. I am just so fed up of dealing with them that I havent been to GP in years. Obviously I have to take my children in when they are unwell and then I have to deal with all this. I have been really unwell and filled in a form this week where I clearly stated I am having occasional chest pain and difficulty breathing for last few weeks along with other things. Well got a call back and the doctor spoke to me about one symptoms I am not too worried about and booked in a blood test next week for it. I told her about the chest pain again and she said she will see me after the blood test and talk about this!!! I've decided to go A&E as these doctors clearly dont know what they are doing! Avoid like plague! This place is abolute chaos.

Thank you for your review. We appreciate any reviews we receive whether they be positive or negative as they help us to improve the service we offer to patients. Here at The Robert Darbishire Practice, we believe that collaboration is key. We have many doctors that have different specialities and encourage other doctors to call on them when they need help with treating a patient. We apologise that you’re unhappy with a member of our team getting a second opinion, but we believe that it better than leaving a problem untreated or offering the wrong solution. We also help to train budding doctors from the local University and give them the valuable first-hand experience of working in a GP surgery. When this happens, each trainee is paired with a qualified GP, and is expected to double-check their diagnosis and treatment with their mentor to ensure it is correct. There are many reasons why a doctor may search online for treatment options. This could be to find patient resources, to double check treatment plans or to check the medication is appropriate. Our team are highly skilled and highly trained, but with their being millions of conditions, diseases and illnesses, we would not expect our team to recall every single one and allow them to use proper resources should they need them. I think it is worth noting that some conditions take time to resolve, and many conditions are similar to others. Whilst we wish we were able to cure everyone immediately, that is not always possible, and it may take time to see results. We apologise you’re not satisfied with the service offered to you. If you would like to register with another GP service, you are able to find one close to you using the NHS website. Kind Regards, Lauren, Engagement & Communications Officer

recent_reviews.author: Naya Rehman
recent_reviews.text: My mother has been a patient at this practise for years now. She has learning difficulties and suffers with mental health problems. She has had ADHD assessments and additional tests done to find out what her diagnosis was, she was told to hand in this paper work to the reception at the practise (before covid) they misplaced all these documents with all her initial assessments and results in there. Since then she has been on several different medications unsure of what it is actually tackling, she has gained weight due to the medication she’s been given. Her doctors have given her numerous numbers to call to redo them assessments and figure out on her own what she has - which she is still on waiting lists for. She doesn’t get a face to face review with her doctor regularly, only last year a mental health nurse rang her up, as it got extreme, however she’s been suffering with severe mental health her entire life. I’m 20 years old and struggle with my own mental health as I have been supporting my mother my entire life and have been on the other end of her episodes which she hasn’t received the right/enough support for. Wouldn’t recommend this practise especially if your suffering with mental health as it isn’t as prioritised.

recent_reviews.author: Eron Ameen
recent_reviews.text: This GP needs a lot of more improvements, when you want an appointment, they tell us do it online rather than book for us straight away over the phone, physical appointments almost don’t exist anymore! then the doctor rings us in unexpected time while we are busy.
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Eron AmeenLocal Guide · 30 reviews3 years ago This GP needs a lot of more improvements, when you want an appointment, they tell us do it online rather than book for us straight away over the phone, physical appointments almost don’t exist anymore! then the doctor rings us in unexpected time while we are busy.Like2 Share Response from the owner 3 years agoHello Eron. Thank you for your review. We do encourage patients who are able to use the e-consult system to do so as this allows our reception team more time to help those patients who aren't able to use the internet. Our reception team also do not book appointments, they only request them - the same as when you submit an online form. A doctor or a nurse will then triage your request and decide what course of action is needed, whether that be a prescription, telephone consult or face to face appointment. Along with our e-consult system, we do also operate a telephone triage system. This means that all patients will be given a phone call first and if it's needed, will be invited into the surgery for a face to face appointment. We've found that telephone consultations have been really beneficial and have allowed patients to get the help they need from the comfort of their own home. We'll always try our best to call at a time that suits you but can't always guarantee this will happen as the demand for appointments is really high at the moment and we try and help as many people as we possibly can throughout the day. To make sure that patients do not miss their appointment, we also call twice throughout the day to reach you. If you aren't available at a certain point in the day, please make sure you let us know on your request so your doctor or nurse is clear on when they can and can't reach you. We do hope that in the future you will have a more positive experience with us here at The Robert Darbishire Practice. Kind Regards, Lauren, Engagement & Communications Officer

recent_reviews.author: Elspeth Woolsey
recent_reviews.text: Go elsewhere. I'm exhausted with this Practice. I have ignored quite a few things but will be looking elsewhere as they could raise your blood rather than help. I'm not a fan of their online system (but that's my preference) and after waiting over 20mins, was then told to explain my symptoms online. When the doctor phoned she was completely fixed on previous blood tests I'd had done for my autoimmune condition and kept referring to those bloods even though I'd spoken to a specialist nurse about it and have an appointment regarding it later in the week. This is not the first time this type of response has happened and I'm sick of a doctors practice getting fixated on my autoimmune disease rather than the issue I've come with - I'm aware they could and can be related but it would be nice to have the issue investigated rather than just put under the umbrella of my auto-immune disease but she completely ignored me telling her ho my body had been feeling leading up the issue. I was, thankfully, prescribed medication (based on the previous time this happened - why they don't want to investigate it beyond ridiculous!), I asked for this to be sent to the pharmacy next to them and was asked "What's the name of that pharmacy"(?!?) I googled to tell her and she said she'd send the appointment there. I walked there during my lunch hour to be told they hadn't received it, went to the doctors and wait ed 5-10mins for the receptionist machine to load up before telling me it was at a different pharmacy!! (Again, not the first time they've done this this when I asked for it to be sent to this pharmacy!) The nurses are the best thing about this place but I'm fed up with the lack of care or interest from doctors - I'm aware of my body, so am also aware when something is not right. It might be good if you could listen to to your patients and go from there.

It is completely unsuitable for anyone in work or study - to get any sort of appointment, you have to wait all day on a ringback from a doctor or nurse who wants a 10 second soundbite of your problem before deciding whether your issue is worthy enough to get an appointment. The receptionists refuse to give you a time for this ringback - it could be at any point during the day and if you miss it you've screwed. What if I am driving, at work, in a meeting, in the shower? Patients should not have to sit by their phones all day to receive basic medical care. On top of this, when you enter the waiting room it is crowded and often noisy and the staff are running late - I've sat there for 30 minutes on occassion and felt physically anxious as a result. Perhaps you could take on fewer patients (and make less money) but provide an accessible service so I feel like I can actually use the NHS? The only upside is that most of the staff I have encountered have been nice apart from a rude Nurse Practioner and GP.

recent_reviews.text: Due to an ongoing and chronic condition, I have to contact the practice often. Most of the staff are lovely and are very helpful and empathetic. However, there is one member of staff that deals with prescription enquiries that often has me in tears afterwards. Her name is 'Becks' (not sure on spelling) and has a well spoken accent. Whenever I call to ask about my prescriptions (sometimes there's an issue with them being sent electronically) she'll interrupt me whilst I'm trying to explain which is incredibly frustrating as I'm often 'woolly' headed due to my medication. God forbid if I ever ask her to check to see if it was ever sent or if my prescription needs collecting from the practice, she'll sigh really loudly as though I'm an inconvenience. I dread calling when there's an issue as I know I'm going to have to speak to her. The other ladies I've spoken to regarding my prescriptions have been so helpful and will do whatever they can to help.

recent_reviews.author: Hamaad Farooq
recent_reviews.text: I visited the surgery today while in severe pain and was told my prescription would be sent to the pharmacy. I went to the pharmacy but the prescription had not been sent. I returned after one hour and it was still not there. When I called the surgery, the receptionist told me to wait another hour while they checked with the doctor. When someone is in severe pain and unable to drive, delays like this are extremely frustrating and unacceptable. The doctor was kind and helpful, but the communication and urgency from reception staff needs serious improvement. What is also frustrating is that when staff are rude it seems to be accepted, but when a patient in severe pain becomes frustrated it is quickly labelled as “abuse.” Patients deserve to be treated with understanding and respect, especially when they are in pain and asking for urgent help.

recent_reviews.author: Sani Vlogs
recent_reviews.text: The reception staff are extremely rude and fail to provide clear instructions when their systems are down. Instead, they assume patients should already know what to do. Communication among reception staff is poor, and speaking through the reception desk does not work properly. As a result, patients are often told “we can’t hear you” in an aggressive manner, rather than the issue being addressed professionally. Even when booking appointments, inappropriate comments are sometimes made when more than one person requires an appointment. In contrast, the doctors are absolutely lovely. They communicate clearly, are respectful, and provide excellent support. Unfortunately, this positive experience is undermined by the behaviour of the reception staff. Reception staff clearly require additional care, communication, and customer service training. Regardless of experience or length of time in the role, rudeness is unjustifiable in a healthcare setting. Professionalism, politeness, and clear communication should be a basic standard at all times.

recent_reviews.author: Nadeem Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: My two young children were unwell, so I booked an appointment Hawthorn Medical walk in centre for 10:00 am. I finished my self-employed work early in order to take them to the surgery and arrived around 9:30 am, hoping to be seen on time. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing. The reception staff were rude and appeared completely uninterested. By 10:30 am, I noticed that patients with appointments scheduled after mine were being called in the walking centre (not GP ROOM), while we were still waiting. When I politely questioned this, I was spoken to rudely and told to go to A&E if I was “in a rush”. My children were crying and exhausted, having been unwell and unable to sleep properly all night. I was hoping for some reassurance and relief by having them seen by a doctor. To make matters worse, I overheard a patient with a 10:30 am appointment being taken straight into the walk in doctor’s room, yet my children were not seen until 11:30 am. I cannot understand why this happened. In total, the doctor saw six other patients before finally agreeing to see us, and only after my patience had completely run out as my children were coughing continuously. When we were eventually seen, I received nothing more than a hollow apology. The doctor casually advised me to continue giving paracetamol, despite the fact that my other two children had been prescribed antibiotics for the same condition just two weeks earlier. I felt that the doctor was displeased because I had stood up for my rights, but I strongly believe that had I not spoken out, we may have been left waiting for several more hours. The whole experience was sad and deeply frustrating. This incident makes me seriously question how this surgery has received an “Outstanding” CQC rating.BRIBERY perhaps

recent_reviews.author: Fabio
recent_reviews.text: EDIT 2: One year has passed and they are still not able to do their job properly. They have been able to forgot about one prescription (left me without medications) and made an incomplete one. They literally put people in danger for their inability of doing their most basic duties. Don't choose them as your gp. Don't do this to yourself. EDIT: Can you imagine calling your GP because somebody stole your purse with your DAILY MEDICATIONS inside and all they can tell you is to send an email and you will get your medications 4 days after? This is the Hawthorn medical centre in 2024. NO ALTERNATIVES offered, they just repeated email and wait 4 days. Isnt this time they should shut down? How can the NHS afford a clinic with this poor level of customer service? ----------- In the last 4-5 years, the efficiency of this medical centre declined until it reached the point that every time I ask to repeat a prescription, there is a problem. I don't know if it's the doctor's fault or the admin, the latest issue is that I don't appear registered there anymore for some reason, altho I confirmed 2 months ago, filling a form, that I live in the area. This comes after a long and persistent history of mistakes, neglect and miscomunications between the staff of the surgery. Many times, when I go even urgently to the pharmacy there are no medications to collect because the surgery had a problem with it without telling me anything. Fifteen days ago I was suppose to have a medication's review with a doctor that was supposed to call me: they didn't. Instead they just unregistered me from the medical centre, picking an old address of mine, that I communicated one year and a half ago, that was too far for me to get registered in the surgery, WITHOUT TELLING ME ANYTHING even tho I am a patient with a permanent disability. This is lack of consideration toward the health of their patients. A big lack of inefficiency. I do really hope that the medical centre will close down soon because there is no point of being there if they are not able to do their job

recent_reviews.author: Brontë Schiltz
recent_reviews.text: I had a frankly shocking experience at this walk-in centre. I spoke to a nurse called Jackie, who was rude from the outset, challenging my use of the term 'boils' (which is used on the NHS website and was used by a doctor I previously saw about the same kind of infection), then gave me instructions on treating insect bites when the bite I showed her was very clearly infected and my actual reason for calling was that it had transferred to my face, and a boil I had on my face previously became extremely painful and the NHS website says to see a doctor if you get one on your face. She finally agreed to see me after saying that I "clearly wouldn't accept that it was an insect bite" (I never challenged this, just stated that the bite was clearly infected and that I seemed to have spread that infection to my face, which was why I called), and as soon as I arrived, told me that I was overreacting, even denying that the boil on my face was red, hot and inflamed, which it very clearly was. A simple glance at my medical record would show that I have only sought medical attention twice previously since moving to Manchester in 2018, once when I couldn't breathe and once for the aforementioned previous boil, and I waited over a week to seek care in that instance because I have a bit of a phobia of medical settings. I showed her the scars from three previous boils for which I had not sought medical care, and she reluctantly agreed to give me antibiotics but said that I would ruin my immune system if I "kept taking them for things like this", to which I said again that I had not had antibiotics since the first boil on my face around Christmas 2020, and she just sarcastically said "okay". She then gave me a prescription for penicillin, and when I said that I am allergic to penicillin, she challenged this, saying that if all I'd had was a rash then I probably wasn't allergic. I said that I didn't know what my reaction had been since it happened when I was a young child but that it had been diagnosed by a doctor, and she chastised me for not mentioning my allergy sooner, when I had presumably reasonably assumed that it would be on my medical record. She was incredibly confrontational and condescending throughout, insinuating that I was wasting her time when providing healthcare is her job, there was nobody else in the waiting room when I went in, and she saw me 40 minutes after our agreed time, during which I was missing work at my job (at a homelessness charity) which I had to catch up on in my own time. I didn't complain about this because I understand that nurses are very busy, but I didn't appreciate being treated like a hypochondriac when I so rarely seek medical attention and my own time is also valuable. As I was leaving, she again reiterated instructions on responding to bites, which at this point I had stated multiple times was not the reason for my visit. I have a chronic pain condition and do not complain of pain unless it is extremely bad. Hugely disappointing overall.

recent_reviews.author: Polly Williams
recent_reviews.text: Attended this walk in centre with my husband after being advised from our local pharmacy after he had been stung by an insect and had an infected finger. We were going away the next day so didn’t have time to see our GP and didn’t want to waste resources at A and E. The Receptionist very rude when I rang to see if there was availability and abrupt when we arrived and seemed to have a bad attitude.we Waited approx 1.5 hours to be seen. We saw the “Nurse Paula “who was very abrupt and we was in and out within 2 minutes. My husband explained the pharmacist had told him to come as he needed antibiotics as it was Infected. She said it wasn’t infected and “the pharmacist had no right to say we could have antibiotics “ she also commented she would not give us them “ just because we were going away” The following day we travelled to Southampton. My husband developed a rash and became unwell. Again we visited the local pharmacy who said she did not like the look of the rash. She directed us to the local walk In centre. We were seen my friendly helpful staff who took the time to explain about the infection. The nurse requested he was seen by a GP. The GP reported my husband did have an infection and prescribed antibiotics. Such a different experience of two walk in centres. The staff were so much more helpful in Southampton than in our own city of Manchester. If I could award this walk in centre a zero I would.

recent_reviews.author: Pi7on -
recent_reviews.text: I was with this medical centre for 4 years whilst I was at uni. The receptionists are great and the nurse is good. In relation to the two doctors there - Dr Garson and Dr Locham - I would say this. First, I used Dr Garson: he seems to be a competent doctor, at least this was the impression I got from a few phone appointments I had with him. However, when I had my first virtual video-appointment (due to Covid-19) he disappointed me for his lack of manners. This is because I had more than one health issue to report/get his advice on, and as soon as I finished the first one and moved to the second, he said: 'now, we will treat this issue, and once this is sorted, you can talk about the others', and when I was trying to explain that they were related, he basically closed down the video-appointment on my face (just like that!). After this, I changed my GP to Dr Locham. However, this GP also has a problem: he rushes you like he needs to catch a train ASAP! This is particularly unpleasant when you are trying to explain a difficult health issue and he interrupts you and makes you feel like you are wasting his time. So, if you have other options and do not fancy being mistreated or rushed through, maybe look elsewhere. Having said that, both seem to be knowledgeable doctors though.

recent_reviews.author: Jackie taylor
recent_reviews.text: The Bodey Medical Centre is the embodiment of why our NHS was created. Compassion for their patients and the family that care for them. I found myself in a situation, where my father needed an urgent care plan, and I didn't know what to do, I felt as if I was drowning. I call my dad's GP surgery for help because I didn't know what to do. The initial call to the receptionist, was so calming and reassuring. Within 10 mins after that phone call, the Dr Patel called me and asked about my concerns for my dad. As I was explaining the circumstances, she paused the conversation and enquired if I had support and about my well being. That for me, was the most beautiful gesture that will stay with me forever. After getting all the information she needed, Dr Patel contacted the Crisis team. Within 15 mins of my ending the all with Dr Patel, I received a call from the crisis team. It took less than 4 hrs, from my initial phone call to the surgery, to my dad having a complete care plan in place and equipment installed for his safety. A perfect example of team work, that worked hand in hand with each other and have given my father and I the best outcome. I would like all who were involved in the creation of my dad's care, to know how grateful my family and I are, because if it wasn't for your actions, my father may not be here today. Thank you

recent_reviews.author: Emilija Mac
recent_reviews.text: The nurses and doctors at this practice are nice and helpful and I’d give them 5 stars, however wouldn’t say the same about reception. Have moved out of my old home over 2 YEARS AGO, Bodey Medical Centre was one of the first places I contacted to inform. Just found out that they’ve not changed it… And I have an ongoing issue, so I’ve been to the practice loads during those two years. I wonder how much time it would have saved me if they did and I received medical letters to my current address rather than the old one. A lady that works in the afternoon reception is incredibly rude and makes you feel like you’re dumb.. Another thing, although it is not the first time, but most recently I had a few appointments only to find out once I’m in the practice that I have no appointments for that day and time. Came the second time, apparently I’m too late although I’ve triple checked with the receptionist to be 100% sure while we were arranging the time over the phone. When I finally got to see the doctor, she said she had the same times and dates as me, and was waiting for me but I never showed up (I did, both times, but thanks to constant reception mess up, the doctor never knew that I was there waiting). So many work holidays are wasted on their mess ups.. Lastly, I was invited to make an appointment, and once I came to it, the doctor said that (again) it must be a reception mess up as I’m not due for that appointment until 2024..

recent_reviews.author: Sally B
recent_reviews.text: Went back today to get my blood taken and was so impressed by the nurse, she was so understanding, reassuring and professional (I'm scared of needles) and allowed me to touch her hand as she put the needle in which made me feel a lot more in control. I was also very impressed with the patience of the rest of the staff, there was another family waiting and perhaps English wasn't their first language (I've been there when I've lived abroad and its scary when you don't feel confident with the language when going to the doctors) and they were so patient and kind with them even though it took a little longer and there was a bit of a queue. It doesn't seem like much, and it should be normal to be so patient but having been in their situation I can tell you that not everyone is so kind. Makes me so happy to see so much compassion, even when the health service is going through a tough time. Thank you.

recent_reviews.author: M Mos
recent_reviews.text: This has the potential to be a great practice - the staff are pleasant, doctors are kind and knowledgeable - but unfortunately there are a couple of points that really let it down. First of all, the booking system is a nightmare. Phone lines open at 8:30am for appointments the same day. By 9:00am you can be pretty certain that there will be none left (if you can get through). This is particularly stressful when trying to book a follow-up appointment for a medication review or for test results, as you are told that you will have to go through the same procedure the following day ad infinitum until finally you get through. I think the longest I have pursued this is two weeks, ringing every day at the specified time - constantly ringing, hundreds of times. This has resulted in not being able to access necessary medication and not being able to discuss test results despite being asked by the doctor to book a subsequent appointment. Because getting an appointment is so difficult, it is equally as difficult to see the same doctor consistently which can be troublesome when trying to resolve an ongoing issue and often results in taking up more time within the appointment. There was talk of an online booking system but at last look this wasn't operational. I understand this is a busy practice and that the same day booking is aimed at reducing the number of people that don't turn up for booked appointments but in reality, it serves to punish the people that always turn up.

recent_reviews.text: I've been coming here for years so I have comments only as a young adult, I don't know how they are for children or the elderly. The staff are sometimes friendly, I've had some impatient and dismissive GPs and receptionists, and I've had very kind ones. TLDR I don't know if this is better or worse than other practices but IF you get an appointment it's ok...just don't bother calling between 8.30 am and 2 pm (12-2 is lunch)

recent_reviews.author: Tony Barlow
recent_reviews.text: I've waited over 3 weeks for a phone consultation despite contacting the surgery because I'm in extreme pain and being told that I would have to have a phone consultation first to be assessed. I've even contacted the surgery a second time to see if the appointment could be brought forward only to be told thar there aren't any other appointments available and that I would have to try ringing at 8am each morning to see if I can get one...a bit difficult when I start work at 7am and drive for a living. Finally got to the day of my appointment only to receive a text message saying that the doctor had tried to get through but couldn't. That's a bit strange because I received the text 5 minutes after I had allegedly been called and also rang the surgery straight back at 16:43 who said the doctor called at 16:28 . Amazing isn't it that I can get through to the surgery but the doctor couldn't get in contact with me when I was in the same location...then again it is getting close to home time after a very long day so why try any harder than you have to. I've now got a appointment with the out of hours doctor in two days time...pity I wasn't offered this earlier. The surgery has gone down the pan and doctors are exploiting the phone consultation.

recent_reviews.author: Roz
recent_reviews.text: 20 years ago Dr Faulkner told me I had IBS without first testing for other causes. Yet on my file it is listed as "suspected IBS" so not formally diagnosed despite being told it was. You cannot diagnose IBS without ruling out other issues. Celiac runs in my family, but it could also be IBD. So been possibly living with either of these untreated for 20 years. Also refused my Right to Choose for ADHD diagnosis (details of which are below, as this was my first reason for the negative review), and had to go private and turns out I do in fact have ADHD. Also failed my Mother in multiple ways, who has now died unexpectedly this year ----- FINAL EDIT: P-UK got in touch personally with Dr Faulkner (only contact they could find) and were ignored. They don't wish to help at all so I'll be switching GP. EDIT: Responded to my letter, basically saying they do not have funding for Bolton, when P-UK have the authority of NHS England that any NHS England patient is eligible for treatment with them under the Right to Choose. I'm now having to follow up. Also, what health centre does not have a way of contacting them online? ----- Really disappointed. Sent a letter to ask to be referred to a specialist (under my Right to Choose) to see if I potentially have ADHD and have had no follow up almost a month later. I'm sure my letter, sent by Signed for Delivery and received, was ignored or thrown away, despite me taking the time to write it and filled in forms which could indicate that I have it and I should be referred. Can't get into the clinic to see someone and ask (though I sent a letter so I'd have some evidence of it). No one has sent a letter or called me. This year has has been extra difficult for me and was hoping I could figure it out so I could get possibly CBT (therapy) to manage it but the clinic do not wish to help. Happy to speak to someone on the phone if they phone me about it, but last time I called about another issue they didn't even know what had happened.

recent_reviews.text: AVOID AVOID AVOID If I could gove zero stars I would, this has taken a while for me to write. Been with the surgery since birth never changed from the area I live in. I had literally just had a baby and within the first week of giving birth contacted the surgery to register him. Not only was I told this wasn't possible due to my area I was then told I was to find another doctor as I was also out the area due to changes within area restrictions. I explained I had just given birth and had been with them myself for over 30 years to which I was told well I'm sure you will find another doctor, I also explained my concerns over my new babies vaccinations and also his health check an my own, I was told we will send all details over but it can take 8 weeks. I was mortified in tears and emotions all over the place to which I was met with a cold non helpful response an one point a laugh, I didn't find this a funny situation at all I was in a vulnerable position and then had to find myself an my newborn baby a doctor. Also my eldest son was registered with this surgery but at no point was it mentioned he had to be removed it made no sense! I Pleaded to stay with the surgery as I felt comfortable with to be met with we have already removed you whilst on the phone I suggest you find somewhere else. Absolutely disgusting. I removed my eldest son from them as I do not want him to have to deal with surgery and reception staff who work within it. I also accept surgeries have to adhere to changes of area etc but I do not accept how it was dealt with and how I left after just having a baby the most vulnerable position a women could be in! I am so glad I found elsewhere who immediately arranged checks for my baby an myself an ensured all vaccinations where taken care of.

recent_reviews.author: Philip Crossley
recent_reviews.text: Lottery appointment system, You need to call between 8am to 8:30am to win a appointment, but everyone else is also calling at the same time. If your call actually connects during this period, congratulations you have a ticket that gets you a 30% chance of an appointment ( providing they have not all been taken already) , if not try the lottery again the next day. You have 1/5 chance for an appointment if you follow my advice. I have a hack for those needing urgent doctor, use all the phones you can get access to and call them one after another, one will likely get through. Edit: It is possible now to go into the doctors before 8 am to obtain a golden ( yellow ) ticket, which helps you bypass the lottery phone system and be seen the same day. While the lottery system is not ideal, I can see its a way to deal with a already struggling health system and therefore I am rating this place higher for finding a way to deal with a failing system. (+2 stars )

recent_reviews.author: Peter Mason
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this practice for over 12 years, whilst it can be difficult sometimes to get an appointment, you can always turn up on the day and wait. As this is a first come first served system you will have to wait your turn. They operate a card system before they actually open so if you get there at say 07:30 and you're the first person there, pick the card marked 1 and when the practice opens at 09:00, book yourself in you will be seen first, simple! Get there after 09:00 go to the window they will book you in and you wait until your name appears on the wall message, again simple! If the waiting room looks full don't despair, many of those might be waiting for other services like nursing services, flue jabs, or child inoculations etc. If you are a registered patient and you need to speak to your GP but not necessarily see your GP you can ring, ask to speak to them and after a few questions from the staff they will decide if it might be better you attend in person if necessary or if not they will include you on a ring back from your own GP. When your GP either finds time between patients or at the end of the patients in the waiting room, you will receive a call back by your GP, again simple... I don't understand some of the complaints I have seen posted, Yes sometimes the staff could friendlier, but they too are human, with their own problems, and the person before you might have been one of those self centered winging buggers who turn up on the day hoping to jump in front of all those other patients who have appointments . Yes the list might be long, but that's because there are a lot of patients who are HAPPY with the services provided you DUMMY! So stop winging, get there early, pick a card, book yourself in, sit yourself down, and wait like everyone else!!!

recent_reviews.author: Hina Mistry
recent_reviews.text: I have edited this review as one of the drs asked me to change it: I am deeply disappointed with the care at this practice. Despite experiencing severe symptoms—including persistent tinnitus and excruciating ear pain—I struggled to secure a timely appointment. On multiple occasions, I was told no slots were available and advised to call 111, only to later receive conflicting information about GP availability. This poor communication delayed my treatment unnecessarily. After resorting to out-of-hours services, I was finally seen within minutes and diagnosed with a middle ear infection, reinforcing concerns about mismanaged scheduling. Some of the GPs at this practice do not seem to take patient concerns seriously, making it difficult to receive necessary referrals. One GP refused to refer me to ENT despite my ongoing symptoms—only for an out-of-hours GP to confirm that an ENT consultation was required to rule out vascular issues. Additionally, my interaction with a staff member, Katie, was unprofessional—she was abrupt, dismissive, and hung up on me without cause. The lack of clarity regarding referrals, particularly with ENT, further highlights ongoing issues with patient care. While I did encounter a helpful receptionist, the overall decline in professionalism and responsiveness at this practice is alarming. I am also concerned that my previous Google review may have been hidden, which raises further questions about transparency and accountability. Patients deserve better communication, respect, and timely medical attention.

recent_reviews.author: Paul
recent_reviews.text: I feel the need to write this review due to the many unnecessary unfair reviews. I am writing this review to provide feedback on the experiences of my wife, who is a patient at Dr. Subramanian's practice. My wife has been a patient of Dr. Subramanian for many many years, and we wish to convey that she finds him to be an excellent and highly valued doctor. She is more than extremely satisfied with the care she receives and would not consider changing practices. Regarding her access to appointments, my wife has always been able to get an appointment when needed and has never encountered any difficulty in being seen. This is in stark contrast to my own doctors at the same health centre, where it can be impossible to get an appointment unless you book three weeks in advance. Despite the option to call at 8 am for a same-day appointment, I have found it nearly impossible to get through to the practice, which often just gives an out-of-service tone. This brings me to a common complaint I hear from people about potential delays to appointment times. I have observed that Dr. Subramanian often makes a significant effort to accommodate patients who present with urgent issues on the day. Furthermore, I have noticed that delays can also occur when patients require a double appointment but only book a standard one, or they present with multiple issues they need addressing. From what I can see, the doctor is very thorough and compassionate in addressing all of their concerns, which can sometimes extend beyond the scheduled time. While this might occasionally lead to waiting longer for a pre-booked appointment, I believe this reflects a true commitment to ensuring those with immediate needs are seen, and that everyone gets the time they need. This responsiveness for urgent matters is something I value greatly, as it is not always my understanding of how easy it is to access care at other practices. Overall, my wife and I are very happy with the care and accessibility provided by Dr. Subramanian. He is a credit to his profession.

recent_reviews.author: R Darksky
recent_reviews.text: I like doctor subramannian a lot he helps you and treats you well, but some staff are not gtheir job on the desk n locums or they do it very slowly when it's a simple thing. EDIT also got good service from Dr Nasarudin I quit smoking and was struggling to sleep, he gave me a week of max dose zopiclone which I appreciate a lot. Other than that the doctor actually treats your conditions, hurray! This is a very experienced G.P., I have had 5 others that were not even 5% as good as him. Some staff on the desk are lovely but others are lazy, they are not bad folks they just can't be bothered doing their job I guess or maybe they are depressed who knows? The Locum gave me an NSAID one time that boosts gabapentin that was silly so I chucked them away as then i'd be up on my does. I have quite a bit of knowledge on medications. I am happy with my G.P. and some of the staff like nearly most of em, the Indian lady is the best on the desk and Dr Subramannian is very good he has clearly read the NHS constitution. I like the new health centre but it can be stuffy at times the library does that I think the books take up moisture in the air an it gets dry n hot if there is a lot of you in there. I think a solution would be fans and maybe somehow having a window that can open on the panels? Anyway, It's way better now I am happy with this one, happy as larry. An actual Doctor worth waiting even for him if it's busy as you can go in very anxious and come out not depressed and anxious I guess the anticipation must release dopamine. I have never left the G.P.'s office suffering not one time unless I am the one messing it up 0-o. Peace.

recent_reviews.text: Waiting on the phone for a referral. Number one in the queue for 17 minutes and counting. Surely it doesn’t take that long to answer a call about a referral. I think the person must have gone on their coffee break. Slowly losing the will to live. 27/10/25 This is the second time I have been pinged to leave a review. I can’t enter a second review because the system won’t let me, so I’ll just add onto my first review. Ok. Today, the phone was answered promptly after being told I was first in the queue. 5:50pm. The person answering told me that I needed to ring my chemist for a repeat prescription of some medication. She didn’t ask my name so could have no idea what the circumstances were. At this point I asked if she would like to check that, which she did. At this point she said oh they aren’t on a repeat at the moment so I’ll order them for you. So, maybe check the persons record before sending them on a wild goose chase to the wrong people. . Sorry, on this occasion I can’t up my score from three stars.

He also let my abusive father into the appointment when I asked for him specifically not to be in there, I'm a 31 year old man with full mental capacity, this is a massive breach of my privacy. To anyone who is thinking about using this GP avoid it at all costs, your privacy is not safe and they do not take your mental health seriously.

recent_reviews.author: Amyn
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at Springview Medical Centre since it first opened, but sadly, the quality of care has declined since Dr. Shrikant and Dr. Gupta left the practice. The appointment system has become increasingly inefficient, and the locum doctors now seem to rely solely on brief questioning to prescribe medication rather than conducting thorough physical examinations. This is a stark contrast to the exceptional care provided by Dr. Shrikant and Dr. Gupta during their tenure. They both consistently offered outstanding medical attention and set a high standard that I wish all doctors could emulate. I would also like to mention my disappointing experience with the in-house physiotherapist. Despite seeking help multiple times for chronic lower back pain and severe pain in my index finger, he failed to conduct any physical examination. Instead, he would simply glance at me and dismissively attribute the pain to arthritis without further investigation or discussion. This lack of thoroughness was both frustrating and disheartening.

recent_reviews.author: J O'Hara
recent_reviews.text: The general practice has been on the decline over the last couple of years, however, they have a fantastic nurse there called Nicola. She is so professional, is great at her job, and always has a friendly smile. I saw Nicola yesterday and she was so helpful and took my blood without me even noticing! I have had to be sent to the hospital in the past because previous nurses have struggled. My husband had an appointment on the same day but his experience wasn't so great. Upon arriving he was told there was a 10 minute delay. This was fine by him and at least he was warned. After nearly an hours wait, he still hadn't been seen so asked the receptionist what was happening. She apologised and said he was next. He then heard that doctor was on his break. He angrily (and rightly so), told them he wasn't prepared to wait any longer. He lost an hour and a half of his working day and never actually got to see a doctor! I think that is shocking and now he is still in pain but will not visit the surgery again. I have to change doctors for him and that means another few weeks until he gets seen. I am just hoping his issue isn't serious...

recent_reviews.text: Used to be quite a good Dr's, but that time is long past. Can't get an appointment for love nor money. Spend ages on hold when you phone up as advised at 8am but then nothing left when you get through. Been quite ill after travelling abroad, no appointments, so sent to the pharmacy. After speaking to them the Pharmacist escorted me to the surgery and made them give me an appointment that day! had tests which have a 48hr turnaround according to the GP, took a week then told I can have a phone consultation in several weeks time! That's useless to he blunt. Also been refused a simple treatment for nosebleeds as they weren't severe enough. Apparently blood needs to be pouring out of you for 20 minutes on a regular basis before you can have a simple 2 second treatment. What's most annoying though is they've got time to respond with empty platitudes to negative reviews on here.... but can't pick up the phone when you call. Do yourself a favour and go somewhere else.

recent_reviews.text: Visited this morning with my daughter who has a severe infection behind her ear. I was informed by the receptionist that there was only one emergency slot left and it was blocked off so she was unable to book my daughter in. This was despite not asking what my daughter’s symptoms were. She advised me to go through 111 which I did. They told me to contact my GP immediately and arrange an emergency appointment. When I rang I was informed by the receptionist that the emergency slot had been booked and now to go through the after hours service. I would like to know how these emergency appointments are allocated as my daughter now has to wait for almost 6 hours to see someone after 111 have decreed it serious enough to warrant an emergency appointment!

recent_reviews.author: Cedar Hodsman
recent_reviews.text: Absolute shambles of a surgery. Dr Butt has prescribed me the wrong medicine 4 times, even after having a phone consultation where we agreed on a course of action, she still wrote the wrong prescription! I've been waiting over a month to get a simple prescription done correctly. Just baffled at this level of incompetency. Also seems to be extremely difficult to get an appointment at this clinic lately. Not sure if this is because of the recent change in management? You have to call up at exactly 8 am to be put on the list and have the doctor ring you back at some unspecified time, so you have to sit by the phone all day just waiting for the call. Some doctors only work 2 days a week, so you might be waiting a while to speak to them. In terms of the pharmacy, I had a similar experience as another lady's review - my prescription was rejected (because the doctor hadn't bothered to read my medical record and see that I'd already had the blood test results to require the medication), but I wasn't made aware of this. It's only when I called up wondering when my prescription would be ready that I discovered it had been rejected. Just shocking service alround. If you can join a different surgery, you'll probably save yourself a good few headaches by avoiding Spring View.

recent_reviews.text: Took my mum who is 95 years old and suffering from Alzheimer’s to the surgery today. She has been suffering a persistent cough and also needed a dementia review. Can I also thank the ladies in the office who have been so helpful in fitting mum in as soon as possible and helping organise the help she needs

recent_reviews.author: Faiza Nasar
recent_reviews.text: If I could give 0 stars I would. THE WORST SURGERY I HAVE EVER BEEN TO. JOTSNA the receptionist is so rude, she thought it was appropriate to argue and laugh while I explain my fathers symptoms, who by the way is a vulnerable patient. She then proceeded to lie about it when she didn't realise she was on a recorded line. She just seemed like a very angry person who doesn't enjoy her job, and to be honest if I had a face and personality like hers I would be angry at the world too. The GP's are no better, they also fabricate things against their patients to cover their own backs, my father was given medication he did not need. This doctor then fabricated a story to DR GUPTA who is also an awful and unprofessional person and when I said to Dr Gupta her doctor is lying she got very angry and threatened me with a warning letter, all because I spoke up against this false accusation. Seems to me they bully their patients and families quite often. The fact she thought I would keep my father at that surgery is ludicrous, I question how any of them became doctors anyway. I had also proceeded to tell the doctor that I believe my father is dehydrated as he has not been able to keep anything down and she brushed it off, only for me to later receive a call to say his results indicate dehydration and he must be taken to the hospital urgently for fluids via IV administration. The surgery itself is a risk to health, with damp and mould and also there is NO CEILING in the waiting area. These combined pose a huge risk to ones health and safety. The place is a complete shambles, its below adequate and I'm surprised its not been shut down. I will be taking all my complaints further, to GMC, The Health Authority Ombudsmen and to PALS. I think its about time the staff at this surgery stop bullying and patronising their patients and their families and fulfil their duty of care.

recent_reviews.author: N Bolton
recent_reviews.text: Whilst the service has improved since Dr Caswell’s departure this practice is inconsistent when delivering good patient care. I have been at this surgery for over 5 years. It is not unusual to wait 2 weeks for an appointment unless you push for a same day appointment. However if you have work or family commitments as most people do it isn’t always possible to drop everything at such short notice. Seldom seen at appointment time, sometimes nearly an hour later. Incredibly inconvenient when I’ve just ‘nipped out’ of work and return 2 hours later. You can ring at 8am or 3pm for a same day appointment but they aren’t guaranteed. You can be on hold for up to 10 minutes before you receive an infuriating message telling you the practice is now closed when it is not. I no longer telephone but go in in person as I can’t be ignored then. Some receptionists are pleasant, some are rude, sometimes the pleasant ones are rude! I have used BARDOC myself without prompting from the practice as I can not rely on an out-of-hours service. I have been told twice recently there are no appointments during an acute episode requiring an emergency prescription. The male doctor seems more open to further testing and investigations when presenting with what could be symptoms of a potentially serious or underlying condition ; The female doctor not so much. Money appears to play a part in decisions, such as what medication is prescribed or potential tests to be carried out. I don’t need to know the cost of a blood test just if I need one thanks. On one occasion I had to ask the nurse to close the curtains upstairs in a room that faces residential properties , whilst removing my clothing and underwear. I shouldn’t have to ask. The building is currently being refurbished but would be irrelevant to me if I was receiving good quality care. I have also often partly heard consultations through the walls/doors when stood by reception or in the waiting room. They should invest in sound proofing as consultations should be private and confidential. My biggest concern is inconsistent care, as sometimes I feel satisfied and others times I feel fobbed off or just a patient number. The service is not personal and doctors don’t seem to familiarise themselves with your notes. I work in the NHS and patient numbers here are low compared to other surgeries across Bolton, where I have experienced knowledgeable and proactive doctors who appear to know the patient even if it’s just because they have skimmed the medical notes. Would not recommend this surgery if you have high expectations or previous experience at a good surgery as you will be disappointed. Never mind the building Beehive Surgery, invest in some customer service training and learn the value of your patients.
