recent_reviews.author: Ellis Birtles
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at this practice for over 10 years and unfortunately the quality of care has declined significantly. I have been suffering with rectal bleeding and recurrent abscesses for several years, and despite repeatedly asking for further investigation, I have consistently been dismissed. Last week I attended the surgery with heavy rectal bleeding. The doctor would not make eye contact, did not offer a chaperone before asking me to lie on the bed with my underwear down, and carried out no proper examination such as pressing on my abdomen. When I tried to explain my symptoms, I was told to leave the room for being “rude”, even though I was in distress. No help was given, and I was simply told to book another appointment six days later. Because of this, I contacted 111 who sent me to the hospital within an hour due to the seriousness of my symptoms. This is not the first time I’ve had to go through 111 or A&E because the practice would not help. Over the years, my abscesses have repeatedly been dismissed as “boils” and I have only been given mild antibiotics. I have now finally seen a dermatologist who believes my symptoms may be linked to inflammatory bowel disease, something I have been worried about for years but the practice refused to investigate. The reception staff often come across rushed and unfriendly, and I leave most interactions feeling patronised and unheard. Even when I raised my concerns with the practice manager, I felt dismissed again. All I want is to be listened to and to receive proper care. After years of pain, worry, and being ignored, I can no longer trust this practice with my health.

recent_reviews.text: One star is extremely generous. A terribly run practice, where profits seem to come before patients. recent_reviews.text: 0 stars. I have been experiencing what I believe to be an infection for over 4 months now. I have had a cyst for over 3 months. I’ve been back and forth to the doctors multiple times now. And I’ve been prescribed Flucloxacillin 3 times over the past 3 months. And my symptoms and cyst are still present. I went to go get my THIRD lot of Flucloxacillin but not to my surprise my prescription wasn’t there. This has happened multiple times now where I’ve been told my prescription will be sent to the pharmacy THAT DAY, but it is NEVER there! And it is weekend now so I will have to wait another 2 days to ring the doctors to chase up a prescription that was meant to have been sent yesterday. I’m so exhausted from my illness and going back and forth to a useless GP. The doctor I went to see about this third prescription was passive aggressive, saying “well we only have 10 minutes”, hinting that she was annoyed at me for being there past 6pm, even tho I was TOLD to come in that time. The doctors here do not listen to you, they do not care about you and they will shut you down when you try to explain how ill you’ve been. Even the lady at the pharmacy was shocked to know that I had been prescribed Flucloxacillin for the third time now.

recent_reviews.author: Alicja Basharyar
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely shocking awful GP. I am diagnosed PCOS patient that just needed a referral for a fertility treatment. After moving to Bolton I registered with this GP hoping for the best knowing I would need a referral as a patient that deals with PCOS for years. I came in January to ask for the referral. I was told that it would be send right away. I expected to wait , because everyone knows the state NHS currently is. But after few months of not hearing anything in regards to fertility treatment I started to push more and more to learn what is going on with my referral only to find out that the referral was not sent at all! I found out about in July after 7 months of waiting for the treatment! Finally,my referral was sent out by the end of July. I still didn’t hear anything about appointment for my treatment so I called Royal Bolton that advised me to ask GP for a letter to speed up my referral. So I made telephone consultation with Dr Khan(the same thy told me he would refer me right away back in January)to ask for it. He said he would issue the letter. This consultation took place last Monday. So I came with my husband last Friday to ask what is going on with the letter. I was told it would be done today and I would be able to see it in the app. I kept checking and still nothing! Absolutely shocking! Not to mention in the meantime of all of it back in April I was bleeding and in pain and I was told by Dr Khan that it’s fine and I should wait for fertility appointment as it would be addressed then! I was bleeding for few weeks and in pain! Shocking ! I absolutely do NOT recommend this practice that does NOT meet any standards! I will be leaving them together with my husband.👎👎👎👎

recent_reviews.author: Ludmila Tomasev
recent_reviews.text: Review of GP Surgery – Dr. Kumari I am extremely disappointed with the level of care my family received from Dr. Kumari. My mother had an appointment due to severe stomach pain that had lasted for three days. She could barely walk, felt nauseous, and had intense cramping radiating to her back. During the appointment, Dr. Kumari only pressed on her stomach (which caused my mum to scream in pain) and then prescribed omeprazole — without carrying out any basic tests such as blood or urine checks. Shockingly, my mother was told she would have to wait six weeks for a scan. Later that same day, her condition worsened, and she had to be taken to hospital. She was diagnosed with acute cholecystitis, treated with IV antibiotics, and is now awaiting laparoscopic cholecystectomy. A simple urine test at the GP surgery would have shown signs of infection and helped avoid a potentially dangerous delay in treatment. The lack of proper examination and follow-up was incredibly irresponsible. In a separate case, the same doctor prescribed cream for my young nephew’s face, assuming he had psoriasis or dry skin. However, the issue turned out to be skin tags around his eyes, which clearly needed a different type of assessment and care. These experiences have left me deeply concerned about the quality of care and the lack of thoroughness shown during appointments. A more careful and investigative approach should be expected from any GP, especially when patients present with such serious symptoms.

recent_reviews.author: Mira Bella
recent_reviews.text: I've been registered with this practice for years, and thankfully, I haven't needed to use their services often. But on the few occasions I have, it's been incredibly frustrating—like trying to apply for a travel visa. Most recently, I was calling on behalf of my mum, who was experiencing bad chest pain and a severe cough. I started calling from 8am and didn’t get through until after 9:30am, only to be told all appointments were gone for the day. They booked her a telephone appointment with a pharmacist, who then prescribed a nasal spray. We ended up going to hospital, where she was diagnosed with a chest infection.On other occasions, they haven’t even answered the phone. I went in person and saw the staff behind the desk chatting casually while the phone rang unanswered.This is honestly the worst GP surgery I’ve dealt with. Unhelpful, dismissive, and inefficient. I'm now in the process of registering elsewhere and I strongly advise others to do the same.

recent_reviews.author: Maria Ebteda
recent_reviews.text: During my appointment, I faced some issues regarding hygiene and patient care. Despite requesting a tissue for the bed, this was denied, and I was informed that the beds were cleaned after each patient. While this assurance was provided, it didn’t address my comfort or concerns at the moment. Additionally, during a vaginal sonography, I asked for the equipment to be cleaned in my presence. This request was refused, and I observed the handles being placed on a desk without any sterilizing measures visible. This experience left me feeling uneasy about the infection control practices. I believe there’s room for improvement to ensure patients feel reassured and cared for during such procedures. Suggestions: • Consider allowing patients to witness equipment cleaning for reassurance. • Provide tissues or disposable covers on beds to enhance comfort and hygiene.

recent_reviews.author: Itsme Ayen
recent_reviews.text: I went there this morning. But as usual they said they’re fully booked (I have been calling since two weeks ago when my illness actually started developing, at least 150 times every morning but never got any appointments) So I asked them to refer me to the pharmacy nearby. And the pharmacy referred me back to them as my temperature was high and I had chronic infection in my throat which clearly needed their attention. So I went to the GP straight from the pharmacy at 10.30 and my GP appointment was set at 11.30. I don’t have any voice now since Friday, and I was so tired of walking here and there just to see the doctor. At 11.20 I went to the reception only to be told to wait until they called my name. I couldn’t even speak because my voice is not coming out but I did come to the counter to ask for my appointment. It’s just to be sure because and I was feeling so fatigued and nauseous. Then I sat again at the waiting area until there’s no one left at 12. I quickly asked the receptionist when will I be attended? she checked the system and she said that I never showed up at 11.30 so the doctor has cancelled my appointment. She even told everyone there that I was late. The nerve she had to say that straight to my sick face was beyond me. She even asked me to go home. It was purely rude. I asked her to check the cctv and she said when I came at 10.30 I didn’t get to the counter for registration. It was true because I was way too early for my 11.30 appointment. So they kept blaming me and said I was late to everyone that’s there. I was so ashamed. I was shaking and crying myself out and asked them to check the cctv at 11.20 because I was positive that I did go to the receptionist to confirm my appointment but she only asked me to wait. But of course they won’t because they knew I was telling the truth. They kept arguing with me until I couldn’t take it anymore and I finally lost myself and my nose started bleeding so bad on the floor. This system is crazy. I really couldn’t understand how the Great Britain falls to this low level. I paid thousand pounds to NHS annually with my visa but not even once I get to use your services. And this time I am really ill I had no choice but to see the doctor physically. And this is how you treat your patients. You should be ashamed to be called a doctor when you refused to see your patients!

recent_reviews.text: I don't even know to what practice to move. I don't know who made receptionists doctors over night but they should stop. Last year at the beginning after I registered even though I had to call a thousand times to reach them I was at least getting an appointment. Now I call them with similar problem, as it is recurring to me every few months, and I am being told that it's not bad enough for me to see the GP and that I should just go to the pharmacy. Since when are receptionists doctors and assessors of how bad the situation is? And how bad does it have to be for me to receive an appointment? Bad enough for emergency so then they can send me that way instead? I've lived in 2 different cities since I am in UK and had GPs there and I never had such a horrible experience as here. And funny enough, now that I look at the reviews and questions I don't see even one good opinion about them. And with other GPs practices at least I saw that people where getting at least feedback from the practice management to their reviews.

recent_reviews.text: Honestly, the only reason I’m giving this 5 star is because of a lady that works there called Sue. She is someone who should truly be in healthcare. These days a lot of people treat it like a 9 to 5 and do not understand that they are in a place of comfort, help and a listening ear to people who may be worried about their health or have one issue or another. But Sue listened, empathised and went above and beyond to get me an appointment for the same week when another colleague told me I would have to wait a whole month! So this is for Sue, and other great health care workers at the GP Practise. Thank you for being such a help 😊 x

recent_reviews.author: J S
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient of this surgery for 30 years and have always had exceptional service until the past few years. Since Dr Newgrosh has retired there is a significant lack of care, communication and professionalism. I don’t believe for a moment that this is the fault of the hardworking individuals of the surgery; the receptionists, cleaners and nurses are overworked and under appreciated throughout the borough. The chemists also provide an excellent service. I also don’t blame certain GPs, who take their duty of care seriously. I do, however, believe that there is a serious problem and someone needs to take responsibility for that. As someone with a full-time job, I have to arrange when I will be ill in advance. There is no walk in option and when it is possible to get an appointment (bearing in mind I have to provide evidence of this at work), they are swift and sharp. Almost as if I am inconveniencing the doctor with my paltry ailments. Now, I am not one of those that has a season ticket to the waiting room (I only go when absolutely necessary), however, when I go to the doctors I expect to be gone appropriate time and attention. This is simply not provided here. Dr Newgrosh was a credit to his profession, I only wish his predecessors had the same commitment to their role.

Thank you, everyone, for your amazing dedication and support. It really does make a difference 🤩

recent_reviews.author: Aziz Ibraheem
recent_reviews.text: Its quite clear that they're trying their best to improve what they do and that's welcomed. However, I cant understand why we are de registered so quickly from this surgery. Online NHS says 5 years of no contact. I think this surgery follows a 1 year rule. Even that it should be necessary to send enough letters, emails, messages or calls before de registering someone. My child needed an appointment and they refused to discuss anything as they'd decided to register both my children and my wife. Seems like its a problem when yoh get too many appointments and also a problem when you stay healthy and away. Then theres a paper form that needs to be filled in, then something online. All of that whilst bringing all your children in as they wont do ID check without them being present.

recent_reviews.author: Ludmila Tomasev
recent_reviews.text: Review of GP Surgery – Dr. Kumari I am extremely disappointed with the level of care my family received from Dr. Kumari. My mother had an appointment due to severe stomach pain that had lasted for three days. She could barely walk, felt nauseous, and had intense cramping radiating to her back. During the appointment, Dr. Kumari only pressed on her stomach (which caused my mum to scream in pain) and then prescribed omeprazole — without carrying out any basic tests such as blood or urine checks. Shockingly, my mother was told she would have to wait six weeks for a scan. Later that same day, her condition worsened, and she had to be taken to hospital. She was diagnosed with acute cholecystitis, treated with IV antibiotics, and is now awaiting laparoscopic cholecystectomy. A simple urine test at the GP surgery would have shown signs of infection and helped avoid a potentially dangerous delay in treatment. The lack of proper examination and follow-up was incredibly irresponsible. In a separate case, the same doctor prescribed cream for my young nephew’s face, assuming he had psoriasis or dry skin. However, the issue turned out to be skin tags around his eyes, which clearly needed a different type of assessment and care. These experiences have left me deeply concerned about the quality of care and the lack of thoroughness shown during appointments. A more careful and investigative approach should be expected from any GP, especially when patients present with such serious symptoms.

recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Ludmila Tomasev2 reviewsEdited 7 months ago Review of GP Surgery – Dr. Kumari I am extremely disappointed with the level of care my family received from Dr. Kumari. My mother had an appointment due to severe stomach pain that had lasted for three days. She could barely walk, felt nauseous, and had intense cramping radiating to her back. During the appointment, Dr. Kumari only pressed on her stomach (which caused my mum to scream in pain) and then prescribed omeprazole — without carrying out any basic tests such as blood or urine checks. Shockingly, my mother was told she would have to wait six weeks for a scan. Later that same day, her condition worsened, and she had to be taken to hospital. She was diagnosed with acute cholecystitis, treated with IV antibiotics, and is now awaiting laparoscopic cholecystectomy. A simple urine test at the GP surgery would have shown signs of infection and helped avoid a potentially dangerous delay in treatment. The lack of proper examination and follow-up was incredibly irresponsible. In a separate case, the same doctor prescribed cream for my young nephew’s face, assuming he had psoriasis or dry skin. However, the issue turned out to be skin tags around his eyes, which clearly needed a different type of assessment and care. These experiences have left me deeply concerned about the quality of care and the lack of thoroughness shown during appointments. A more careful and investigative approach should be expected from any GP, especially when patients present with such serious symptoms.Like Share Response from the owner 6 months agoDear Ludmila, We apologise that the experience you have had with the practice has not been a positive one. recent_reviews.text: I've been registered with this practice for years, and thankfully, I haven't needed to use their services often. But on the few occasions I have, it's been incredibly frustrating—like trying to apply for a travel visa. Most recently, I was calling on behalf of my mum, who was experiencing bad chest pain and a severe cough. I started calling from 8am and didn’t get through until after 9:30am, only to be told all appointments were gone for the day. They booked her a telephone appointment with a pharmacist, who then prescribed a nasal spray. We ended up going to hospital, where she was diagnosed with a chest infection.On other occasions, they haven’t even answered the phone. I went in person and saw the staff behind the desk chatting casually while the phone rang unanswered.This is honestly the worst GP surgery I’ve dealt with. Unhelpful, dismissive, and inefficient. I'm now in the process of registering elsewhere and I strongly advise others to do the same.

recent_reviews.author: Maria Ebteda
recent_reviews.text: During my appointment, I faced some issues regarding hygiene and patient care. Despite requesting a tissue for the bed, this was denied, and I was informed that the beds were cleaned after each patient. While this assurance was provided, it didn’t address my comfort or concerns at the moment. Additionally, during a vaginal sonography, I asked for the equipment to be cleaned in my presence. This request was refused, and I observed the handles being placed on a desk without any sterilizing measures visible. This experience left me feeling uneasy about the infection control practices. I believe there’s room for improvement to ensure patients feel reassured and cared for during such procedures. Suggestions: • Consider allowing patients to witness equipment cleaning for reassurance. • Provide tissues or disposable covers on beds to enhance comfort and hygiene.

recent_reviews.author: Itsme Ayen
recent_reviews.text: I went there this morning. But as usual they said they’re fully booked (I have been calling since two weeks ago when my illness actually started developing, at least 150 times every morning but never got any appointments) So I asked them to refer me to the pharmacy nearby. And the pharmacy referred me back to them as my temperature was high and I had chronic infection in my throat which clearly needed their attention. So I went to the GP straight from the pharmacy at 10.30 and my GP appointment was set at 11.30. I don’t have any voice now since Friday, and I was so tired of walking here and there just to see the doctor. At 11.20 I went to the reception only to be told to wait until they called my name. I couldn’t even speak because my voice is not coming out but I did come to the counter to ask for my appointment. It’s just to be sure because and I was feeling so fatigued and nauseous. Then I sat again at the waiting area until there’s no one left at 12. I quickly asked the receptionist when will I be attended? she checked the system and she said that I never showed up at 11.30 so the doctor has cancelled my appointment. She even told everyone there that I was late. The nerve she had to say that straight to my sick face was beyond me. She even asked me to go home. It was purely rude. I asked her to check the cctv and she said when I came at 10.30 I didn’t get to the counter for registration. It was true because I was way too early for my 11.30 appointment. So they kept blaming me and said I was late to everyone that’s there. I was so ashamed. I was shaking and crying myself out and asked them to check the cctv at 11.20 because I was positive that I did go to the receptionist to confirm my appointment but she only asked me to wait. But of course they won’t because they knew I was telling the truth. They kept arguing with me until I couldn’t take it anymore and I finally lost myself and my nose started bleeding so bad on the floor. This system is crazy. I really couldn’t understand how the Great Britain falls to this low level. I paid thousand pounds to NHS annually with my visa but not even once I get to use your services. And this time I am really ill I had no choice but to see the doctor physically. And this is how you treat your patients. You should be ashamed to be called a doctor when you refused to see your patients!

recent_reviews.text: I don't even know to what practice to move. I don't know who made receptionists doctors over night but they should stop. Now I call them with similar problem, as it is recurring to me every few months, and I am being told that it's not bad enough for me to see the GP and that I should just go to the pharmacy. Since when are receptionists doctors and assessors of how bad the situation is? And how bad does it have to be for me to receive an appointment? Bad enough for emergency so then they can send me that way instead? I've lived in 2 different cities since I am in UK and had GPs there and I never had such a horrible experience as here. And funny enough, now that I look at the reviews and questions I don't see even one good opinion about them. And with other GPs practices at least I saw that people where getting at least feedback from the practice management to their reviews.

recent_reviews.text: Honestly, I would give 0 stars if I could! I had the worst experience as a whole.. ABSOLUTELY UN CALLED FOR! I’ve waited long enough with my baby, who was by that time getting wingey! Also DATA PROTECTION, as I heard the whole conversation. I know exactly what he spoke to them about. He Spoke to the patient, and his wife and I knew exactly when he booked the appointment for and why. This was my last time visiting this surgery!

recent_reviews.author: Anmole Shah
recent_reviews.text: I never take out the time to write negative reviews but this place really needed one with their extremely poor service from the receptionists. I called the reception at 8am at 39 weeks pregnant with cold and flu symptoms and was told by one of the ladies (who had a extremely unprofessional tone) that the GP can’t do anything and I should call my midwife. Common sense says that midwife’s don’t give prescriptions out for colds and flus. I told the receptionist this and she totally dismissed me and said there’s nothing they can do after I was on hold for 15mins. I then proceeded to Call maternity triage who said they don’t understand why I had called them as the GP normally deals with cold and flu symptoms, pregnant or not (surprise surprise). She told me to call the Gp back. So I called the GP surgery back and a different lady answered the phone this time and said ‘We wouldn’t have told you to call the midwife as we know they don’t give out prescriptions’. I told her someone at the reception DID tell me to call the midwife and turned me away and I ended up wasting an hour calling everyone back and fourth. I told her the call should be looked into and she didn’t even apologise, completely dismissive and told me that she will book me in for a telephone consultation. recent_reviews.author: Steve Cahill
recent_reviews.text: Reception staff are unhelpful in the last few years they have become less and less helpful, all the while hiding behind the zero tolerance to anger posture, when they are the very people that cause the anger and frustration, I see no point in them answering the phone because when they do, they do nothing but point to idiotic rules they have created in an effort to "help", help who?
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Steve Cahill3 reviews6 months ago Reception staff are unhelpful in the last few years they have become less and less helpful, all the while hiding behind the zero tolerance to anger posture, when they are the very people that cause the anger and frustration, I see no point in them answering the phone because when they do, they do nothing but point to idiotic rules they have created in an effort to "help", help who?Like Share Response from the owner 6 months agoDear Steve. Our reception team try to help our patients and guide them through our systems set by the NHS and the practice to ensure all our patients receive safe care. They do not create the rules. Often anger is aimed at them, and that is why we protect our staff with our zero tolerance anger policy. A zero tolerance policy towards violent, threatening and abusive behaviour is now in place throughout the National Health Service. The staff in this practice have the right to work in an environment free from violent, threatening or abusive behaviour and everything will be done to protect that right. At no time will any violent, threatening or abusive behaviour be tolerated towards staff, patients or other visitors to the practice. This relates to any form of abuse from patients or staff which includes (but is not limited to) sexism, racism homophobia, biphobia, transphobia and ageism, or harassment or abuse on basis of disability, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, religion or belief. Our Practice staff aim to be polite, helpful, and sensitive to all patients’ individual needs and circumstances. They would respectfully remind patients that very often staff could be confronted with a multitude of varying and sometimes difficult tasks and situations, all at the same time. The staff understand that ill patients do not always act in a reasonable manner and will take this into consideration when trying to deal with a misunderstanding or complaint. If you are still experiencing an issue please contact Diane, our Governance and Patient Experience Manager at the practice who will provide assistance. Many thanks

recent_reviews.author: Greg Roberts
recent_reviews.text: This place is a disgrace from top to bottom. Booking appointments to seeing an actual doctor is an imposibility, I had to wait 50 mins to see a ACP????, only to be asked well what treatment do you want🤣. This place clearly needs a CQC investigation into its practice and into the competence of the practice manager, who for as far as I can see has the intelligence of a glass if water.
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Greg Roberts1 reviewa year ago This place is a disgrace from top to bottom. Booking appointments to seeing an actual doctor is an imposibility, I had to wait 50 mins to see a ACP????, only to be asked well what treatment do you want🤣. This place clearly needs a CQC investigation into its practice and into the competence of the practice manager, who for as far as I can see has the intelligence of a glass if water.Like2 Share Response from the owner a year agoDear Greg, Firstly, I am sorry to learn that you are unhappy with the care that you have received from the practice and the distress the situation has caused you. I am grateful that you have brought this to our attention. As I understand it you are complaining because of a recent consultation with our ACP. The practice takes all complaints seriously and your complaint has been investigated in line with our complaints procedure. This involved me speaking to our ACP, who provided me with an account of their recollections of what happened, as well as reviewing your medical records. From your records I can see you completed a triage form request for an appointment on Thursday 17th October at 3.28pm stating you had a chest infection for one week. This form was triaged by the duty doctor, Dr Yelland, who actioned this request and he felt it was appropriate for you to see our Advanced Care Practitioner with an urgent appointment for your symptoms. Our ACP’s are fully qualified clinicians and are more than capable of treating a chest infection without the need to see a doctor. At 3.39pm on the 17th a member of our reception team booked you an appointment for later that day, 17th October at 5pm. You arrived before your appointment time at 4.43pm, and was seen at 5.35pm. This was a 35 minute delay. The ACP apologises for this delay and explains this was due to her seeing a child earlier in her clinic who’s appointment over ran, and the subsequent appointments were running behind. Unfortunately it is hard for us to predict medical emergencies and the length of time they will take, however, we do build blocks into the clinics to allow clinicians time to catch up and prevent delays to patients. On this occasion the ACP was still running behind. Reviewing her consultation she did full diagnostics for a chest infection, she enquired if you had tried anything prior to the appointment and you advised over the counter treatments. She asked if you had tried things in the past that had worked for you and you advised antibiotics and inhalers. She documented a treatment plan and a safety net then prescribed antibiotics. This is in response to her findings and your responses. With regards to your opinion of myself, I’m not aware that we have ever met, but I am happy to arrange a meeting to discuss your issues further with regards to the practice. We welcome all feedback and encourage our patients to feedback and suggest improvements. We also encourage you to join our Patient Participation Group that meets regularly. This group often discusses challenges that patients face and help work with the practice staff to resolve and improve our services. If this is something you would be interested in please contact our reception and ask for the Office Managers who run the PPG. I am sorry for the distress that this situation has caused you. We are appreciative of you bringing this to our attention and providing us with an opportunity to learn and make any necessary changes going forward. I hope that we have been able to fully address your concerns and questions. Please do not hesitate to contact me at the surgery if you feel that you need to discuss this further. If you’re not happy with our final response to your complaint and would like to take the matter further, you can contact the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman. The Ombudsman makes final decisions on complaints that have not been resolved by the NHS, government departments and some other public organisations. The service is free for everyone. To take a complaint to the Ombudsman, go to www.ombudsman.org.uk/making-complaint or call 0345 015 4033. It is important that you make the complaint as soon as you receive our final response as there are time limits for the Ombudsman to look into complaints’.

recent_reviews.text: For the third time this year I've been disappointed with the service I've been given by this practise. First of all asking for injections to travel after many earlier attempts when I didn't have time to wait on the phone to make an appointment I was told my injections needed to be called for 2 months in advance (I was six weeks in advance of travel) when fellow travelling companions at a practise in another area of Bolton had no problems two weeks in advance to get their injections and I was informed by one of the travellers who works for the GMC that these vaccines are always in-house at the GP practise ??? Second problem having read on social media that Kearsley medical center where taking part in the lung cancer check that was taking part at a mobile unit on Tesco's carpark I called to ask if I as an ex smoker could get an appointment only to be told that Kearsley medical centre was not involved and to call Farnworth Health center who where far from impressed by my call and didnt understand why I'd recieved this information from Kearsley. I then with some searching and checking managed to arrange this appointment for myself. This morning whilst not expecting to receive the medication I've been given for years to help with panic attacks and anxiety ( I appreciate I'm older and medical procedures have changed!) I was told there was no other help for me unless I went private or perhaps contacted a travel clinic for support. So much for empathy and understanding checking if a possible other medication could be considered. I have been at this practise since I was born other than the years working abroad and over this time had treatment from some fine GP 's who went out of their way to help and understand their patients Dr Wall springs to mind, those days are sadly gone and perhaps it's time for me to check out what else is available in this area. Whilst understanding the pressures within the NHS surely the bottom line is understanding and the care of your patient.

Not the best practiceLike Share Response from the owner a year agoDear Marius, we are sorry to learn that you are unhappy with the care that you have received from the practice and the distress the situation has caused you. I am grateful that you have brought this to our attention. As i understand it you feel the wait for an appointment is very long. The practice takes all complaints seriously and your complaint has been investigated in line with our complaints procedure. From your medical records i cannot see that you have requested an appointment recently. The last time you attended surgery was the 9th May and you booked this on the 11th April. As you wanted a late evening appointment there was a longer wait than usual for this type of slot. On 15th April we introduced a total triage system where patients can request an appointment by completing an online form. A GP then triages this form and determines the most appropriate clinician and urgency for the appointment. Since introducing this service most patients have received an appointment within 0-3 days if urgent, and up to 10 working days if deemed routine. Patient choice can effect this, but overall we feel this change has massively changed our appointment system for the better for our patients. we hope that we have been able to fully address your concerns and questions. Please do not hesitate to contact me at the surgery if you feel that you need to discuss this further. Practice Manager Kearsley Medical Centre

recent_reviews.author: Alison
recent_reviews.text: Can't get a appointment at any time the new system is terrible you might as well go to A and E cause you will have the same wait time as getting a doctor's appointment
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: AlisonLocal Guide · 19 reviews · 13 photosa year ago Can't get a appointment at any time the new system is terrible you might as well go to A and E cause you will have the same wait time as getting a doctor's appointmentLike1 Share Response from the owner a year agoDear Alison, thank you for your feedback. We are sorry you had a poor experience from the surgery. Total Triage is a new approach recommended by NHS England, to improve accessibility to Primary Care services. The main objectives are to enhance the quality of care our patients receive, to ensure that they are given the most appropriate appointment or advice to meet their needs and that this is done in a timely way. All patients will complete a short form, either via our website, or by the reception team who will complete this form on the patients behalf. This is to ensure that our patients who are unable to access the internet or do not have a smart phone have the same accessibility. The form is triaged by the triage GP who will decide which member of our healthcare team is best placed to help, the most suitable time frame for the appointment and whether it is best suited to be via telephone or in person at the practice. The new system also aims to reduce the 8am rush on the telephones, as patients can bypass our reception team and access the forms themselves via our website and at their leisure. Already, the practice has seen an increase in capacity with more appointments available to patients within a shorter time frame. We have to put capacity limits into the system so that both patients and staff are safe, and once our safe limit has been reached for the day you may be told to try again the following day. If it is an emergency you will be advised to attend A&E, as this is best placed for a medical emergency that cannot wait 24hours. We hope to support patients and their families/carers to get used to the new way of contacting the practice and to become comfortable with this over time. We will, of course, provide additional support to those patients who are unable to use online resources. We continue to advise that if you cannot use the internet for any reason, please call us – we will enter your details into our website for you. This may take longer than our previous system, so please be patient. We apologise again and will take your feedback on board.

recent_reviews.author: Katie Himsworth
recent_reviews.text: Just rang to make an appointment with a doctor and was told off by the receptionist for ringing at the wrong time. She told me i had to ring first thing in the morning and then went on to rant about the 40 appointments they had already booked. Im sorry but how am i supposed to know how many people have already rang! Also the phones are answered from 8am each morning, it was 8:30 when i rang. It doesn't tell you on the automated phone system that you have to ring first thing and it also doesn't say anything about ringing at certain times on the website. What happens if people are unable to ring at 8am sharp, what happens if the line is busy at 8am? I have a newborn at home who ive been up all night with, i managed to snatch an hours sleep from 7 to 8 am so i only just got the chance to ring at 8:30. I was made to feel stupid by the receptionist, i appreciate that they are busy but they shouldnt take it out on the patients. They need to update the automated phone system and the website to reflect the preferred ringing times that way people won't be faced with a ranting receptionist like i was.

Short story - refused to prescribe me a needed medication despite my explanation of I know it's not normally done on the phone etc but I'm having trouble. 9 times I rang them today going back and forth, I managed to get a pharmacy to help me and they rang the gp for me from their end told me to go to pharmacy at 5:30 prescription would through on the system. Long story short, I was spoken to in vulgar ways by more than one member of staff who accused me and the pharmacy i went to ;of lying. recent_reviews.author: Kay Thomas
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely appalling service. Long phone winded phone menu to spend over half an hour on hold to be told there are no appointments for a week when you are in agony and literally can't move and are told back pain (from an injury not just something thar is ongoing and they are already aware of) isn't a medical urgency. They would put a request in to doctor for some stronger tablets but no guarantee I would get any and if I did, it would be two days before they were ready. I had already explained that over the counter strength codeine wasnt touching the pain, which you aren't supposed to take for more than 3 days without seeing a doctor as they can become addictive, but what can you do if you have to wait a week for an appointment because you are told it doesn't warrant an emergency one? The "highly trained receptionist who can sign post you to the right course of action" asked no questions about whether there was any numbness or tingling in the legs etc (which could indicate something more serious). When I was having a miscarriage (which is an emotional enough situation as it is) I was told to "leave it a few days and ring back" so i just took myself to the early pregnancy centre at the hospital. No wonder so many people just turn up at A and E. They are going to miss something really serious with someone soon. You're reminded more than once that calls are recorded and they have the right to put the phone down on you, luckily I'm very calm but I can see why they put this on, they probably get so many people seething and making a fuss because the shocking service makes them feel worse when they are already ill! I emailed a complaint once but didn't even get a response. We are looking for an alternative GP surgery but dread ending up walking into something worse! I've spent many years working both reception and other customer facing roles so I am well aware of how hard it is sometimes dealing with the public, but I would certainly have been sacked by now if our service was so terrible. It's so sad and feels like nobody cares.......

When I was having a miscarriage (which is an emotional enough situation as it is) I was told to "leave it a few days and ring back" so i just took myself to the early pregnancy centre at the hospital. No wonder so many people just turn up at A and E. They are going to miss something really serious with someone soon. You're reminded more than once that calls are recorded and they have the right to put the phone down on you, luckily I'm very calm but I can see why they put this on, they probably get so many people seething and making a fuss because the shocking service makes them feel worse when they are already ill! I emailed a complaint once but didn't even get a response. We are looking for an alternative GP surgery but dread ending up walking into something worse! I've spent many years working both reception and other customer facing roles so I am well aware of how hard it is sometimes dealing with the public, but I would certainly have been sacked by now if our service was so terrible. It's so sad and feels like nobody cares.......Like10 Share

recent_reviews.author: Fran Barlow
recent_reviews.text: I’ve been disappointed and truly saddened with this practice recently following how they treated my mum. I’ve been with the practice all my life and my mum has been there pretty much since Dr Silvert first opened it. She’s now in her 80s and got an impersonal letter from the practice basically telling her to go elsewhere. She was very upset and I was angry on her behalf. She’s been forced to change doctors at her time of life and she feels it’s just because she’s old. They claimed it was because she was outside the area but the surgery is only about 10mins away. I think it’s a terrible thing to do to an old lady with not even the courtesy to speak to her in person. Ive completely lost faith in the practice cause all I can think is that they might do the same to me when I’m old or cost them money. EDIT FOLLOWING RESPONSE: Thanks for your response. The only trouble I have with your reply is that she hasn’t moved, and I live literally across the road from my mum so it just doesn’t make sense.

recent_reviews.author: Jonathan
recent_reviews.text: Dear Woodbank Surgery Management Team, I just wanted to take a moment to write and express my sincere gratitude for the care and support I receive from everyone at Woodbank Surgery. At the moment, everyday life can be a real struggle for me as I am often in constant pain and regularly dealing with infections due to my low immune system. During these difficult times, Natalie has truly gone above and beyond in caring for me. I honestly don’t think I would be here today if it wasn’t for the care she has provided. I have never experienced care like it before. She understands my health conditions and always makes sure I receive the help I need when I need it most. Natalie has genuinely been a lifesaver and is probably the reason I am still here today. Please pass on my heartfelt thanks to her — she is truly amazing and a great asset to your team. I believe she will help take Woodbank Surgery very far. I would also like to thank Dr Javid, who has always been so kind and supportive and has consistently looked after me with great understanding of my care needs. In addition, the young doctor I saw this morning was fantastic, and I am very grateful that you have such wonderful doctors working at the surgery. Lastly, I want to say that Woodbank Surgery is truly a lifeline for me. I know that my health is complex and I do not have much family support, which makes the care I receive from your team even more meaningful. This morning, Natalie arranged for me to be seen straight away as I was feeling very poorly and had an infection, which meant so much to me. Your service is truly person-centred, and you should all be very proud of the care you provide. Once again, thank you ever so much for all your support and dedication. Kind regards, Jonathan

recent_reviews.author: Hannah Norris
recent_reviews.text: I was 4 minutes late to my appointment and would have been happy to rearrange if needed but no one said a thing. Waited in the waiting room for 5-10 minutes after check in. Dr then called me through and said I was very late for my appointment to which i said I was 4 minutes late at most but I apologised and said thank you for seeing me. I gathered then that I wasn’t going to get anywhere with this dr as her attitude was disgusting towards me. She asked me if I did any exercise as to which I started explaining and she just cut me off and asked if I did any set exercise. I said if she would have just let me finish I would have told her. I mentioned that my mum who is a nurse had pointed out some changes on my bloods and had said I should go back to the drs if I was still having concerns. She then asked if my mum was a dr to which I replied no a nurse. At this she rolled her eyes while looking at her computer screen. She offered me no help other than things that I have already tried and just kept repeating there’s nothing wrong with you. I wouldn’t be at the drs if I genuinely thought I was ok. At this I got up and said I wasn’t having her attitude anymore and that she was no help and left the room. When I went to reception I politely asked if I could have a note on my record stating I did not wish to see that dr again. The receptionist then stated that this is yet another dr I do not wish to see. I will point out that the other dr I did not wish to see told me to get over my depression and to just get on with it when I went for a review of my mental health/medication. So yes I do not wish to see a dr that doesn’t take my mental health seriously. Back to today I was left feeling utterly hopeless and that I cannot go to this surgery again. They have some lovely drs, nurses and receptionists at this surgery but when you are not listened to and just made to feel unheard it doesn’t fill you with confidence in the surgery itself.

recent_reviews.author: Paul Rimmer
recent_reviews.text: Simply cannot get an appointment to see a GP at this place now. Call in or phone up during the day and you'll be told (politely, in fairness to the receptionist) that there are none available so you'll have to phone them at 8am the next morning. So you call at 8am the next morning, and of course there are dozens of other people doing the same thing. Sit in the queue and you'll be told there are "more than 30" people ahead of you. Wait patiently for 20 minutes, then get cut off. Call back and be told again that there are "more than 30" people ahead of you. If you choose the option to get a call back, they'll send you an SMS with a link to a website where you can see exactly where you are in the queue. I did this the other day and I was 113th in the queue. That's not a typo: one hundred and thirteenth. So that "more than 30" you hear while you wait patiently, could mean there are 31 callers ahead of you, or it could be 112 callers. Or more. Go on the app to book an appointment and, if you're lucky, there'll be one or two available - in a month's time. I guess if you're going to fall ill and need to see a doctor, plan it a month in advance.

recent_reviews.author: Paul Dutton
recent_reviews.text: It would be comforting to feel that these reviews change anything, but here goes. Greenmount Medical Centre, on Brandlesholme Road was an excellent Practice until they amalgamated with others in the area. We were never told why that was, but experiences since suggest to me that per capita, here in Greenmount we were lucky to have a good GP:Patient ratio (with up to seven or eight front-line GPs), (nearly all of whom were truly excellent) some first-class front-line Nurses and a lovely team of Admin staff that always made you feel welcome. Waiting times for the telephone were rarely more than five minutes and you were always able to get a face to face appointment with a GP within two weeks,-sooner if you agreed to one other than your first choice. I remember there being facilities sometimes for early morning or evening/ Saturday appointments. The growth of the Practice to being part of TFH was introduced very quickly and stealthily; all of a sudden we had several times more (probably up to twenty times more) patients and far fewer front-line GPs to take care of them. Funding gave us money that was spent on privatising the administration of the practices, redefining of roles, introduction of a heinous telephone system and several iterations of computerised management, more than one legal constitution of the new “business” and total chaos for all the patients. Not surprisingly, many complained. Then many more, so that some more GPS and more qualified Nurses have left. I wrote to the Practice Manager three times over a number of months, also the Care Quality Commission and only received a reply seven months later from the Practice Manager that patronisingly complimented me on my IT skills ( they are not very good) and then claimed that the new systems in place are working and that the patients are no longer waiting so long to receive urgent treatment in the NHS. She also said that many of the problems had been down to COVID, although the decay was set in far before that. I now know that the Practice Manager has left, “for a far bigger job” elsewhere and that the real problem, as a few of us expected has been a migration of GPs away from their jobs here. Nevertheless, I believe successive governments have been complacent and blind in letting a lot of these things happen. Why do we need a Triage system to filter out less demanding cases to newly-defined roles for cheaper employees? Why do we need outside administrators to run our surgeries? Why do we allow barely-qualified staff to take on so many of the appointments GPs used to handle? The answer, I fear is “money” and yet so much of it has been spent and wasted elsewhere with expensive IT software that didn’t work (Lorenzo), hordes of HR and IT admin staff and all sorts of roles created in pursuit of Diversity and Equal Opportunities problems that seem to be far worse elsewhere than in the NHS. Our telephone staff at Greenmount number only two some days and they have to handle hundreds of incoming telephone calls and still answer the bell at the door! I for one would be glad to help for nothing if that would help, but please everyone, write to your MP to get some support for the restoration of 1:1 appointments.

recent_reviews.author: AM 90's
recent_reviews.text: Exceptional Care To the Practice Manager at The Rock Healthcare, I am writing to share my recent experience at the Moorgate Primary Care Centre. I attended an appointment for my son’s blood test on the first floor, and I wanted to express my sincere gratitude for the outstanding care we received from a nurse named Michelle. From the moment we arrived, Michelle welcomed us with a beautiful smile and a warm energy that immediately put us at ease. In the rush of the day, I had unfortunately forgotten to bring my son’s labels and had failed to apply his numbing cream an hour prior to the appointment. As a parent, this was a stressful realization, but Michelle handled the situation with the utmost professionalism and kindness. Rather than simply turning us away, she was incredibly gentle and understanding. She took the time to explain exactly how to apply the cream and kindly arranged a new time slot for us to return later that same day. When we returned, Michelle greeted us with the same wonderful smile. My son has autism, and medical environments can often be challenging for him. However, Michelle was so incredibly patient and gentle that I felt entirely at ease throughout the entire process. I told her at the time, but I want to reiterate: Michelle is one of the most wonderful professionals I have ever met. She clearly takes immense pride in her work and treats her patients with genuine heart. She turned what could have been a very difficult day into a positive experience that made me feel truly happy and supported. Please ensure this feedback is shared with Michelle and her supervisors. She is a credit to your team and a shining example of what exceptional healthcare looks like. Thank you, Michelle! Best regards, Amir Abbas

recent_reviews.author: Charlie Green
recent_reviews.text: This practise is awful, I desperately wish someone would come and give this place a revamp. Call waiting times are horrific, I called three times this morning - twice the receptionist couldn't hear me and kept saying 'Hello?' before hanging up, this was on two different mobiles so definitely an issue on their end. I was first in the queue when I rang and when I had to call back there were no appointments left. Recently I started trying a different tactic and arriving at the practise for 8am to try and get an appointment in person first thing. Multiple times I've been in there before the receptionists have, despite the practise opening at 8:00. Girls walking in and sitting down in their coats, turning their computers on at 08:10 while there's a queue of people, the phone ringing off the hook and being unanswered. Another time I got a letter saying 'Please ring us about a letter we have received.' and both times I rang the receptionist had no idea why they'd sent the message and booked a very vague appointment for me where I had to wait a week to find out what it was for. Anxiety inducing to say the least. There's just no onus on the team there. The doctors and nurses are lovely but the reception team need serious training. It's awful.

recent_reviews.author: Yawar Malik
recent_reviews.text: You will never see the same GP. You will constantly be making multiple trips to the pharmacy because they either mess up or don’t send the prescriptions at all. You decide to call them in advance of each pharmacy trip to check that the prescriptions have been sent (to mitigate the above mentioned issues) they will of course assure you all has been sent correctly. You’ll subsequently visit the pharmacy who still won’t have it. You’ll sure enough fall behind on your medications and the matter will still take 2-3 calls, 1-2 weeks and possibly another 1-2 fruitless pharmacy trips to resolve. Each call will have you on hold for at least 10-40 minutes. You’ll want to book an appointment but they can never offer one for at least 3-4 weeks. If your matter can’t wait that long the receptionist will tell you to call at 8 AM during the week in order to book one. So you call the next day and after being on hold for at least 40 minutes (a problem they create by offering no appointments) the usually apathetic admin member on the phone with presumably no medical training will make a judgement as to whether or not your issue is urgent and this will not be open to discussion as the advisor will terminate the call on you quickly to deal with the queue of 50 other calls. So even then theres a fair chance that you won’t get an appointment at all. You’ve had a blood test booked for weeks and unfortunately the only nurse on shift has come down with an illness so they cancel on the day (after you’ve waited 2 weeks for the appointment in the first place). Fair enough the nurses are human as well. Unfortunately at this practice you won’t get another appointment for weeks and it will take multiple of the above excruciating phone calls to rearrange. You’ll decide to make a complaint since you’ve had enough, surprise surprise the practice manager call back will never come. Don’t bother unless you’re a junkie for anxiety (in which case this is the practice for you)

recent_reviews.author: Lynton Susman
recent_reviews.text: Significant turnover of GP's, within a couple of years, many often seeking partnerships with other practices. Nursing staff have always been fantastic, without which, Rock Healthcare just would not function.. Receptionists, whilst polite, efficient and well meaning, are clearly overstretched. As much as 20 mins+ to get through, is questionably a "health risk" in itself, more so for those who may be so unwell, yet may, give up and so hang up. What happens to them is anyone's guess. recent_reviews.text: A decent surgery, but don't advertise online patient services if you cannot provide them! I've been a patient here since January 2018, and so far, I've had positive experiences with all the doctors and (all but one of the) nurses I have seen. Sister Nicola Rigby is absolutely brilliant, and has helped me tremendously with treatment and advice for a condition I have struggled to control for almost 15 years. However the admin system and online patient services tools are TERRIBLE and really let this otherwise decent surgery down. My partner and I both had to fill out the same new patient forms (including all our medications) and online access forms THREE TIMES before anything was processed correctly - why this happened we weren't sure. Even this wasn't 100% successful as my partner then had to book an appointment to see the the doctor to get his long-term prescription verified. The online appointment booking system is also non-functional; I have tried to book appointments several times, searching weeks and months ahead for a session with any doctor at either of the surgeries, and whatever parameters I set, the result is the same. THERE ARE NO APPOINTMENTS AVAILABLE. Yet if I call the surgery, I usually get an appointment within a week or so with no issues. I've heard from a number of patients who've also had the same problem. Rock Healthcare, PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE DO NOT ADVERTISE ONLINE PATIENT SERVICES IF YOU CANNOT PROVIDE THEM.

recent_reviews.author: Steve Hepworth
recent_reviews.text: I've been with Minden since it was quite a small practice. However, in the last few years it has gone rapidly downhill. It's gone from not being able to get a face to face appointment with a GP you know for a couple of weeks, to not being able to get an appointment with any GP for weeks. Even a telephone appointment is unlikely for over a week! This is in no way a critique on the quality of the GP's who actually work in the practice, as I couldn't properly comment on what they're like as I can very rarely get to see one! It seems that this practice is too big and has too many patients to cope. It does not therefore provide quality healthcare. In fact, it could be argued that you are sometimes effectively without healthcare at this practice.

recent_reviews.author: Johanne Harvey
recent_reviews.text: Why do they treat patients so poorly? There have been many times over the last two years when I have wanted to write a review regarding how poor this practice is, having been poorly over the last couple of years. Today has spurred me on to do this. It is such a shame that the pleasant and efficient members of staff are so overshadowed by the poor members of staff. Yesterday morning, I made an urgent call to the surgery regarding a prescription for Levothyroxine. Whilst the urgency was the fault of the chemist (for which they have apologised), the only way to remedy the mistake and get the needed medication was to ask the doctors to approve the prescription urgently. As I had no remaining tablets, I was assured by the receptionist that she would mark as urgent and get it signed yesterday. I have to say, she was polite. The chemist, this morning, advised that they had not had the confirmation from the surgery so I was forced to ring again. What is completely laughable, is that the surgery have recently changed their answering machine service detailing exactly how members of the public are to speak to the staff. No mention of the way in which the staff speak to the public! My goodness, speaking to the receptionist this morning was a thoroughly unpleasant experience. What an unpleasant lady. When I explained that I had no medication and had not taken it today and that I was advised it would be marked as urgent yesterday, I was told, and I quote, 'they don't like being pushed into signing a prescription request'. I presume that the 'they' are the doctors. When I attempted to stress that I need the medication and that if it was not approved, it would, tomorrow, be two days of not taking it, I was then told - 'Well it will be approved within 48 hours'. She was rude, dismissive and had a 'could not care less' attitude. How is this allowed to happen? When I tried to question whether it would definately be done, I was spoken over consistently. Truly unpleasant. This surgery should not employ such poor members of staff. What is remarkable is that they do not question why patients may become frustrated or annoyed? If they just took the time to train staff members and look to retrain staff members that are thoroughly unpleasant, then I am sure that not only the patients, but the staff would be much happier. Their care is atrocious and sadly, the practice is tarnished by a few 'bad apples'.

recent_reviews.text: I previously wrote a review about this practice last year and didn’t get a response when I called the surgery to discuss my concerns and issues. The service hasn’t improved since my previous review which I have had to take down as it appears I can’t write more than one review about the practice. I called the practice last November to arrange to get a sick note and spoke to an incredibly rude receptionist called Anita. She stereotyped me and asked what is the sick note normally for! It’s the first time I had called for a sick note as I had a serious accident and was unfit to work. Unsurprisingly, I didn’t get a call back when I asked to speak to somebody about the appalling service having spent almost an hour trying to get through and over 100 calls before the call was connected. The surgery now has a new pre recorded message about staff not tolerating abuse from patients. I personally wouldnt be abusive to the staff but find it interesting that it’s ok for staff to be rude to patients but they won’t put up with patients being rude to them. I can understand why patients might be rude to staff. I’m currently sat trying to get through on the phone for over an hour as I need a face to face appointment and my call has been disconnected once so have had to redial and have also logged into the nhs app to try and make an appointment with no appointments available for over 16 weeks. The reception staff should all be sacked and new staff employed who actually know the meaning of patient care and providing a good service. This practice is a joke and needs to be shut down. It’s a waste of tax payers money.

recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at Ribblesdale for over 20yrs and personally have always received good service from resident doctors, locums and reception staff. recent_reviews.author: Amanda Stanley
recent_reviews.text: I was a patient from birth until I was 19 when I left the practice for good. I honestly couldn't think of a worst doctor. My doctor was Dr thacker not sure if he's there anymore but these are just some of the issues I've encountered. Couldn't diagnose my depression and in their words "just smile more" and "what you depressed for your just a kid". Had a spot problem being a teenager gave me an alcohol liquid which actually burnt like anything and told to come back in 6 months. Went back 6 months later, I said it wasnt working and was just burning my skin. Got told it was working and to come back 6 months later. Sacked off the alcohol stuff and bought some proactive plus 2 weeks later my spots where gone. Had a telephone conversation about my toe, that turned out was a fungal infection, but without even seeing it was adamant that I had "banged my toe" I hadn't. Bought some fungal infection treatment 1 week later the toe had gotten better. Went with a back problem 12 months of its a UTI its a kidney infection went to the hospital to be diagnosed as "drinking too much water" had a white blood cell count in my urine of 745. Which aparantly the normal amount is 20. Also had given me high doses of pain killers to just mask the pain in which they claimed was due to "crushed kidneys". Turns out my back issues was due to a crooked spine and I'm now seeing a chiropractor after no doctor could actually deal with it. I've been to about 4 different doctors . I've currently had 5 sessions with my chiropractor and I can actually no walk more than 10 minutes without being in constant pain. There are many more issues, but these are the ones that stick the most, also I could rarely see my actual assigned doctor and was just sent to any random person who couldn't diagnose anything.

I will be changing doctors.

recent_reviews.author: Faiz ul Haq
recent_reviews.text: I would like to leave negative feedback regarding Dr. Hussain’s behavior at this surgery. Whenever we ask him for medicine, even for our small children, he always responds by saying: “Go and pick it up from the shelf.” Most recently, my wife, who is pregnant, needed medicine. Whenever she calls, despite the language barrier, Dr. Hussain should at least try to understand that a patient is in need of proper medical advice and prescriptions. Instead, he simply tells her to “get it from the shelf.” I want to ask: if we always have to buy medicine directly from the shelf, then what is the point of having a doctor or a surgery? What role is he fulfilling? During the last call, my wife explained that the medicine he had prescribed previously did not help her at all. She requested an alternative. Instead of listening, Dr. Hussain told her she must not be using the medicine properly. My wife clearly said she knows how to take it, but it was ineffective. At that point, Dr. Hussain disconnected the call and again told her to “buy it from the shelf.” This behavior is extremely unprofessional, dismissive, and rude—especially towards a pregnant woman and parents with small children. A doctor should listen carefully, show empathy, and provide proper medical guidance. Unfortunately, Dr. Hussain’s attitude shows the opposite. I strongly believe that this kind of conduct is unacceptable within the NHS. If doctors are not willing to provide proper medical care and instead simply tell patients to “buy from the shelf,” then they are not fulfilling their responsibility as healthcare providers. I will also be submitting a formal complaint to the NHS regarding this matter. In my opinion, Dr. Hussain should consider retirement, as he does not treat patients with the respect, care, and professionalism that is expected from a doctor.

I've never felt rushed. The nurses who run the clinics and do bloods etc are so nice, it's good to chat and laugh with them. The office staff are always polite and ready to help if they can. recent_reviews.author: Gabberdabberdoo
recent_reviews.text: I have recently had to change my GP after 30 years of being with Huntley Mount. This was due to so many things going wrong with this practice the last couple of years. The main problem is the male receptionist who usually answers the phone. It always feels like he’s not listening and several times he has told me “we’ll look into that for you” and tried to end the call without even asking for my name. I also called the surgery when I became pregnant a year ago and was told that Bury residents have their antenatal care at Oldham and given the link to register with Oldham hospital which is incorrect. This mistake ended in me having to transfer my care to North Manchester late in pregnancy and only getting my first midwife appointment at 32 weeks pregnant. I have also had nurse appointments made for me at the surgery when I needed a GP appointment, resulting in the nurse calling me to say she doesn’t deal with that and me having to call the surgery to rebook. Another problem I’ve had is that I paid for the doctor to fill in some travel insurance forms for me and waited 2 months to receive them back. I chased them up several times, once being told they were waiting for a member of staff who comes in once a week to do paperwork - then the next week being told it had been passed to Dr Butt. Several times I chased them up and they said they’d be ready in a few days and never got back to me. I even attended the surgery in person one time for an update and after looking in the computer the receptionist told me they were waiting for me to have my nurse appointment for my immunisations for travel - I asked what this was for as the forms I needed were for a holiday cancellation (to a country I would not need to have jabs for - Spain!) and he seemed totally confused. It seems they lost the forms for a few weeks but kept making up excuses to hide that. I understand how busy the GP is, but I don’t think they should be picking up what they call “private work” if they don’t have the spare time to be doing it. I could’ve paid an actual private doctor to do it for me within a couple of days. The running of the surgery seems to be a complete mess which is a shame as I have been with Huntley Mount for most of my life and have only recently started to have problems. I am already getting much better service at another surgery and I only changed over to them a week ago.

recent_reviews.author: Lilliana
recent_reviews.text: Lovely GP practice with amazing staff and services! The one star complainers below have so much entitlement it’s unbelievable 😂 how about you trying working in an NHS service and see how you get on? It’s not easy and the staff are doing their best to cater to your needs, however they are not miracle workers. There is only so much they can do, you should appreciate whatever it is that they can offer. If you have to wait for something, you have to wait, end of story, and this is for ALL medical practices, no matter where you go. And if you’re rude to staff, how else are they supposed to respond? They do their best to be professional with you and offer their support but you’re not happy with it? Sounds like a you problem. If you’re that entitled and think you deserve higher treatment than anyone else, go somewhere else. I guarantee you the next practice you go to won’t tolerate your behaviour either. As for GP appointments, they only do them on the day and don’t pre-book them like other practices do because then they won’t have a back log of appointments. You’re lucky to even get them on the day! My previous practice never had appointments for a GP available for at least two months because of all the patients they had pre-booked! You would be complaining a hell of a lot more if this practice did the same thing, which thankfully they do not. NHS 111 is always an option if you don’t manage to get an appointment. Honestly none of you know what you’re talking about (evident in the way that a majority of you one star reviewers can’t even spell) so if you’re that unhappy, transfer somewhere else. The staff here don’t deserve your awful attitudes and complaints. Best GP in Bury!

recent_reviews.author: Leanne K
recent_reviews.text: I've always been made to feel welcome at this practice and received the highest level of care, that's from the reception staff and nurses, right through to the GP's who are fabulous. Dr Butt in particular, I find to be a very kind and caring doctor, who I feel understands my history and despite his very busy practice, seems to remember me and my medical background. In the few years I have been with this practice, I've never received anything but the highest care and been treated with kindness and respect. I have moved house since originally registering, so the practice is not as close as it was, but I haven't / wouldn't want to move to a different / closer GP practice, simply because the care my baby boy and I receive here, is second to none. I don't envy the staff here though, as it can be a difficult environment to work in. recent_reviews.author: Lynton Susman
recent_reviews.text: One of the most innacurate cliches from the public, describing the emergence from this pandemic is that, "GP Practices are all the same," suggesting, no matter which practice you are with, they all suffer from the same shortcomings. ie: they don't answer your calls, there are no face to face appointments, the receptionists are rude and GP's are still hiding under the cover of Covid. So, are they, indeed, all the same ? The reality is, whilst many practices have emerged from this pandemic, very successfully and efficiently, Unsworth Medical Centre have, somehow become frustratingly "stuck," and haven't appeared to make the kind of progress that, most would describe as, "getting back to some kind of normality." I have experienced hanging on the phone for up to 50 mins before my call to the practice was finally answered and more recently, an automated message suggesting receptionists were busy and to call back later. To ad insult to injury, the infamous text to all patients, advising to call the surgery ONLY if, "urgent/emergency assistance" was required. I heartily believe, certainly at the time of this posting, that this medical practice might actually fail to meet even the most basic needs of some of its patients. So, reaching the point at which I was begining to feel very vulnerable and neglected, I whole heartedly knew it was definitely time for a change. My wife and I are so, so, lucky to find a new GP practice, which thankfully resembles, absolutely nothing like, the above !

recent_reviews.author: bgn aquariums
recent_reviews.text: My mother was carried into this practice by my father after suffering from dizzy spells. She had been a few time but they found nothing wrong as she wasnt dizzy at that moment in time. This time she was dizzy. But the receptionist sent her away saying it wasnta walk in centre. I spoke to carol armstrong ( the practice manager) regarding this poor service. She promised me it would never happen again. Fast forward 18 months. Now my Father is suffering from high blood pressure. He tried for 6 weeks to get a face to face appointment and failed. Then one day he went to the surgery feeling desperately ill, to be turned away at the intercom. Eventually he got a face to face with a GP (a poor one at that). He was told by this waste of time GP that he was the fittest 79 yr old man he’d ever seen and was sent away. 2 days later my poor father suffered a massive stroke. Because we waited over 30 minutes for an ambulance we rang the surgery to see if a doctor could come and help, only to be told no, the doctor has other patients. He wouldn’t even speek on the phone. Where was this doctors duty of care? He was taken to Fairfield hospital. We rang the surgery and got a phone appointment with this so called GP. He said he was worried about what we had told him regarding my Dads condition as he was very good at detecting oncoming strokes. He missed this one, and it hit my Dad like a freight train. My Dads specialist said if he had been sent to A&E they could have prevented the stroke. 3 1/2 weeks after being told there was nothing wrong with him and he was the fittest 79 yr old man ever, my Dad sadly died. I hold this disgraceful so called Doctors practice responsable for my Dads death. This place needs a total overhaul. From doctors to reception. Especially the practice manager. A zero star rating is still too much for this disgraceful practice.
