recent_reviews.author: maic 66
recent_reviews.text: If there was an option for a zero rating then that's what I would have given it. If you're looking to change practice and use Blackford House Medical Centre my advice would be to give it a wide berth and choose a different practice altogether. Due to moving into the area I had to change practices so I've now been with this practice for just over 4 years and have regretted joining it ever since. The doctors at this practice seem pretty decent and genuine... however, if you're looking for quality care, respect and a level of helpfulness then forget it. From practice manager and right down through the ranks to receptionists all you get is a total lack of professionalism, rudeness, failures in duties followed by lies and false accusations. Normally I wouldn't take the time to write reviews however in this particular case I thought it's my duty to warn people what they would be letting themselves into. From the offset of joining this practice, I've been constantly accused of being rude and abusive towards the members of staff resulting in which I believe to be a "SPECIAL NOTE/black mark" being placed on my medical record. From my very first encounter to the very latest visit to the practice I've just encountered barriers ever which way. Not receiving notifications for things like flu jabs (because I'm type II diabetic), or simple things like changing quantities of medication on prescriptions. Constant barriers! For me what instigated all this animosity was my very first visit to the practice. I approached the reception desk to ask about a medical certificate and how long it would take to issue. My approach was calm but direct because to me... this was an important medical certificate which was needed for a new employer. Rather than replying with a simple "let me check... " what I got was "I haven't got the f-ing time to chase up stupid requests and it'll get sent out when it's sent out!" When I challenged her on why she was being so rude she tried twisting the situation and replied that it was actually me that was being rude and abusive and that she would be reporting me to the practice manager about my alleged abusive behaviour. I subsequently received a letter from the practice manager informing me that the practice will not tolerate aggressive and abusive behaviour towards NHS staff from patients and that any re-occurrance would result in me being struck-off the register. At no point was I ever approached or asked for my account of what was said or done...it was automatically taken for granted that I was the aggressor not the receptionist. Since then I've had countless incidents where receptionists have been rude to me, application forms for medical exemption certificates being lost preventing the certificates from being issued which inturn delaying me from getting my presciptions of upto 3 weeks or more. (forcing me to incur a financial cost for something that's free on the NHS with an exemption certificate). I've heard receptionists saying under their breaths here's that Bl**dy awkward Mr W _ _ _ _ again, what the F**k does he want now...? When I reported these and many more similar incidents to the Practice Manager her response were always totally dismissive and supportive towards her frontline staff insisting that it was I who was always being rude and the aggressor and that if I was not happy with the service provided by the surgery then it's my perogative and that I should go enrole with a different medical practice. These are just a few geniune accounts of my experiences with this practice. It's a closed shop where everyone sticks together and lies their ways out of a situation. Where no complaints are ever being logged or followed up on. "Duty of care" doesn't exist at this practice. It's literally a case of.... If you don't put a fake smile on your face then you're being abusive! lets see what happens when the CGC gets involved and they're Audited!

recent_reviews.author: Dana Sharkas
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this Practice for more than two years now. My experience has been a mixture between good and bad and here is why: Medical staff the two times a thorough follow up and requesting the right tests that led to serious diagnoses (one of them is hypothyroidism and the other is inflated gallbladder) were due to the good work of tow female medical staff members who put efforts to listen to me and ask the right questions. For the female medial staff members who’ve been in the practice in the past two years I give 5 starts. My experience however with male staff members was completely different. Before requesting the thyroid test by the female staff, another male doctor was taking my calls. For almost six months he kept insisting that my vitamins blood tests were ok (done 20 months before the consultations) and resisting doing new tests. He referred me to physiotherapy and offered a referral to psychotherapy but never occurred to him to check the Kidney, liver and thyroid like the female doctor did. After the results came back with underactive thyroid, I was referred to him again for explanation and was relieved that I finally knew the reason. His answer was don’t be so sure as we need to repeat the test twice to confirm. Later, during these two years my follow up on the symptoms and requests do more check were resisted often by other male staff members. One time I spoke to a senior doctor and ask him to explain the blood test, he did not know how to explain them so I asked to be referred to a specialist who can help me understand why my body in not settled until now, he shouted on the phone: no, will not refer you. If you want more tests check back in three months and hang up the phone! I kept having the abdominal pain and bloating until a new female doctor referred me to do an ultrasound and was then when we found the gallbladder problem. Phone system: was very bad in the past, then it was replaced with one that the line kept dropping after waiting for 40 minutes and when you manage to get hold to the reception staff, they will say they ran out of appointments for that day. Things have become better recently though, but you need to call at 8 am. Nurses: there have been several nurses in the past two years. One time I was asked to come and do the blood test again because the label was not fixed properly on the sample, so the lab refused to process it. Another time, I was called to do general check, weight, hight, blood pressure. The nurse measured my height while I was wearing heels! And insisted the scale was calibrated although it showed 4 KG discrepancy than 4 other different scales I used in the past few months. In the recent couple of months, medical staff have been more responsive, and they made some referral, and I am hoping the improvement will continue.

recent_reviews.author: Daisy Moyle
recent_reviews.text: Please if your a student and need a GP do not go here, I have been under this GP since my uni experience started a few years ago and it has been nothing but added stress throughout my long term health care issues. Every time a consultant has contacted in them in regards to information/a request for medication or treatment they have ignored,”lost” or simply forgot to contact me. I am never contacted in regards to important test results despite being told during these tests my doctor will ring me ASAP, I am ignored when I try to contact the GP manager. You will be more successful getting an appointment (as they’re apparently all gone by 8:15am) by calling 111 who will book you in to the appointments that are “taken”. If your health condition requires urgent care expect no urgency, if your medication is urgent expect it to be sent to the pharmacist in 4-6 week. Please avoid this GP at all costs, students coming and going seems to mean the GPS feel no patient commitment as they do not expect to be dealing with these people down the line when they eventually leave. I have dealt with stressed and overworked GPS before just not ones who seem so fed up and negligent towards their duty or care and patients. Told I had muscle pain, turned out to be a serious heart condition, amongst many other problems so please if you care about your health do not register here. UPDATE Since writing this review I have had referrals from consultants ignored, prescriptions never sent or acknowledged, multiple “lost results”, the survey claims a 4 week turn around for processing urgent test results, aka staff are sat in an office of results and it takes them four weeks to process can’t imagine how many people are waiting, during this time you won’t be told this it will be “still waiting for results” not we have received but still haven’t processed” whenever consultants chase up magically things are done, I suggest everybody takes up complaints with the NHS board as I have done because the practice truly doesn’t give a flying f*ck about anyone’s wellbeing. Avoid this GP practice like the plague.

recent_reviews.author: Lucy Inch
recent_reviews.text: Awful experience this morning at this practice. First of all they thought the best time to do a fire drill would be with a full waiting room and in the freezing cold and rain. Then when we came inside which was 10 minutes after my appointment was meant to be I checked my nhs app to see that my appointment had been changed to 10:45 without my knowledge or notification. There was a reason I booked it at 10:20 not 10:45. I have also never experienced this in the past but I assume it’s so they meet their key performance metrics around access and availability. Some clarity on this would be good and do not blame the fire drill as it was nearly 10 after I should’ve had my appointment when the fire drill was done. Then the nurse I saw basically just fobbed me off when my condition hasn’t improved at all in a week. I have been told to wait another week and come back if it doesn’t improve despite already waiting before I came in to see someone in the first place.

recent_reviews.text: Had to drop off a sample to be sent off and so I arrived at 6pm (half an hour before closing!) and was told they wouldn't take it as samples had already been sent off that day. There is 0 guidance anywhere that suggests what time they send samples off. Since it was a Friday night, I'd now have to repeat the sample due to it being time sensitive with the practice being closed over the weekend, before I could even walk back in to request more pots upon realising this, the staff had locked the practice door on me claiming they were closed, probably because they couldn't be bothered having someone walk in where they've already cleaned. Furthermore, my condition I've been visiting about causes me unbearable pain which the practice won't even prescribe pain killers for.

Furthermore, my condition I've been visiting about causes me unbearable pain which the practice won't even prescribe pain killers for.Like Share Response from the owner 2 months agoDear Sydney Thank you for taking the time to provide feedback regarding your recent experience at the practice. I am sorry to hear about the distress and frustration this caused you and appreciate the opportunity to respond. My name is Lesley Hyde and I am the Practice Business Manager and part of my role is to monitor and investigate any concerns or complaints made to the practice. Please se below my response to the issues you have raised: Sample Collection Arrangements We apologise for the inconvenience caused when you attended the practice to drop off a sample at 6pm and were advised that it could not be accepted at that time. We understand how frustrating this must have been for you. For clarity, samples must be received by the practice by 4:00pm to ensure they can be included in the scheduled daily laboratory collection at 4:30pm. Samples received after this time cannot be accepted, as they may not be stored within the required conditions and timeframes set by the laboratory. Accepting samples outside of these parameters risks inaccurate or invalid results, which could affect patient care and safety. We do have a poster displayed in our reception area outlining the sample cut off time; however, we acknowledge your feedback that this information may not have been sufficiently visible prior to your visit. As a result of your comments, we have now placed additional signage on our front entrance door and updated our practice website to make sample submission times clearer and more accessible. You can view this update here: https://www.thearchmedicalpractice.co.uk/practice-information/sample-collection/ Our clinicians usually advise patients of the relevant sample drop off times when issuing sample pots. If this did not occur in your case, we sincerely apologise. We have reminded all clinical and reception staff of the importance of clearly communicating sample cut-off times to patients to help prevent similar situations in the future. Access to the Practice Building We are sorry that you felt unable to re-enter the practice and that this added to your distress. For staff safety reasons, when a receptionist is working alone at the front desk and their colleague is temporarily required elsewhere, the front door may be placed on a buzzer system. In these circumstances, patients are still able to gain access by pressing the buzzer and would be let in by a member of staff. We regret if this was not clear at the time and if it appeared that the practice was closed earlier than advertised. I can assure you however, the practice was still open. Pain Management and Ongoing Care We are sorry to hear about the level of pain you are experiencing. Prescribing decisions, including pain relief, are made by clinicians based on individual clinical assessment and current medical guidance to ensure patient safety. A GP would only prescribe “pain killers” if they felt there was a clinical indication to do so. If your symptoms are persisting, then I would encourage you to arrange a further appointment with a clinician so that your pain and ongoing symptoms can be reviewed again. Next Steps We take all feedback seriously and are grateful that you have brought these matters to our attention, which has already led to improvements in how we share information with patients. If you would like your concerns to be investigated further under the NHS complaints procedure, or if you wish to discuss my response further, please contact me at the practice (0161 226 0606). We are always looking for new members to join our PPG, if you would like further information of if you are interested in joining is, please click the below link: https://www.thearchmedicalpractice.co.uk/practice-information/patient-participation-group/ Yours faithfully Mrs Lesley Hyde Practice Business Manager

recent_reviews.author: Lea Shaughnessy
recent_reviews.text: This is the first GP I've really loved being with, and as someone with multiple chronic conditions I couldn't praise them highly enough. This does mean I have experience with many Drs which can make communication easier for me, but I find all the team here perfectly reasonable. I also will say you must request appts through the app at 8 am as is generally standard, but no phone waits. I have had multiple conditions diagnosed here that are infamously under-diagnosed and ignored, for example especially with regards to female hormonal health. These are conditions I have spent up to 10 years visiting GPs about and bring turned away. The even use local anaesthetic for IUD insertions, before I requested! I have never found any of the doctors here dismissive. I've seen Dr Kandola, Dr Chaudri, Dr Hamza, Dr Collabella, Dr Chhoangalia, Dr Cooper, maybe even more. But I could not highly enough praise Dr Kidd. Both the care she offered and bedside manner were far above standard, and made some pretty horrific experiences absolutely tolerable. She does not sugar-coat either, she is truthful about what is uncomfortable and helps you get through it. Hailey Daniel has been fantastic to see as well. Both these staff have been very thorough to answer my questions and make sure my consent is informed. My meds get regularly reviewed. I get contacted about my necessary jabs. Script refills are done VERY promptly through the app too. The standard of GP receptionists in England seems to be dire, but I've always found those at the Arch to be pleasant and as helpful as they can given the NHS systems in place. They also have an option where you can keep your place in the phone queue for a callback, which I find great. I may often wait 10 mins for my appointment, again a factor of NHS conditions I believe. For Christ's sake they give out free fruit, I don't think they could do better if Jesus himself came down to heal the sick.

recent_reviews.author: Andrew
recent_reviews.text: From my experience the doctors in this surgery are hit and miss in terms of your care. It is like a lucky dip you could get someone really good or someone not that good, one doctor in the past smirked and laughed when I was being serious talking regarding my mental health with them and that wasn't very encouraging experience, but on other occasions I've seen really good doctors in the surgery where I've left feeling good. And some of the receptionists can be rude and not caring, and don't know correct information as recently I've had one of them tell me in a condescending tone that they do not do something in a certain way but I knew for a fact they can do as someone I know had emailed them earlier that day for me regarding the situation so I told the receptionist to go and check the emails and they came back on the phone after checking and they didn't have that rude condescending know it all tone anymore as they probably felt a bit silly once they knew I was right, so sometimes it's hard to trust what they say is correct. On another occasion I was told I would be able to get a doctors letter regarding a personal issue and I was asked to pay 30 pound to have the doctor type up the letter for me, the letter was supposed to take up to 4 weeks so 1 day before the 4 week timeframe was up I contacted the surgery to see what is going on and I was told the doctor can't do the letter anymore, they can do the letter if they wanted to as I know of other people that have had the same letter done by a doctor, but why take the payment from me for the doctor and then why does It take 4 weeks to tell me the doctor can't do the letter, surely I could of been told that a lot earlier and if I didn't chase them up they wouldn't of even contacted me within the 4 weeks timeframe I was told I would receive the letter by. This surgery could be doing better training with the receptionists to have better manners and be more mindful when speaking to people, and maybe get some better doctors so that every doctor is good and there is more consistency in the care of patients so it's not as hit and miss... And you state in your most recent reply to this review that you've replied to my 'reviews' many of times and they are always changing, as if you are trying to make out I'm lying and I'm making numerous separate reviews, I can guarantee this is the only review I have made and I have only edited this review to correct spelling errors etc that I have noticed, you have replied to this review twice not many of times like you said. I can assure you everything I have said in this review is true. I hope things improve with the surgery in the future as it's my local surgery and I don't like going anywhere else as there is some good doctors and staff at the Arch Medical Practice. Thanks for listening.

recent_reviews.author: Liam
recent_reviews.text: Impossible to get an appointment. Despite what is claimed below. I have since changed to a different surgery.
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: LiamLocal Guide · 18 reviewsEdited a year ago Impossible to get an appointment. Despite what is claimed below. I have since changed to a different surgery.Like1 Share Response from the owner a year agoHi Liam Thank you for taking the time to leave us a review. I am sorry that you feel we only deserve a 1* rating. One of the things we pride ourselves on is how accessible we are here at The Arch, therefore I am surprised to read that you find it "impossible to get an appointment". As of today, at 9:31am, we still have over 20 GP appointments free to book (including via the NHS app). Mon-Fri 8am - we release appointments which can be booked via the NHS app. These remain bookable all day long until the appointments have all been taken. Most days we still have appointments free to book until late morning. Mon-Fri 12pm - we release appointments which can be booked via the NHS app, these are for 6 days in advance. We have lots of other services which too can be booked via the NHS app such as physiotherapy and symptomatic sexual health checks (which remain available to book all day long). Mon-Fri 8am to 6:30pm you can submit a request via our online service where we can offer you advice and guidance, you can also submit admin requests for letters, sick notes, forms to be completed etc via this method: Contact us about your request (accurx.nhs.uk) Mon-Fri 8am to 6pm we operate a duty GP list, this means we never turn away elderly, vulnerable, mental health, chronic disease, palliative patients and we always see children up to the age of 14, regardless of the time the patient contacts us. We also have extended access appointments available in the evenings and weekends and currently they too have not been used at maximum capacity. If you cannot use the NHS app for any reason, you can of course call us, however we believe that if a patient can use social media then there should be no reason for them not to use the NHS app. You can also visit the practice if for any reason you cannot call us or use our online platforms. It is important for us to keep the phone lines free for our elderly and vulnerable patients who simply cannot use the NHS App. I would reach out to you to directly to discuss how you can easily book appointments here at the practice, however I am unable to trace you on our system. Please can I ask that you contact me as soon as possible on 0161 226 0606 so that I can try to understand this issues you have encountered and if indeed this is a review for the correct practice. I look forward to hearing from you. Many thanks Lesley Hyde Practice Manager

I am sorry that you feel we deserve a 1* review & I to read that you are unhappy with the service you have received from us. On investigation it has been reported to me that you booked a GP appointment for a letter to confirm you have been unwell for 5 days. There are lots of reasons why we would be unable to provide you with the letter: 1) you have a self-limiting condition which doesn’t currently need treating by a GP. 2) as we have not seen or treated you for your illness we would not be able to provide you with a letter confirming that you have been unwell. 3) private letters do not form part of our GMS contract & must be done outside of our NHS core hours. The letter you requested is also chargeable at £30 & the wait for a private letter can be up to 4 weeks. 4) as you were unhappy with the above information our receptionist provided you with, she booked you a call with a GP tonight to discuss the self-management of your illness, however I must stress that this will not result in a letter being produced today. If you need proof of your call with the GP, please visit the NHS app where your consultation will be available. I can see that you have 2 cancelled appointments & I am extremely sorry that this has been frustrating for you. Yesterday you booked in with a GP for a mild illness, we care navigated you to the pharmacy which you were agreeable with. You then booked in today for the same reason but explained it was for a letter to day say you have been unwell. Our care navigation team are trained to signpost patients appropriately to reduce the amount of avoidable GP appointments that are booked unnecessarily on a daily basis. You can book appointments lots of different ways (Mon to Fri). Via the NHS App: 8am - on the day appointments for urgent issues. 12pm - routine appointments for 6 days in advance. If you prefer a weekend or evening appointment then you call the Practice (anytime) where we will book this for you (we call this enhanced access). We also refer patients to the pharmacy throughout the day. If you have an admin request, i.e. for a letter, then you can request this via our online consult: https://florey.accurx.com/p/P84630/patient-form I hope that this answers any question you may have around our appointment system & that you can now understand why your face to face appointments were cancelled. Should you wish to discuss this further, please reach out to me on 0161 226 0606. Yours faithfully, Lesley Hyde Practice Manager

You can book appointments lots of different ways (Mon to Fri). Via the NHS App: 8am - on the day appointments for urgent issues. 12pm - routine appointments for 6 days in advance. If you prefer a weekend or evening appointment then you call the Practice (anytime) where we will book this for you (we call this enhanced access). We also refer patients to the pharmacy throughout the day. If you have an admin request, i.e. for a letter, then you can request this via our online consult: https://florey.accurx.com/p/P84630/patient-form I hope that this answers any question you may have around our appointment system & that you can now understand why your face to face appointments were cancelled. Should you wish to discuss this further, please reach out to me on 0161 226 0606. Yours faithfully, Lesley Hyde Practice Manager

recent_reviews.author: Requiemae
recent_reviews.text: I would advise avoiding this practice if you can. They are frustrating to deal with and at times have bordered on dangerous. Referrals made for the wrong patient/ unnecessary investigations Of course, no apology given when this was brought to their attention. Referrals they said they would make - not making them and not informing you of this. Borderline impossible to book an appointment if you have a job while simultaneously holding long term medication hostage if you don't book one. I'm not sure what they expect patients to do, book a day off in case theres an available slot when you call in at 8am? And if there's no slot then what? Do the same the next day? There is there online system as well which can be unavailable for weeks at a time. Of course when you do finally manage to book in you get a 4 hour window during which the GP will call you and even then they sometimes manage to call outside those times. Now I appreciate that GPs are overworked and busy and I don't mind being called later than expected. But it's ridiculous to have to clear an entire morning/afternoon for a 10-15min consultation. And god forbid you miss their call (when they call outside the stated times), you'll get a condescending message saying that they couldn't reach you and you have to do the whole process all over again.

recent_reviews.author: Sam Brown
recent_reviews.text: The doctors and medical staff at this surgery are attentive, professional, knowledgeable and are all round great and I couldn't praise them any more. What really lets this surgery down is the staff who answer the phones - their entire goal is to usher you away, whether or not they've actually dealt with your problem or not. They really couldn't care less in helping your issue or sign posting you in the right direction, they just incentivise you as much as they can to look elsewhere. Considering they are the face of their doctor's surgery, that just astounds me. Every single time I interact with them it's incredibly disheartening, as they don't answer your queries and just come back with useless and empty suggestions or advice. I just rang up asking about updating a prescription as there's a manufacturing issue with the pharamcies, and the reply I got was "I'll message someone, OK?", and I literally had to probe with multiple questions as what exactly that means as she was trying to hang up the phone. I had no idea what exactly had been resolved or what the next steps were? They genuinely couldn't care any less about your issue, they just want you off the phone. Not long ago I rang about holiday vaccines, before I had even finished my sentence their reply was "we don't do that here, OK?" and just before she was about to hang up after deploying her 'golden advice' I had to say "can I have a bit more than that please, where should I go to?". They either have not been trained sufficiently to deal with relevant patient issues, or they simply do not care. I'm going to go for a mixture of both.

recent_reviews.text: Mostly okay experience, it takes a while to get through on the phone (I’ve been 50th place in the queue at 8:30am) but I’ve always managed to get an appointment and the nurse who did my blood test was lovely. One of the receptionists , not sure who , usually has a dismissive tone. I was told by the NHS website to book a GP appointment if experiencing symptoms of tachycardia. I explained this to the receptionist who admitted “I don’t know what you’re talking about” in reference to my symptoms. She didn’t direct me to a GP and instead tried to schedule a video call with a contracted private company. When I said I wasn’t free that day, she told me to ring up another day to see if they had any spaces. I don’t understand why she thought this was the appropriate avenue, when I rang 111 about my tachycardia they correctly gave me a GP appointment for it. I dealt with the same receptionist after my GP appointment. The nurse specifically instructed me to wait for a call back for the admin team about any cancellations for an ECG. I missed a call from them, waited that day, and called back the next day to notify them that I hadn’t made an appointment still. When I told this to the receptionist she was confused and told me that it was my responsibility to call the practise, contrary to what I was told. Throughout the call she had the same dismissive tone and it sounded like my problems were just an inconvenience to her. I get that receptionists have to juggle appointments and what not but I didn’t do a single thing wrong. I don’t even want to call the practise anymore because I feel stupid when I speak to her.

recent_reviews.author: Albert Ross
recent_reviews.text: (Using a pseudonym as people appear to have been removed from the register for writing critical feedback) To have limited resources and capacity is one thing, but what brings the NHS and The Arch Medical into the realm of systematic neglect is that it copes with its shortcomings through gaslighting, invalidation and dishonesty which severely affects patient outcomes. Whilst I like socialised healthcare, and despite the sanctimonious PR, I could never again speak praise of such a harmful system in dire need of reform. If you ever have an injury that affects your judgement in any way, please, please, please find somebody who will help you act in your best interest because it certainly won't be The Arch Medical practice or better yet register somewhere else in the first place with a track record of responsibility. I saw the reviews, brushed them off and registered and it is something I will regret for a long time and perhaps the rest of my life. Please don't do this, this is your health, it is worth so much more than that.

recent_reviews.text: It’s true that it can be difficult to book an appointment here due to how oversubscribed it is. recent_reviews.text: I had to change this as my current experience during the last few months has been awful. Today (Saturday 19/10/19) I had to go to the GP because I had an appointment with my son that got cancelled for the second time. Since I'm working full time I thought I could use this opportunity to collect my repeated prescription from the reception. I went there and I was told that today they are only attending Flu patients, I can understand that, although I didn't know. I've asked for an exception given that I need to take this everyday for life, explaining that I wasn't aware that they are not supposed to do so, because it wasn't a 'normal day'. To my surprise I've just found a person with a lack of empathy and common sense. This person didn't even ask whether my prescription was for a life-threatening illness or not. That is worryingly negligent from an institution entrusted with the care of people. Just to clarify, the waiting room was empty, there were two receptionists at the time, my prescription was 50 cm and 1 minute away from there. I was not asking for anything unrealistic and I tried to explain the reason for my confusion, but I just received a “no” for a response. Obviously, I was denied the chance to speak to someone else. I can understand rules, although I wasn't aware of those. This was clearly a terrible misunderstanding as I thought the practice was open (due to my son's appointment). I think this world would be a lot better if people were more reasonable and empathetic. My experiences with doctors, on the other hand, have been mainly positive

recent_reviews.author: E
recent_reviews.text: This doctors surgery have let me down immensely. Previously this doctors have provided an okay service, but for the last 3+ months they have been incredibly useless. I had an appointment in November of which was then given a referral to the orthopaedic department for a potential stress fracture in my knee and badly damaged ankle and I needed help relatively quickly. I changed my address the day of that appointment at the Doctors request to speed up the process. Three weeks later I got a call saying they hadn't changed my address so my referral hadn't gone out yet, so I changed it for a second time during that call. I called several times since then but still no referral. It is now over three months since that appointment and today I have been told that the person who changed my address didn't notify anyone so my hospital letter was sent to my old address and there is a possibility I have to start again on the waiting list. This is appalling and I was unable to walk for a long period of time and as an full time endurance runner my entire ability to do any form of training has been ruined and set me back a great deal. I am incredibly upset, and it is down to the staff that work there that I have been forced to stop training for months longer than I needed and in pain to be due to getting no help I needed because of this. I am incredibly upset and do not recommend this doctors if you require help as they can't even seem to change a simple address. Edit: Even after constant calling and trying to get my referral sorted, the receptionists continue to be rude and have even blamed the situation on me several times stating that "They were waiting for me to change my address" even after all this time. They have refused to help with the referral even though it is all down to this practice that I will now not see a specialist for over 5 months.

recent_reviews.author: Dave Marshall
recent_reviews.text: The level of care from medical staff is excellent, but this practice is marred by systematic operational failure. In attempting to book an appointment, you are directed to call back at 8am on a certain day of the week, once the next batch of appointments are released. This creates a free-for-all in which all patients, desperate for appointments, have to call literally hundreds of times in order to be connected to a receptionist. This system is not fit for purpose. Arch Medical, please listen to the reviews being submitted here. Everyone is saying the same thing. How you are operating is not satisfactory. No other practice I have been registered with uses this system, nor do they have these issues. Since you seem to put so much effort into responding to every one of these reviews, please can I use this medium to get a response: Please help me book an appointment. Please send me registration documents so that I can book online, I never reieved these. This practice needs to recognise that when it comes to booking appointments, the responsibility for being organised lies at their feet and not at the patient's. Not interested in a copy & paste response telling us that you're looking in to the problem because I don't believe it.

It is true to say that our list size has increased over the last couple of years. This is due to the city expanding and more residential properties (and student halls) being built. This is the same with many of the central manchester GP practices. We have addressed this by recruiting three more doctors and an new nurse practitioner. We are also trying to manage appointments by writing to those who book and don't show up and by signposting patient to other health professionals so patients can be seen sooner. Pill checks can be done by many local pharmacies and is not necessary something you need to see you doctor for. Likewise the Hathersage centre is there for more complex health needs. The NHS in general is over subscribed but by choosing well and the right service for you needs, you can help the NHS meet this growing demand.

recent_reviews.author: Russell Lindley
recent_reviews.text: In my experience this is one of the best NHS GP practices in the city, if not the North. It has a functional online booking system in addition to telephoning. The reception staff are generally professional and sympathetic. They have two sites in the city and they are opening a third soon. At some other GP practices in the city, the *only* way to get an appointment is by phoning first thing in the morning and hoping that they still have some slots available. By contrast, at Cornbrook it's usually possible to book routine appointments about 2-4 weeks in advance, and get more urgent appointments much more quickly. All GPs are struggling at the moment because the NHS is underfunded and overstretched in accordance with the government's austerity policies. Most of the negative reviews reflect that.

The waiting room may look empty, but staff, especially doctors, have a huge list of responsibilities they need to do, including signing off prescriptions, arranging referrals, writing letters for patients, reviewing results, updating medical records, planning ongoing care, attending training and more. All of these take time and as they form important parts of patient care, need to be accommodated into a doctors working day. Unfortunately, I am unable to go into detail on each point you have made as I cannot confirm your identity. However, if you would like to make an official complaint and would like these incidents looking into, please fill out a feedback form on our website or speak to a member of the reception team. Kind Regards, Lauren Engagement & Communications Officer

recent_reviews.text: AVOID AVOID AVOID...worst GP practice in Manchester. Shame I had to register my family here as it was the closest to my home. However my elderly mother is in so much pain and they can not even issue her medication on time which has been order via the chemist a week in advance as the practice ask. I have had to call the practice personally to ask what the Issue is , to which she said put a request in... erm I have twice !!! no review is due and medication is on repeat so what is the issue??? The receptionist wouldn’t put the request in so again I call the chemist and they have requested the medication and here I am two weeks later and still no medication for my poor mother. Now this could be serious if the person in question was on end of life/ cancer or heart medication for example and I feel it’s very careless. I do not blame the chemist as they have shown me the request with the dates and times. The reception there will nit do anything for patients so what exactly do they do all day if they can’t even issue medication? This seriously need to be looked at and a complaint will be going in. To be in pain at any age is bad but a 93 year old suffering is heartbreaking. I will be moving GPs, this practice needs to be shut down as it’s not at all bothered about patients but how to make money.

recent_reviews.author: Jess Linfoot
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely awful experience, avoid this practice at all costs. On attempting to book a face to face appointment online, it was shown to me that the only option available was a phone call appointment, not suitable for this particular issue. Called the practice to attempt to get an in person appointment, and the receptionist was absolutely abhorrent. Condescending, rude and was insistent i book online even though i had repeatedly explained why i could not. After less than a minute long conversation, she had clearly decided that it was not worth her time to book me an appointment and put the phone down on me. As much as i would love to say this is a one off incident, this is now the second time this member of staff has hung up the phone on me. I worry for vulnerable people who may need an appointment urgently and are unable to get one because one member of staff has decided it is not worth her breath to do her job. Worth noting however that all of the doctors and suede practitioners are absolutely lovely and if you can jump through the thousands of hoops to get an appointment they are all very professional, patient and quick.

recent_reviews.author: Parul Singh
recent_reviews.text: I actually cannot fault this GP practice! I have been with them for around 18 months now, I’ve never struggled for appointment when I’ve needed them, they process my repeat prescriptions same day etc. I’ve seen various GPs at the practice depending on who is available and I have felt heard and supported by every single one, which is so rare in general but particularly as a young, disabled, neurodivergent woman of colour. I had my most recent appointment with Dr Aunet regarding a recent decline in my mental health following a traumatic event. I was struggling to articulate myself because of my mental state but she was kind and let me take my time. I felt my mental health was taken seriously and her priority was ensuring I was safe, then we explored some support options and she offered regular check ins with the GP No GP practice is going to be perfect given the pressure they’re under but that’s not always in their control and I’ve genuinely never had a negative experience and I couldn’t recommend this practice more Thank you to all the team here for restoring my faith in GP practices and doing your best to keep me in good health ❤️

Dr. Tamara is not only highly professional, but also compassionate and thoughtful. She goes above and beyond to help her patients, and I feel very fortunate to have had her as my doctor. The reception staff needs to understand patients emotions and the situation they are in, these blood test was very important n am waiting to find out the result eagerly but why they bothered abut it. recent_reviews.author: elle beee
recent_reviews.text: I would absolutely love to give 5 stars for the amazing doctors and medical staff. They deserve it! However, whats made me knock one star off is the receptionist. Most receptionists at the range are lovely, but there is this one member of reception who delivers her words in a sarcastic, dehumanising tone. Because I have a stuttering issue and have a hard time getting my words out she sighed as loud as possible and interrupted me as I was talking and ended the call before I even got a chance to thank her. It’s almost as if she is bored of her job… or me. Or both. And with the current situation with the job market, she’s taking a huge risk. It’s not hard to be kind and patient. After seeing reviews here mentioning the same issue with this one lady, I think it’s safe to say it still hasnt been dealt with. And it’s not my first run in with this particular woman either. However on a lighter note, the doctors and other medical staff are wonderful, kind, and deal with things as quickly and efficiently as possible! But that receptionist gives the whole clinic a bad name.

recent_reviews.author: Ally Wilson
recent_reviews.text: I've attended this surgery for over 20 yrs. I've watched the Practioners, nurses, admin/reception staff come and go. However, I have never felt the need to re-register at another GP practice, once leaving the one I grew up with and joining this one. They work as a team, are exceptionally busy and they have to put up with alot, due to the ever changing society we live in. They can get irritable and frustrated, alittle bit abrupt at times, but they're only human, just like us after all! (and this is only the frontline that I am referring to by the way). recent_reviews.author: Asima Mahmood
recent_reviews.text: Recently I had the experience of calling my parent's GP surgery (not the range medical centre). The way I had to navigate through the receptionist, the online form that is there to book an appointment that is x3 pages long was frustration on another level. Whilst I was filling that form to obtain an appointment for my poorly dad, I was thinking to myself my GP’s practice doesn’t have all this plava, how on earth can my 72 year old father who is not internet savvy possibly do this, no wonder he was going around in circles over the last month unable to get an appointment. Long story short “the range medical centre” is absolutely brilliant! Now that I have had the experience of other GP surgeries I can say that honestly, I always get an appointment, the ladies are lovely at the reception, the whole team are great!! I have never had an issue the 19 or so years I have been registered there. One star short is for the reception decor. Other than that the rest is all brilliant.

recent_reviews.text: Prior to this GP I tried one down the road, they spent an hour on the phone and told me it’d take 28 days to register me. This GP It’s a way from me but I regret nothing, I called them and they registered me on the spot. I have moved a lot, and can honestly say this is the best GP I have had by miles. Every time I interact with them I am bowled over. Receptionists are friendly and helpful. The pharmacist is outstanding, first pharmacist who actually read the NICE guidelines for my conditions let alone took the time to ask me about the specifics and tailored the prescriptions to my needs. Today they issued my repeat prescription within an hour of the request. An hour! I’ve had private healthcare nowhere near as good. Kudos to the practice manager for maintaining an impeccable service in these trying times.

recent_reviews.author: Guz Chuz
recent_reviews.text: Avoid this practice if you have any other choices available. I have been using this practise my whole life, 26 years, since they were opposite the park. I don't much remember how things were when I was young and I haven't had much cause to go in my adult life. Every time I have though it has been a nightmare. When trying to book an appointment they usually don't have anything available for around a month so if time is an issue you have to book an emergency appointment on the day, even if you wouldn't class it as an emergency. When calling for an emergency appointment in the morning you will typically wait on the phone for 30-45 minutes. When you eventually get through to the rude reception staff you'll be asked for information about your emergency. The secretary, with no medical training, will then decide whether she wants to give you an appointment or not. If you tell them you'd rather keep the info between yourself and the doctor they will insist you tell them or refuse to give you an appointment. In the last 10 years I think I've actually seen a doctor 3 times, I'm not dead yet but this kind of treatment of patients in dangerous and unhealthy. Im not oblivious to the reasons here either, with so many people on the books they want to prioritise but treating everybody like a time waster is not a good way to do that. Once again, if you can sign up at another practice do so, it will save you unnecessary stress. Maybe your life too.

recent_reviews.text: I initially wrote a one star review as I got Appalling service by Dr K . This is also not the first occasion this has happened with this specific Dr (infact previously she was one of my favourite GPs especially when it came to children as I felt she was thorough). On this occasion I contacted the gp practice for my son who is under one who had a nose bleed. As a pharmacist I am fully aware of what pharmacy can offer and what knowledge we have and this needed further investigation. Instead of seeing my son she referred the query to pharmacy first for us to only be told this is not an appropriate query for pharmacy first and that my son should be seen by a gp and that this is a red flag. I was completely disheartened by the practice with the constant pushing me to another health care, usually pharmacy or some random resource but my faith has been restored by Sami as a result I have changed my review from a one star to a four star. Sami is an asset to the gp practice, kind and considerate and very polite and professional. I accidentally missed my blood pressure appointment and had the times mixed up and he didn’t make me feel guilty or bad or anything but rather simply booked me in the next day. Thank you Sami!

recent_reviews.author: Afroz A
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely appalling service – avoid Limelight Health at all costs. I was booked a follow-up telephone consultation three weeks in advance. I stayed in all day from 7am, phone in hand, waiting for the call. Nothing. No call, no missed-call notification, no voicemail. When I rang the surgery, I was told the doctor apparently “called twice and I didn’t answer” – completely untrue. The receptionist refused to investigate, offered no apology, and just said “nothing can be done” and “we’ll just go round in circles”. I now have to start the entire process again and wait weeks more for the appointment I should have had. No accountability, no empathy, and what appears to be a falsified clinical record stating calls were made when they weren’t. Patients are being blamed for the surgery’s failures. Reception staff clearly need urgent training and better systems are needed to stop this kind of thing happening. Deeply unhappy and still without the medical follow-up I need. I do not recommend this practice to anyone.

recent_reviews.author: Angie McGibbon
recent_reviews.text: WorstGP ever. I'm trying to move after being moved here because my practice closed. Virtually impossible to get an appointment. Told if you have a smartphone you need to book via the app. So I downloaded the app and logged on. At 10.45am the app appears not to be working and so I call. 20 mins to get thru on the phone to be told no appointments left and I have to log in to the app at 8am the next day. Here we go again 8.15 app crashes takes a long time to get thru on the phone to be told no appointments left again for that day. Even if I could have one it would have to be a telephone appointment not to see a doctor. How hard can it be. I give up. It's too stressful. I was also referred to the menopause clinic in April but have heard nothing. I mentioned this and was told I had to chase the referral myself. Not very helpful as I've no idea who to call to do this. This GP practice does not care about the patients or want to help them. I will have to try and get transferred. UPDATE 2 years later still shocking. After trying for days to get an appointment get asked to attend the surgery, Seen by a medical student who tells me my ear infection is fine and will clear up on its own. Qualified doctor checks, sees a problem and orders a prescription to be sent to pharmacy downstairs. Go to pharmacy they don't have it - say GP not sent it. Back to GP who say they have sent it to a different pharmacy 45 miles away? Told to call other pharmacy and get it sent here. Do so, other pharmacy don't have it they state it was sent to pharmacy here - the one downstairs from the surgery. Two hours of chasing later, pharmacy downstairs from surgery says they will order it but no idea when it's in to keep calling them. I think the surgery and the pharmacy are competing for who can be the most incompetent , jury's out - it's a close call.

recent_reviews.author: Kevin Gallagher
recent_reviews.text: I had to come back on here and edit this review with a update. In May 23 I went into this surgery to pick a prescription up they couldn't find it anywhere, after me waiting 20 mins, they asked if I could come back tomorrow and it would be ready no waiting at all. Went back the day the prescription wasn't ready, they asked me to take a seat I refused and walked out telling them we will try again tomorrow so back I went the next day it was ready but not signed by a Dr another 5 mins waiting. In August I filled the online form in at 8am to see a Dr I got a text back to go and see the pharmacist at Ayres Rd chemist, I rang the chemist they knew nothing about it. recent_reviews.author: Angharad Huw
recent_reviews.text: Been with this gp for two years now and have been needed appointments around twice a month due to various undiagnosed issues. Quick, same day appointments/ prescriptions every time I submit an AskMyGp request apart from maybe two times in late summer/autumn 2022. I dislike that I’m given a different doctor nearly every time I have an appointment, but all have been very empathetic, friendly, and focused on finding a solution that works for me. I can see that there’s a lot of negative reviews and there are some organisational things like only being able to book appointments at 8am that are annoying to deal with. It’s frustrating when I have to wait for a callback at an unknown time of day, as in my work I’m unable to use my phone, which results in me missing the doctor’s calls. However, the quality of care is excellent. I’ve had many GPs even call or text me after leaving the appointment to supply extra details or give me a more in depth answer to a question I had during the appointment. This is also the case when they chase up hospital referrals for me so that I don’t have to. Overall I’m very happy with the care I receive at Limelight, but there are definitely things that could be done better, namely the booking system.

recent_reviews.text: Im giving one star because Google won't allow me to give anything less. One of the most unhelpful, time-wasting, and uncaring practises out there, especially with the staff that sit at reception. Everytime I call in, I get messed around, told to email, use the app etc which doesn't always work or display the name of the doctor I want to speak to. When I inform the receptionist of this, she just says to try again later as if I've got nothing else to do than spend a whole week trying to book an appointment for a problem that has left me in severe pain. I then ask if she can at least put in a request for repeat medication that I've been on for several years; she again refuses saying I need to use the app. I explain that I've tried but I had several problems last time which left me without medication for a long time as the request wasn't going through for some reason: she says there's nothing she can do. I've been waiting for MONTHS for hospital appointments which were delayed because they didn't pass on my messages to the doctor; I could go on and on but the reality is you can expect better service at 99p chickenshop takeaway. If you can, AVOID!!

recent_reviews.author: Rebecca Neale
recent_reviews.text: Doctor Mashal was very understanding and listened to my concerns. It was easy to tell that he cared about what I had to say and that's a really reassuring trait to come across in a Doctor. The AskmyGp system is a little hit-or-miss and you do have to make a request as soon as it goes online at 8am to ensure you get an appointment but I expected that due to business. I would have also preferred to have had a time slot allocated so that I was sitting and waiting for a call all day but other than that, I can't fault the treatment.

The last time he had a fever I didn't even bother contacting them as I couldn't be bothered with the thought of being fobbed off with a pharmacy referral. I get that the NHS is stretched and particularly GP practices, but you should be allowed a consultation every once in a while without a battle. I definitely hope nothing serious ever happens to myself or my family or we better hope the pharmacy can treat us. However having seen the pharmacist as they told me to, I'm none the wiser so what an absolute waste of people's time and energy to pass them round such a useless and inefficient circus. recent_reviews.author: Mike Chidley
recent_reviews.text: Ashville clinicians are always accessible via AskMyGP and the advice they give is helpful and constructive. I consulted one of the Ashville GPs yesterday (Dr Garside), requiring help to improve the management of my chronic severe back pain. The assistance he provided was twofold: firstly to explain about some specific pain reduction medications and to provide more appropriate dosages; and secondly he undertook to expedite an appointment at a regional pain clinic for which I've been waiting an excessively long time. Both these actions were very relevant and supportive and will, I'm sure, improve my situation.

recent_reviews.author: Shereen Simmonds
recent_reviews.text: Awful experience. Taken me off the database because I’ve moved from the area, even though I work 5 minutes away. I expressed that I would struggle changing gps because of underlying issues and they didn’t show any empathy. I expressed that my dentist etc were still in Manchester, as I am physically unavailable through the week to attend any appointments, working 6am until 8pm Monday to Friday. I stated that I’d had an ongoing condition, knew what it was but they had to test me. The first test they lost, the 2nd test they tested for the incorrect issue, the third they said I didn’t have what I thought. When I was referred to a specialist they confirmed on the day (within minutes of being tested) that I did in fact have what I initially thought! My family member used a doctor here when she was extremely depressed. When they asked what was wrong with her, she expressed that she didn’t know, to which they replied, “well if you don’t know how am I supposed to know.” For someone who was vulnerable at the time, that isn’t what you’d expect to be said from a health care professional. I believe if she wasn’t as strong as she was, just may have tried something unthinkable. When I sent a letter of complaint nothing was done. The doctors name is Dr Hoddes! They misdiagnose people, give them antibiotics or painkillers and they end up dying of cancer. Avoid at all costs!!!

recent_reviews.author: See See
recent_reviews.text: If you want to die, not get referred or seen, visit this GP surgery!!! A family member visited this surgery on several occasions with stomach pains and weight loss. This GP surgery fobbed her off with painkillers and antibiotics. My relative collapsed at home, ended up in hospital via ambulance requiring 4 units of blood because of a burst ulcer. Another family member has had chest issues, she's been wheezing for months and the GP only prescribed her with antibiotics over and over again. No referral to find out what's happening. A friend is suffering from chronic pain in her leg due to having surgery. All they have prescribed her is co-codamol. She needs something stronger but can't get an appointment. The staff here are also rude. They have no compassion, come across as patronising and have no respect, especially the reception staff. As some have mentioned the staff are good, it makes me wonder if this GP surgery has it's prejudices. The only good respectable doctor they had was Dr Beresford and he retired. This surgery needs closing down. If I could give a zero star rating, I would.

recent_reviews.author: Oj B
recent_reviews.text: It's so heartbreaking to see this practice degenerate to this level. How hard can it be for people to be nice and professional? They have a lot to do in terms of training all their staff. And I mean ALL of them! From people's skills to civility, mannerisms, tone of voice when addressing patients and how to approach to patients who are already suffering. I've had so many unpleasant encounters with them that I don't want to mention. They make it look like they are doing a favour by attending to you. So appalling! They soon will be having no stars whatsoever if they don't make proper and needed adjustments on their people's skills. It really is appalling! Yelling at patients!! 9/03/2026 I can't believe that I am back here after 4 years to leave a very negative review of this establishment. Before, I go any further - I want to make it clear that, whatever issues patients are having with this medical centre are 90 to 95% front desk, admin, nurses and lesser staff (sorry, for lack of a better word to use.) The Dr's are unaware of the front desk, admin, and lesser staff issues - and yet bear the brunt of the end of the stick should the establishment suffer. I've had very unbelievable and excrutiatingly painful experiences with them from the beginning of this year. In short, (they put up lies and mark your profile, including your number should you call and then mete you undeserved shabby treatment by whoever picks your call, and for whatever reasons best known to them). From the tone of answering your call and how you are responded to is clear and obvious! It is like a syndicate in operation!!! Very evil and unprofessional!!! But we must continue to voice these issues until changes are made, and wrongs are righted. This afternoon I made a call to the centre, having moved to a new home, my daughter who had ran out of medication, due to pressure of moving into a new home and the process of registering with a near gp when settled; called Gorton Medical centre before the weekend to kindly ask for a repeat to be sent to the pharmacy for her to collect. It was not actioned. We called 111 for emergency prescription over the weekend. Today being Monday and on her last tablet, I called the pharmacy to ask if her prescription has come through from the gp, and they said it hadn't. I then called this medical centre to ask why my daughter's prescription had not been actioned and sent to the pharmacy since last week - Knowing she's been on same medication for several years and should not miss days? I was bluntly told by the reception to call back again,(of course, profile marking and syndicate operations in action.) I quickly reminded him how important her medication was, and he should please send it over to the pharmacy for collection. He said he was not in charge of that, and ended up pretending not to understand which medication was needed, (She's only on 1) and is in her profile. To cut the story short, I had no choice but to call 111 again. "Profile marking or spewed lies on the profile" was highly resonant in the voice at the end of the receiver too. I want to clearly state that these issues should be looked into by the right bodies in charge. People are being abused by those that should be providing care, and lives are lost due to these. (I nearly would have lost my life with this centre, cause i was refused care and gp appointment, and was bluntly told to do the worse I can not too long ago.) My daughter was refused duty of care, when she needed, and the excuse was, we had moved homes and was removed by the gp from their system- even when we had not yet registered with another gp. Where is the duty of care? What is the professionalism in this? This is gross misconduct and should be called out. And like I said in the beginning, Dr's are in consulting rooms doing their best and in very high cases are unaware of what goes on at the front desks, admins, and the rest. This types of evil must be called out and put away and far, please.

recent_reviews.author: DragosDM
recent_reviews.text: This is somehow a twilight zone practice, as it seems that it would be easier to contact the aliens on Mars than getting in touch with a receptionist here, not say a Doctor, who is like someone living in a black hole in a far, far away corner of the Universe. I am in urgent need of medication, following Covid-19 and hypertension problems that lead to a 187/123 readings of my blood pressure, and apparently only my registered GP practice can prescribe it, as following the laws in England. It was impossible even for doctors at A&E to contact them and today I rang for at least 30 times, starting at 08:00 a.m. without success. I am sorry to say it, but as time goes by, this seems to be a bad taste joke. It is not like we are having enough hardship in life due to Covid-19, we are all alone here and getting help from people designated to provide it is such a rare commodity. It is shameful and I am sure I'm not the only one in this position! Why don't you just admit failure and close the practice? At least leave the opportunity of helping people to others more willing to do so! I am totally, completely and utterly disappointed! It's a disgrace!

recent_reviews.author: Neville Gordon
recent_reviews.text: Your Feedback: Poor treatment from the practice. On Monday 12/3/24 I went to A and E with severe pain in my left hip due to arthritis. The doctor suggested because the pain is so severe I should consider naproxen I explained that I had diabetes and I’m aware it’s not recommended but I said I would discuss it with my GP. I contacted the practice and explained my delemma but was informed there were no appointments available and the 21 march was pencilled in. Mean while I attended the practice to ask for a repeat prescription of co-codamol because I had run out.Then in the early hours of 12/3/24 I called 111 and spoke to staff as I was in severe pain unfortunately no one got back to me until 1500 later that day, however earlier at 0800 I phoned the practice and asked for an emergency appointment, I explained my pain and the steps I had gone through. I was told my request for naproxen would be sent to the practice pharmacist and to ring later in the afternoon no appointment was offered. I called back in the afternoon and was told the pharmacist was on annual leave and the request had been sent to a doctor. Still with no pain medication or naproxen I contacted 111 again who were very helpful. This afternoon I was contacted by my chemist to say the medication was available. Meanwhile for the last 2 days I have been in sever pain with no medication or help from the practice at all. And later in the afternoon a doctor from the practice contacted me after a 111 request but by then thankfully I had my medication. I think your response to request for help was extremely poor and I can only thank the 111 system for their help.

recent_reviews.author: Saad farooqi
recent_reviews.text: ********Not recommended at all******* *** Disappointing Experience at Kingsway Medical Practice**** I recently had a very disappointing experience at Kingsway Medical Practice, and I feel compelled to share my thoughts and concerns. Firstly, the staff receptionist were incredibly rude and unhelpful. I approached them with a simple query, but instead of providing assistance, they seemed disinterested and dismissive. Their lack of professionalism was truly disheartening. Furthermore, it is important to note that Kingsway Medical Practice makes it nearly impossible to have a face-to-face consultation with a doctor. The receptionists consistently provide evasive answers and display an unhelpful tone of voice. Instead of prioritizing in-person appointments, they frequently push for telephonic consultations, which are far less effective in addressing medical concerns. This approach leaves patients feeling unheard and frustrated, as it seems like the practice is intentionally avoiding addressing the actual issues at hand. Moreover, the doctors themselves seemed rushed and uninterested in providing thorough care. During my appointments, I felt like I was being rushed through, with minimal attention given to my concerns. It is disheartening to see healthcare professionals who lack empathy and fail to prioritize patient well-being. Moreover, it is worth mentioning that it is nearly impossible to meet with a doctor face to face at Kingsway Medical Practice. The receptionists consistently provide runaround answers and have an unhelpful tone of voice. Instead of scheduling in-person consultations, they often opt for telephonic appointments, which are not as effective in addressing medical concerns. It feels as though they are intentionally avoiding addressing the actual issues at hand, leaving patients feeling unheard and frustrated. Overall, my experience at Kingsway Medical Practice was extremely disappointing. The unhelpful staff, long waiting times, lack of attentive care from doctors, and poor hygiene standards all contribute to a negative impression of this practice. I strongly urge others to consider alternative healthcare providers in order to receive the quality care they deserve. **********Not recommended at all****

recent_reviews.author: Meena Majid
recent_reviews.text: I contacted the surgery at 8.30am on 11th June to request further fitnote. The receptionist assured me she had put a request to the GP and when issued it would be emailed to me. At 14.00 hours I had not received the fitnote and contacted the surgery again to find out if the GP had issued the fitnote. I was advised by a different receptionist that she could not find my earlier request. She assured me she was going to send an urgent request for a fitnote to the GP. When I asked what time should I call back to find out if it had been issued, I was advised to ring after 16.30 hours. I still had not received the fitnote at 16.35 hours and contacted the surgery. I was advised by a different receptionist that the fitnote was waiting to be signed off. But she said we require one days notice. I told the receptionist, I wasn't aware of this and the 2 receptionists I spoke with earlier didn't tell me that. At 18.35 hours I still had not received my fitnote and contacted the surgery and was kept on the phone for 15 minutes before I disconnected my call. I am still waiting for the fitnote. There was no need for ANY of the receptionists to lie to me. All they had to say was....'sorry but we will not be putting a request to the GP for another fitnote'. The actions of these so called receptionists caused immense anxiety and reduced me to tears....No empathy, no sympathy, the surgery doesn't care what patients want. This will be going to the NHS as a complaint. Kingsway practice should shut the doors for good and go home because your service is a sambles!!

recent_reviews.text: Always waiting - WAIT to get the appointment because there are never any available so you have to WAIT til the next morning to try and get one at 9pm when new available slots are released. Then when you call, you can end up WAITing for nothing as the appointments go so quick. When I finally get an appointment, I have to wait to get checked in because the computer check in screen isn't working. Then on top of this I have to wait at least an hour for the doctor to see me, only to be rushed out half the time and advised to take medication that costs the NHS less to produce. Most the doctors just care about getting you in & out of their 10 minute slot so they don't get even later. Why they don't allocate longer time slots for appointments to reduce waiting times I do not know. "One problem per appointment" I've been told by a few doctors now. You'd think a doctor out of all professions would consider the possibility that all symptoms a patient has link together. But no, it's too much for them (Dr. Bowley in particular) to even skim read through the medical notes let alone consider all possibilities. If I have a test, I wait over 2 weeks for the results. I've had to chase them up with something that they should have sorted but I was tired of waiting. My advice would be to use another GP practise if you can. Your condition will probably get worse before you even get an appointment with this practise.

recent_reviews.author: Parnian yusra Haidery
recent_reviews.text: I’m writing this review after taking my 12-year-old brother to West Point Medical Centre to see Dr Mehra, and I’m extremely disappointed by how we were treated. Our dad is recovering from a heart attack, and our mum has serious mobility issues due to her knees — so I (as his 28-year-old sister) attended the appointment to support him. He was completely comfortable with me being there and explained our family situation clearly, but Dr Mehra refused to accept it. From the moment we arrived, he was cold and dismissive — no greeting, no kindness. He kept repeating that “the law” only allows parents to attend, even though in many situations, a responsible adult family member is acceptable if the child is willing and understands what’s going on. My brother is 12, mature, and wanted me there, but the doctor wouldn’t listen and made everything more stressful. He eventually treated my brother, but with a bad attitude — unfriendly, impatient, and completely lacking empathy. This is not how children especially ones already dealing with family stress should be treated by any doctor. I do not recommend Dr Mehra to anyone looking for respectful or compassionate care. If you want a GP who listens and understands, especially with young patients, I suggest booking with Matt Johnson — a great doctor and a true listener Follow-up to my review: Thank you for your response and for acknowledging my concerns. I fully understand and respect the need for medical professionals to follow guidelines, especially when it comes to treating minors. However my issue was never with the policy itself but with how the situation was handled by Dr Mehra on the day. If specific documentation or parental consent was required this could have been explained in a calm and respectful manner I would have been more than willing to provide what was needed even something as simple as a quick FaceTime call to our parents for verbal confirmation could have resolved the matter smoothly. Instead we were met with a cold dismissive attitude from the very beginning which added unnecessary stress for both me and my 12-year-old brother. I appreciate that Dr Mehra has many years of experience, and I do not question his clinical expertise. However, experience does not excuse a lack of empathy especially when dealing with a child already under emotional pressure due to family circumstances. How a situation is handled is just as important as the outcome, and in this case I truly believe it could have been managed with more understanding and compassion. I am someone who is calm and reasonable, and I would have appreciated a more human, considerate approach. That’s all we were asking for. Thank you again for your time 🙏

recent_reviews.author: Lisa J
recent_reviews.text: I've been a patient at Westpoint Medical for about 5 years, having moved into the area. I haven't really needed to see my GP until recently, following a cancer diagnosis. As a former GP practice manager, I understand exactly how practices operate and Westpoint seems very well run, organised, and efficient. In my experience, I have never had an issue when calling the practice - there has never been a long wait for my call to be answered and the reception staff I have dealt with have been lovely; really polite, professional & very helpful. I've quite often needed same-day access, be it for an impromptu prescription or needing to speak with a doctor, and a quick chat with reception has always resulted in my request being accommodated. My consults with the GPs have been mostly positive so far. I would recommend Westpoint Medical based on my experience to date.

Thank you West Point.

recent_reviews.author: Jeff Tipton
recent_reviews.text: My wife and I have been patients at West Point for over forty years, since we moved into the area. In all that time, we have been seen by by many doctors and medical staff. We can both honestly say that we have always felt fortunate to have a medical practice, not only on our doorstep, but one where we have felt valued, and have experienced a high quality level of care. We are well aware of the problems being suffered by the NHS, at this time, and these have brought about their own problems within the practice. However, every member of staff, both medical or clerical, always endeavour to try and meet patients needs for appointments and information which apply to their needs. We are both in our senior years but I have noticed that the whole spectrum of age groups are considered and catered for, to the highest of standards. We both have no hesitation in awarding West Point Medical Practice the highest of marks for the care that they provide to ourselves and the community in which we live.

recent_reviews.author: Raza Shah
recent_reviews.text: Update July 2023. Lots of improvements over the last year and easier access to appointment times. Things are starting to go back to the levels pre pandemic. Certain factors of backlogs in the NHS itself do affect some services but I'm pleased to say that I have had no problems in getting appointments for myself or my children lately, especially if you ring up at 8am. Well done to all the staff at West Point and hope to see more improvements in the future such as extra consultant rooms by using upstairs rooms and installing a lift, better air circulation in the basement and employing a few additional GPs Older post below. Updated review above . To blame Covid for not being able to ever get an appointment or see a doctor here is now the norm. Has gone from being a good surgery to the worst for patient care. What is the point if no one can ever get to see a doctor, yet when you visit it's always empty and yet on the phone they will tell you they are fully booked, over run and at breaking point. People in the community are dying, children are suffering and here they like to make excuses not to see anyone at all. It's time they learnt to live with COVID like the rest of the country and not hide behind closed doors . This is my local doctor's surgery. Have been a patient here since it opened over 20 years ago and now as a parent and a patient have suffered neglect of care from them for the past 2 years. Hope things can be turned around here and they can address the issues at hand and improve.

recent_reviews.text: I thankfully do not need to visit the doctors often. When I do need to it seems that you have to ring at 8am to try and get an "emergency" appointment. Otherwise you need to wait three or four weeks. I rang the surgery 3 weeks ago with an ear problem that concerned me. I was given an appoinment date of 15th of June even though I had lost a significant amount of hearing and didnt know if it was infection or something more serious. I explained this and was told to try for the "emergency" appointment. I couldnt get through on 2 consecutive days and I have to go to work ! I resigned myself to waiting for the appointment on the 15th June. Today, 8th June I have received a text message cancelling my appoinment due to unforseen circumstances. No explanation, no alternative appointment times. Disgraceful service and I have will now move from here.
