recent_reviews.author: Sally Bond
recent_reviews.text: I use this surgery regularly and find the team friendly and helpful. Sometimes I have to wait a little longer for my appointment but I would rather that and the doctor or nurse listen to my concerns about MY health than see a medic who is writing a prescription as I walk through the door. I like to discuss my health concerns and options as I think everyone should. Sometimes through discussion we can find solutions without medication and take some responsibility for our own health. In addition, if some people with minor ailments - who could self treat (ie colds and flu) or go to the pharmicist. - did not take up GP time it would leave more time for other patients. The NHS has limited resources and we ALL need to use it responsibly and understand that it is under pressure and treat ALL the staff with courtesy and respect. If you are not happy go elsewhere or pay for your healthcare.

recent_reviews.author: Mery Nt
recent_reviews.text: I think this GP clinic does have space for improvement. Negatives: - Bad first impressions: Unfortunately, not the best impression when you first communicate with the staff about an appointment. Either due to long delay before answering the phone or low interest in helping. - Bad book appointment system: You also get the option to book online but it is limited to time between 8-9am and there are too many steps until getting to book the appointment. - Location: it is not the easiest location to park or to get too due to the business of the roads etc (not the practice fault), but need to plan ahead of time before getting there. Positives: - I do think that if they start improving on their phone communication that will massively change the impression of the practice. - Doctors: they are excellent and super helpful once you get to to discuss with them your issue. Super attentive to detail and look after all areas of concern. - Environment: Overall pretty clean and the reception staff are nice when you ask for help. - Check in: easy check in system on arrival.

recent_reviews.author: Helen Jones
recent_reviews.text: This review is for Dr. Ben Addelstone, my adult daughter has been under his care for just over eighteen months. When we first came my girl was in a dreadful state and really needed someone to listen to her and help her get a diagnosis. Dr Addelstone was fantastic, he was kind, and got on the case with referrals straight away, made us feel heard and important! Later when her mental health started to take its toll he was open and proactive. We now have a diagnosis and financial support, and without his dedication she would not be in as good a condition as she is today. Even tho she’s not better yet, he’s helped her to have a better quality of life. As a parent who doesn’t live in the same city I am so grateful for his time, understanding and professionalism. This is a doctor who makes people’s lives better. Thank you so much.

recent_reviews.author: Alice Girling
recent_reviews.text: UPDATE regarding potentially the rudest receptionist I've ever come across! I asked for a fit to work statement and they tried to charge me £20, which is completely and totally illegal (ask the DWP). I am seriously considering taking this further as people like her shouldn't work with vulnerable people. Magically, after being forced to become irate with her, she miraculously managed to book me in next day, after being completely adament they're full up for a month! I later rang to find out her name (Bethan) and she was possibly the single most sarcastic, demeaning and patronising person I have ever had the displeasure of speaking to. I will be following this up with further, private authorities. If you're reading this, Bethan, look into a new career path, perhaps in a warehouse where you don't have to interact with potentially difficult public. I am fortunate in that my mental illness is manageable (with correct help), but for anyone else that phonecall could have been the end of their lives. Other people are iller than myself and it is simply not acceptable to treat them this way. I would get sacked on the spot if i was to speak to anyone the way Bethan spoke to me, and rightly so, and I work in a cafe! Walking into the reception to pick up a registration form, the elderly lady at the left-hand-side desk was extremely rude. She didn't say a word and silently pointed to another desk where nobody was. Turns out the entire reception team was on a lunch break (why they need to take their breaks together I have no idea) and we had to wait 15 minutes to even get a form, regardless of the fact the woman on the other side was sitting there with a face like thunder doing absolutely nothing. Okay so first impressions aside, I needed to make an appointment this week for a doctor to sign a form (urgent for me). Called on Monday, after 20 minutes of 'line busy', a rude lady answered and told us we can't have an appointment because it's 'triage day' on Mondays and Tuesdays. So we protested, and she said she'd get the doctor to call. Obviously, the doctor never called. So we waited until today (Wednesday) to phone up, which was the absolute last day I could get this form signed. Again, 20 minutes of 'line busy' (how about you get more than one phone line? You have enough receptionists sitting around), and another rude lady answered and said the same thing again - it's not urgent (in her 'professional' opinion) and therefore we can't have an appointment until next week. I also have medication that I need to see a doctor to get, and I have now been cold turkey for a month thanks to this practice. It's a repeat prescription, but since they appear to have their own rules, I have to make appointments which, again, takes around a month minimum. How anyone goes about getting seen by a doctor here is anyone's guess. It seems like they only have receptionists and they're all trained to get rid of people. I've seen people saying they're racist, but I wouldn't go there (though there's no smoke without fire). I think they just hate people of all races. I should note, I have worked with the public for 16 years now and have never once even thought about speaking to a customer the way Bethan spoke to me. You may have nasty notes about me on your computer system, and you're welcome to do that, but be a little more professional in your actual interactions with the general public, and realise that people who call the doctors need help, not beration.

recent_reviews.author: Julia
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this surgery for 10 years now, although over the past 2-4 years I have been more of a frequent patient. Very much hit and miss experience. They've lost a few samples which I had to re-do and told me I have been booked in and on the day I call to say nobody called me, the appointment was not on the system. So now, naturally I double check everything from appointments to requests being fulfilled. (even if this means being on hold for 30 mins for a 1 minute question/query) I have had 2 negative experiences so far with DR but I believe it may be the same one. recent_reviews.text: Dreadful. Had a prescription cancelled on a random date with no warning or confirmation sent through to me. The pharmacy weren't informed when I re-orderd it, so after 3 days of not having the prescription sent through they called the surgery, to be told I needed to ring the surgery directly. There were no notes on the system as it to why it had been cancelled, and they couldn't see any reason why this would happen, but as the doctor who cancelled it was on leave for three weeks, nothing could be done. In order to get it sorted, I needed to book an appointment. As others have said, this process is also dreadful. Eventually, another Doctor signed it off (apparently). Went to pick it up at the pharmacy, no prescription. Called the surgery, it hadn't been put through. No notes on the record to indicate why, no doctor available to confirm anything. You can only blame COVID/NHS funding n so far, I'm fairly sure this is just down to all round incompetence from Al lstaff involved.

recent_reviews.text: I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the treatment my wife and I received at the reception of our GP surgery on Friday. We arrived for a scheduled appointment, only to be met by a receptionist (Blonde, mid 50's) who informed us quite abruptly and without courtesy-that the appointment had been cancelled and that we should have received a text message. We never received such a message. What was most troubling was the lack of empathy or willingness to help. The receptionist showed no interest in understanding my wife's medical issue or in offering any alternative or support. Her attitude was dismissive and unprofessional, simply telling us the appointment was cancelled and leaving us to figure things out on our own. Today, we attempted to book another appointment via the Patch app. After not receiving any follow-up, we called the GP. Unfortunately, we were again met by the same receptionist, who claimed there was no record of our request and abruptly hung up the phone before we could explain further. This level of service is unacceptable, especially in a healthcare setting where compassion and patience are essential. I strongly believe this individual is not suited for a front-facing role that requires daily interaction with patients. It is deeply disappointing to encounter such behaviour in a place meant to provide care and support.

recent_reviews.author: Steve D
recent_reviews.text: As always, my sincere thanks to ALL the staff at Barlow Med Centre for all they continue to do, but a special mention has to be for Carol, Sue, Pam, Uma, Doc Allcock and of course, Doc J for all the amazing care and support you have all given me over the last 8 years!! This isnt a book i promise, long read maybe but gives you a better understanding of why Barlow Med Centre is THE best med centre. Grab a cuppa and have a read. Without the genuine compassion, care, support, help and understanding of the amazing reception staff and Doc J, I wouldnt be writing this review. The reception staff front and rear have and continue to go above and beyond to help every individual and myself who walks in with the upmost consideration and wont ever fob you off and will do all they can to help. Those who say otherwise are on another planet and are clearly Harpic! (Clean round the bend) Im ex military and knew i needed help, i was too proud to say i needed help but in the end i did and explaining who i was and my background they reassured me and gave me that support and confidence to open up, who truly cared and understood my issues. All the staff bent over backwards and go tbat extra mile to help me. No issue is too big and they will help. To this day they all know me and continue to go the extra mile no matter what and for that i am truly grateful. Thankyou all so much Doc Jeffery is my GP and without a doubt the best Doc ive ever had. His ability to reasure, help, guide who will go out of his way to get you sorted. His bedside manner and feeling of ease has helped me open up and with that he has gone above and beyond to get my mental health and ptsd under control and he shows his emotions to your particular issues. Im not being a bum kisser but Doc J is that doctor who cares deeply. His reasuring and handling of all my issues he truly understands. I can honeslty say id be in a grave if it wasnt for his knowledge of what i needed and never once fobbed me of.. he listens, he understands and he wants to help. I class the Doc and receptionists at Barlow Med Centre as family and can call them anytime. They are there to help. Thankyou or a box of chocs go along way and its the small things like that which make a huge difference. If you are looking for a med centre I 100 percent recommend Barlow Med Centre. Id run naked down the high street if you found a better surgery in the local and surrounding areas. I cant say thankyou to them all as they truly and unknowingly saved my life. Dont suffer in silence, all the staff want to help amd will help. Ive finished my review now and bet your glad. Hope I didnt bore you. If it did then my name is Charles Dickens!! SDA 2411

recent_reviews.author: Joe Thurston-Harris
recent_reviews.text: Appointments can only be made online through a system called PATCHS, which is only available between 7-10am. We attempted to book an appointment today at 7:10, and the system was still unavailable, so you can't even rely on the very limited stated operating hours. This contradicts what is said on the NHS website for this GP practice - it claims that appointments can be made by calling. When we did call on a Friday we were told dispassionately to use the online system on Monday. PATCHS itself is an awful AI based system that asks you inane questions about your issue before allowing you to make an appointment - "is there anything you're particularly worried about with this symptom" making you repeat the same obvious information. The experience of this insensitive health AI is very distressing when you have genuine health concerns. The AI will then encourage you to contact 111, and ask you to submit feedback on your booking experience. There's no reason to put this limit on appointment booking. Technology is supposed to make life better, rather than make medical care awkward and difficult to access for all. Computer systems can (in theory) be online 24 hours a day. We are not being treated like human beings. I'd suggest going in person and being very insistent, although I've not tried this yet

recent_reviews.author: Susan Dobson
recent_reviews.text: Let me say first of all the clinicians here are probably the best you’ll find anywhere. But the huge paraphernalia that exists between patient and clinician has probably been worse than the anxiety I suffered to prompt me to seek medical advice in the first place. Firstly, the reception team are woefully understaffed. If you are unlucky enough to endure the 1.45 minutes of totally superfluous introductory message about how you can get all this fab information on the fab new look website (and then laboriously go into detail about said info instead of saying we’re on line go to the website deal with it and if you don’t get the help you need ring us back) and THEN don’t get through to a receptionist, be prepared to listen to this for 11 TIMES or so before you get anyone to pick up. I have cleaned the whole house some days with my phone on loudspeaker by the time I’ve got a response. If you are really unlucky and ask them if they’ve requested a script from a clinician and they haven’t done it, be prepared to be hanging on the line (or outside the door in the pouring rain , as I have sometimes had to do because as you can probably guess, this is a common occurrence) don’t expect an admission that actually no, they didn’t actually action the request, or God forbid offered an apology but that it will be done straight away OK? And then when you’re sent packing across to LLoyds Pharmacy next door, where you’re wondering how can they still be in business, despite the fact that there is zero customer service and you are eyed by every one of those white-coated assassins as some evil threat, they answer dead-eyed that nah , we haven’t got the prescription through and would you go away cos I’m on lunch now and then you trot back to the surgery door, dying inside while some Priti Patel like quasi empress approaches the door with barely concealed contempt at your daring to question the information she’s just given you. I have anxiety and depression and I am dependant on strong painkillers because of a hip condition and awaiting surgery.. if I don’t get these meds I can go into unpleasant withdrawal symptoms. Despite the fact that these ostensibly knowledgeable people are aware of this both the surgery and the pharmacy behave in such a way that they have merely withdrawn your daily chocolate ration. This has happened to me with depressing regularity and I am preparing to dispossess myself of the twin evils of Lloyd’s Pharmacy and Barlow Medical Centre but not before I have literally been reduced to tears at reception by their passive aggressive and unhelpful demeanour . Sorry Doctors, Nurses all you’re great but your practice absolutely sucks. Oh and by the way, if you’re wondering why I’ve left this review instead of submitting a formal complaint to the practice, guess what?! You can’t

recent_reviews.author: Dave Jones
recent_reviews.text: Contrary to several other reviewers, as a long time user of the practice I feel compelled to stand up for the telephone callback service which I've had no problems with. Sure, it's not quite as personal as it used to be, but it still guarantees same-day access to medical staff. A further upside is that it avoids overwhelming the waiting room with a heaving mass of potentially infectious patients first thing in the morning (a not uncommon sight prior to the phone service's introduction), instead spreading out the appointments of those that need to be seen over the day. In several cases, I've even been prescribed medication without needing to be seen at all, which naturally frees up a bit of the staff's time for seeing those that really require an exam or consultation. Yes, it's fairly obvious the NHS is struggling under the load, but I've been very impressed with Barlow Med's response to the times. The staff have always been professional and polite, in my experience, and the practice is clean and accessible. The adjacent pharmacy is convenient and, although the recent switch to electronic prescriptions seems to be causing some headaches, a pharmacist friend assures me that's a common complaint - not specific to this pharmacy. Hopefully, training will smooth out the issues there in the coming year. Overall, when I compare my experience at Barlow Med to friends and family who are registered at other practices in the area, I'm very happy with the service.

They are a family based business and neglected my care and gave me the cheapest medication possible to save up and put the remaining into their pockets. Instead of B12 injections and blood infusions which i’ve always desperately needed they only ever gave iron tables and made me feel like it’s already so much that they’re doing. It’s only when I ended up in A&E and got these things that I realised how bad they’ve been with me. Turns out I should have had it after every child i’ve had and not silenced with just iron tablets . To this day they didn’t investigate why I have anaemia in the first place which my recent dr is shocked they never did. Thanks to this lifelong anaemia I now have a serious heart condition. This is your job!! You’re supposed to know what I need not have me as the patient tell you or resort to A&E when it’s your job! This is a huge problem with family owned businesses and yes this is family based. First dr Mohammed the father and now the daughter. Please avoid them and if you can’t avoid then just use their locum which I resorted to until I moved.

recent_reviews.author: chrisby53
recent_reviews.text: I was highly impressed. I first registered and was told it would take 2 days to process. After 2 days I called the reception to see if I could get an urgent appointment to renew my prescription. I was given an appointment for the following morning at 10am. I was warmly greeted by reception. I was then called into room one where I met Dr Zeenat. She was so very pleasant and helped me with a prescription for my meds. As I am 66 she also offered me the flu and pneumonia vaccinations on the spot. Dr Zeenat was really lovely and I will not hesitate recommending the Al-Shifa Medical Centre. There is also an amazing pharmacy right next door called Withington Pharmacy. As I am invalid, I found access to both the Medical Centre and Pharmacy was amazing too. Plenty of handrails.

recent_reviews.author: Qamar Mahmood (Mahmood)
recent_reviews.text: I had an appointment scheduled for 11:20 AM today. By 12:10 PM, I was still waiting and had not been seen, meaning I waited for around 50 minutes before having to leave again without being seen. This is not the first time this has happened. I had an appointment with Dr Hamilton yesterday as well, where I was kept waiting for nearly one hour and was not seen on that occasion either. On both days, I had to take time off work specifically to attend these appointments, and on both occasions I ended up leaving after waiting for almost an hour. Over two days, this has resulted in unnecessary loss of work time and significant inconvenience. I understand that delays can occur, but repeated long waiting times without being seen or properly informed is unacceptable. Better appointment management and communication are clearly needed. I hope this feedback is taken seriously so that patients do not have to repeatedly take time off work only to leave without receiving care.

recent_reviews.author: Meg
recent_reviews.text: I would like to take a moment to show my appreciation for Aneka on reception. At a previous practice I was at I had awful experiences with the reception team, they were so rude and dismissive during a time where I was highly vulnerable and unwell. This has led to me developing a strong anxiety when visiting a GP practice. While I was sat in the waiting area, silently stressing, a lady came in who was clearly distressed and in pain. I could clearly hear her interaction with Aneka. Aneka treating this woman which such kindness and compassion. She spoke to her with respect and patience. she didn't belittle her in any way. As I'm sure everyone knows, the waiting area of a practice is hardly a private place, and I have been made to speak about private matters where other people can hear, Aneka didn't push the lady to explain or justify her reason for being there. Aneka is a credit to the team at Ladybarn and a gold standard for others to follow.

recent_reviews.author: Jason
recent_reviews.text: I cannot praise the staff at this surgery enough! I feel Ladybarn Group Practice strives to offer the best possible service to its patients in very difficult times. The introduction of more modern working practices and innovations is praise worthy. Furthermore, I feel the reception staff always go above and beyond to be helpful and accommodating- even though they are under immense pressure every day. The same is true of the Drs. This year, I have been in very impressed by two experiences. Firstly, my annual medication review with Mrs Forkan Shareet Practice Pharmacist. Not only was Forkan very knowledgeable and helpful, but my review saved valuable Drs’ time to see patients in real need. Secondly, I referred myself to Sue Cunningham Practice Physiotherapist with extreme knee and hip pain. Again freeing up the Drs’ time. After a thorougher initial consultation, I was referred to Withington Community Hospital for an X-ray. Thankfully, the problem was not caused by arthritis and Sue has been able to give me an exercise programme to follow. Already, l can see improvement. Many thanks to all at LadybarnGroups Practice!

recent_reviews.author: Sarah
recent_reviews.text: I’ve been tapering off antidepressants after 13 years, and Megan, the pharmacist at my GP surgery, supported me through every step. Over the four to five months it took, she called regularly to check in—especially important given my previous difficulties coming off this medication. Megan was always kind, patient, and genuinely caring. Just knowing I had her support made a huge difference, and I felt safe and heard throughout. I’ve had poor experiences with mental health support in the past at other surgeries, but Megan was and is truly exceptional. She never made me feel like a burden and went out of her way to stay in touch, even when I was hard to reach. Her dedication and compassion meant so much. I won’t forget it - Thank you.

recent_reviews.text: Mrs Forkan shareef the pharmacist, made me feel comfortable as soon as I entered the room, She explained to me why I was having a review of my medication and asked how I was doing with them and If I had any concerns, I explained that I was getting a lot of swelling in my legs. She looked through my medication and changed my blood pressure tablets to see if this would improve and rebooked me in for a follow up appointment in a couple of months. I felt that I wasn’t rushed like when seeing a doctor she had more time to listened to my concerns, she was very thorough and even took my blood pressure reading. She also booked me in for blood test. She also rang me up to see if I could come in to discuss the blood test results, which since I have been and will be happy to continue seeing Mrs Forkan to discuss non emergency appointment instead of a doctor as I wouldn’t feel guilty.

recent_reviews.author: Sharon Davis
recent_reviews.text: Updated 2025 review I don't understand the low ratings. Both today and the last time I filled in a medical request form I was called and assisted same day. This time with a very helpful telephone call and last time I was invited in for a f2f consultation same day. If you explain your issue in detail then they help you straight away. Also I've learned that it is very rare to get the bi-annual full check up (health MOTs!) offered by Ladybarn. The GPs at the practice said they don't get that service from their own home GP surgeries. Cannot recommend highly enough. 2023 Try to book online if you can because you'll wait an age by phone, I've been 'caller number one' in the queue for the last 20mins trying to make a routine health check which they texted me about. Shame you can't book appointments with HC assistants as well as GPs online. Once you're there the doctors and assistants are on the whole friendly, empathetic and knowledgeable. They are almost always running behind, think they book their appointments too short or too close together. They offer free regular human MOT healthchecks (bloods, blood pressure, various other tests) which is a brilliant service not provided by most surgeries and reassures you that your cholesterol and other things to watch are under scrutiny

recent_reviews.author: Diane Paul
recent_reviews.text: Deciding to change clinics recently, I had several recommendations for Ladybarn Group Practice and one doctor in particular. This is a very welcoming surgery with open plan spacing and clean so I was delighted to become the patient of Dr Kate Poole, who is the most delightful and empathic doctor I have ever met. I have white coat syndrome but it isn’t showing up any more as Dr Poole listens to me when I speak, is not at all patronising and treats me like a human. No longer do I dread going to the doctor to be patronised or sidelined by a negative test result. She has made me welcome from day one, makes her own appointments for me ahead, with necessary tests. She is very knowledgeable and gives me the impression that she genuinely feels for her patients and doesn’t regard them as inanimate objects. I am very happy with the situation and think I have made the correct choice. The receptionists are very welcoming and helpful too and so in my turn, I can recommend this practice wholeheartedly.

recent_reviews.author: Victor Ashiedu
recent_reviews.text: I had an issue that made my life miserable for years. When I met Dr Ruby Basson, she listened to me and told me what she thought was wrong with me. Then, she asked me a question that I do not believe any GP has asked me before - "what do you think will help you recover." I told her and based on that she offered me options for two medications and explained why she was leaning towards a specific one. Based on her explanations, I agreed that the medication appears to be the best option for my situation. After that, Dr Basson carefully explained the side effects to me. This turned out to be very helpful because when I started on the medication, I experienced those side effects - which were horrible. However, because she already told me that I may experience those side-effects and that they will eventually ease off, I was able to hang on and eventually the side effects cleared and I GOT MY LIFE BACK. I have not felt this good in 3 years. A big thank you to Dr Basson and everyone at Ladybarn Group practice.

recent_reviews.author: heidi holt
recent_reviews.text: I sent a request to my GP surgery to speak to a GP. I was called by a Dr Adams within half an hour, to tell me he had arranged an appointment for that morning, it was a half hour appointment. Such time slots are unusual but I did have a lot of things I needed to talk about so appreciate the time I was given. During my visit the time I spent with the doctor to give her a full picture was important because I could not have shared everything in a 10 minute appointment and she would only have got snippets of my health. Dr Jessica Walsh listened to me without judgement and showed me nothing but kindness and understanding of my situation. She has arranged for numerous tests to be done, I’m so lucky to have walked in to her room yesterday. I love the online booking system and would never go back to ringing the surgery for an appointment. It’s just much easier and far less stressful. If you haven’t already tried it, you should.

recent_reviews.author: Mo H
recent_reviews.text: My experience with the Ladybarn Practice Group was great despite the sad ending. It started when my elderly father, who passed away suffered from Mesothelioma, asbestos cancer. We went to the gp to look in respiratory problem and a lump in his groin. The appointment was with Dr. James Anderson. With his great experience and vision beyond the scene, he suspected it was a cancer even before the tests were done. He discussed the issue with us and made very quick referral to the hospital for the necessary procedures, then after to be confirmed It was cancer. Another doctor from the gp involved in my father's case, Dr. Emma Barnsley, who showed ultimate compassion and care even outside of her working hours and in her days off. she made frequent visits to the house and made sure to provide everything necessary for my father's comfort and was so helpful and professional in her medical plans at every step of disease development, and to set all the legal documents. Will never forget how the doctors were always supportive, passionate to help, and beyond the call of the duty till the last moment of my dad's life. Now, with my family we still have the best treatment options. The new Team Hub system which had put in place recently is wonderful and makes it so easy to access same day appointment in emergencies. Many thanks and gratitude.

recent_reviews.author: Dannielle Hooper
recent_reviews.text: Actually came with my son who was seen and prescribed antibiotics within 1hr of me requesting an appointment online for him. Whilst there the GP (Dr Pigney) thought I looked very unwell myself and arranged for one of the nurses to squeeze me in to take a blood test before we left. I suffer with extremely low iron & sometimes need blood transfusions as it gets so low. I am awaiting my results and I am 100% positive they will be acted on urgently & should my levels be low again i’ll be receiving replacement therapy asap. Cannot fault Dr Pigney, the Nurse or the reception desk staff. Edit: Dr Pigney contacted me quickly after receiving my results & arranged for me to go to a special clinic at Wythenshawe Hospital where I received an iron infusion and 2 units of blood, attending at 10am and home by 7:30pm. Can’t ask for better care.

recent_reviews.author: laura holland
recent_reviews.text: I tried the new online appointment system for the first time - it was not the improvement in communication I had hoped for - I was finally able to access it today - at my 3rd attempt having tried on the two previous days. When the new system was first announced - I thought it would make access easier - to some extent it does - the form enabled me to give all the information I needed to tell the surgery - and I was VERY impressed when I received a call within a very short space of time I was given a face to face appointment for the same day - I saw a GP who explained how my issue could be dealt with gave me some easy to understand advice. 10 out of 10 for today - I always find once I’ve got through to the surgery they are very helpful ! I know they are very busy and the telephone issues are out of their control but as much as I like the new online system I don’t think it’s a solution - it is only available for a short time each day I understand some of the reasoning behind this, but I’d like to know if this limitation will change going forward - but for me today - it worked well.

recent_reviews.author: A D
recent_reviews.text: I have had a lot of communications with the surgery over the last few years. Whilst I am upset with the NHS system as a whole, primarily due to the underfunding and continued privatization by the Tories, the people within this doctor's surgery truly seem to be doing their best despite those constraints, which are out of their control. The ladies on reception are fantastic to talk with and to deal with. Courteous, helpful, understanding, friendly and professional. A great mix to have. My personal favourite is Lesley, whose attitude and character lights up the world when she answers the telephone. What a lovely, helpful and fantastic person. My utmost gratitude to everyone at the surgery. Thank you very much. Andrew

recent_reviews.text: Myself and my husband have been with this practice since 1980. It was the old practice on Mauldeth road. We have seen many changes mainly the move to Briarfield Road. We have seen Dr's come and go. Never in all that time have we had a problem. We feel we have been well cared for by staff and GPs. When Dr Walkley left the practice, my husband was moved over to Dr Anderson who has and still does look after him very well. When Dr Helen Burgess retired, i was also moved over to Dr Anderson. My first appointment was a phone call. I/we find him very informative, patient and understanding. He listens and puts you at ease. We would recommend this practice by our own experiences.

recent_reviews.author: VN83
recent_reviews.text: Avoid this Doctors Surgery at all cost! The management team of this place are a complete joke. The receptionists are completely above their station. You would think they were the actual medical professionals you were trying ( and I mean trying ) to get an appointment with, with their rude and condescending attitudes towards patients. The only bright side to this Surgery is that one or two of the Doctor’s here are lovely (when you can actually get an appointment) Dr McCaffrey, Dr Barnsley, Dr Pigney and Dr Murray-Brown are all lovely. The Nurses have always been great. The major problem with the surgery is the unprofessional, rude, arrogant, disrespectful down right disgusting stuck up attitude of one DR JAMES ANDERSON. My family have had nothing but problem after problem with this Doctor. We have all made several complaints about him with nothing but completely hollow un-sincere apologies back from Ladybarn Group Practice Management. We are now taking this to the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman (PHSO) I would imagine this is a completely futile process to undertake as nothing will undoubtedly happen with regards to this awful GP but we shall go through the process anyhow. Thank you for reading my review and hope it helps anyone looking for a GP’s Practice locally in the South Manchester Burnage/Withington area.

recent_reviews.author: hywel Evans
recent_reviews.text: A great team working hard in tough times, Dr Adam’s Strump has been my doctor for years there and he, along with other the doctors occasionally seen, have helped me through some very difficult times. Patient and kind, professional and extremely good at his job, he has been instrumental in me being able to tackle a dark period in my life. In terms of booking: yes it has been tough. Their new online(app) booking service has changed things immeasurably for the better in terms of getting appointments. It used to be incredibly difficult and stressful to wait on the phone at 8am for hours, the phone system is long and Addison’s, however, their recent changes mean that if you use your nhs app, and check regularly (as new appointments are released throughout the week) it is an easy click, albeit still part of a busy nhs. Support and believe firmly in your nhs and the people working so hard!

recent_reviews.author: Gavin Manchester
recent_reviews.text: Unwilling to make reasonable adjustments (due to learning disability) despite the Equality Act 2010 and The Autism Act 2009. Not a suitable surgery for neurodivergent adults (ADHD/autism) with long term lifelong mental health conditions or/and learning disability, not unless you have a parent/family friend to speak on your behalf, book and accompany you to appointments. Admin staff not understanding or particularly helpful and hold grudges/make assumptions, no training in autism/learning disability. (Even if the patient is on the NHS Learning Disability Register). On one occasion I had a local authority social worker attend an appointment with me as an advocate and to see the challenges I face accessing lawful care. Complain or raise concerns and get told “go elsewhere”. Not a particularly modern thinking practice. Very much the “you don’t look autistic” attitude and “go for a long walk outdoors” when facing a serious MH relapse/crisis. Seem to have the attitude that anything mental health related means you must see the CMHT only and if not under psychiatric care they won’t help you. They don’t feel the need to update medical records despite communication from medical consultants. No excuse for treating vulnerable patients so ineffectually or cruelly.

recent_reviews.text: I needed a same-day appointment but the open surgery was full, so I got redirected to another surgery for an appointment the next day. This was great. I had to leave a swab test for testing with my practice though. The doctor from the other surgery said I’d get the results back in 2 working days. I still haven’t gotten them back (6 working days and counting). I needed to be seen again rather urgently for the same unresolved issue, so I tried setting up a same-day appointment. It is practically impossible to get one. I called at 8.30 (on the spine) on two different days and was told that all receptionists were busy with other calls, so my calls were terminated. This happened 3 times each of the days. On the second day, I was able to get on their 10-caller hold line, being 9th in the queue. I moved up the queue to number 2 when my call was terminated. When I called again, there were no more appointments for the day. The first day I was told there were no more open surgery appointments for the day right away. The telephone booking system is terrible and dated. Will be switching to a different surgery.

recent_reviews.author: Theo Eze
recent_reviews.text: this place needs a 0 star option. I know it's hard to get placements at GP's but for your own sake avoid this place like the plague. I've been dealing with an illness for the past few years, and Corkland road surgery, more specifically it's reception staff have only ever made things ten times worse. They lose prescriptions. They forget to hand in prescriptions. They tell you they've done things that they haven't and then pass the blame on to other members of staff that aren't in on the day that you speak to them. usually I'd feel bad about condemning an entire practice and it's staff, but over the last few years I've dealt with all of them and I'm not exaggerating when i say that every one of the rotating cast of women on reception is rude, dismissive, and completely inept. They can't carry out the most basic of tasks, and they couldn't care less that the people they're serving come to them often in times of desperation and experiencing pain. Maybe it's a bit idealistic to expect everyone who works for the NHS to actually care about patients (and thankfully I've had experiences at other practices that prove this wrong), but you would hope that they'd at least pretend to care as that's what they're paid to do. i've had to complain about them multiple times in the past already but nothing changes, they keep their jobs and they keep making vulnerable people's lives harder. But it gets worse. When you're at your lowest and simply want to get hold of prescriptions you handed in ages ago, that they "forgot to put through" and you go in to see them in person, be prepared for all four of the girls on reception to laugh in your face. I would name and shame as it's gotten to the point where I've had to take most of their names but honestly they're all as bad as each other. This isn't only the worst GP that I've ever experienced, it's the worst service i've ever experienced bar none. the only silver lining is that I only have to look after myself. God forbid that you leave the care of your children or vulnerable loved ones in the hands of these people.

recent_reviews.author: john Geary
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at this practice for a number of years , unfortunately I have to say over the last 12mths the service and professionalism has significantly deteriorated. it is almost impossible to obtain an appointment with out 3 weeks notice if you work in a job where you can not take time off for a GP appointment and have to arrange in your own time . The reception managers attitude to this problem appears to be that its the patients problem and you should take the time off work to fit in with them. . for many years I have been prescribed medications to cover 2 or 3 months supply. However, now I can only get 1 months supply at a time this means I am now paying between £400 and £500 per year extra for prescriptions. Today I have been informed from another GP that I could buy a pre payment certificate for £104 per year that covers all my medications. ??? There is no information available in the surgery about this. Why have they not informed me ?? I believe we need to increase NHS funding and I have no issues with an increase in taxation to help with this as then we all pay more for the fantastic service the NHS provides .but this practice does not seem to want to help its patients and provides a very poor service . That said the girls on reception are excellent in tough circumstances and poor management

The second nurse didn't take enough bloods for all the tests needed. So am obviously going to have to return again for the correct tests to be done. Very disappointing.

recent_reviews.author: Rose Carbone
recent_reviews.text: Dr Atherton was absolutely great - as always - however it’s the whole booking/reception where there seems to be difficulty & errors - this last apptmt was at least the 3rd time where I’d been given incorrect information. This time it was an error in phone apptmt/face to face apptmt. Id been told it was a phone apptmt - whereas in fact it was supposed to be a face to face one - so I was waiting by the phone at home & no call came. One before I’d been given the wrong month info - so when I turned up at the surgery - my date & time was right but for the wrong month. Prior to that I’d been given a date and time but just before the booked apptmt I received a message from the surgery to tell me I couldn't actually have that apptmt as it had been booked in incorrectly & had been given an ‘emergency’ slot as opposed to routine - I had booked it 3 wks in advance - so then had to wait a further 3/4 weeks to finally speak to a doctor. Like I said when you do manage to speak with a doctor/nurse at the Practice they are brilliant - however some of the booking/reception team do let it down & it becomes very frustrating - especially if you are concerned about an issue. There were further errors - in a similar area but I have bored myself with this already - I’m only writing this because I was asked to & also hope that it can lead to an improvement in the booking system.

recent_reviews.author: Stephen Pumfrey
recent_reviews.text: I have been registered with this practice for over 20 years, and it has evolved and expanded. I am currently very satisfied with the care it provides. It has improved in recent years in two ways. First, online contact, via its website and the PATCHS system, has transformed my ability to get timely appointments, responses to queries and the general level of communication. Secondly, it seems that staff changes to the running of the reception desk and administration have improved efficiency and approachability. The latter was necessary. I know from my own experience and that of others that in the past it had led to mistakes, frustration and even to people transferring from the practice. As a result I am happy to recommend it strongly. One does not always get face-to-face appointments, consultations with GPs as opposed to other medical professionals, and not routinely with the same GP. This does not unduly bother me, although a return to seeing the same GP who knows my history would be welcome. The online contact is good and developing. However, I have found it difficult, both via PATCHS and the website, to navigate to the relevant page if I am looking to make a non-urgent enquiry rather than an urgent appointment. I expect there will be further improvements.

recent_reviews.author: Elaine Smith
recent_reviews.text: I have tried to make an appointment for my sons which is a follow up and the requirement for a follow-up is stated in their medical notes. I went into the practice on 28th Nov 2025 spoke to the receptionist and explained why I required the appointment. The receptionist was disinterested and unhelpful. I explained I required the appointment ‘not within school hours’. She could only offer me a 2.10pm appointment on 11th Dec and told me I had to use the booking system Patches for a more suitable time or phone!!!!!!! I explained that when I’ve phoned previously the waiting queues could be as high as 30 patients before me! Due to another patient in reception speaking to the other receptionist at the desk and the glass barrier it was difficult to hear and there is no confidentiality. The receptionist could see it written in the record of the set of notes she opened that an appointment was required but repeated she couldn’t help. When my husband returned home we put the request in on Patches on 28th November 2025 ( before Patches closing time!). A text came to make an appointment for one son but not the other. Patches only offered 2.10pm which means taking the one offered the appointment out of school on 4th December! No other appointments available on Patches til 15th December- which is too late. The system and practice is not patient centred. Parents work like myself! Education is the foundation of child development and yet no importance is placed on it. We are completely dissatisfied with the practice and Patches. The fundamentals have been lost, disregarded and de- personalised.

Since enquiries went online I have stuck to the system always and then on the one occasion I need a bit of help because I am unwell and my dad has been in and out of hospital for a fortnight, I’m still told to fill an online form in the morning. it is an absolute joke.

recent_reviews.author: Rebecca B
recent_reviews.text: I was shocked to learn that the only real way to get an appointment here is to show up at the surgery in person before 8am and wait in a long queue to try and get an appointment before they are all gone. This is just to get a telephone consultation with a doctor. I have waited 45 minutes on the phone to speak to someone before and I heard the receptionist advising people that the only way to get an appointment is to come first thing in the morning, so this is obviously an accepted practice. I’ve seen disabled people and older people struggling to wait in such a long queue (up to 30 mins) because of the time they have to spend standing, and it’s also dangerous to have such a large number of potentially infectious people gathered in a small space that’s meant to be a waiting area, when they could have just called. A really poorly managed practice.

recent_reviews.author: Plussize Hansi
recent_reviews.text: Unfortunately, the government has changed the way people can make appointments in centres like this one. So it means that you can ring up to 42 times or more (because the line is busy) before you get through to a receptionist. By that time all the appointments for the day have been taken and they do not do advanced bookings. Not only that, it is very frustrating when the receptionists ask what is wrong with you/what you need an appointment for and they take it upon themselves to decide 'how bad' you are and if you're worth an emergency appointment. Receptionists have no right to judge people like that as they are not Doctors. And when telling them personal information that should be confidential between patient and Doctor, they reply with a patronising "Uh you have that" type of response which is very unprofessional. Younger staff are quite pleasant but forget to do their job, so when you take a trip to the GP and your prescription isn't there it's time wasting and frustrating. You can see why the receptionists would be under stress with the new system in place, however, they should treat patients with more respect. If you ever get an appointment, the one to one experience with the Doctor is usually ok, but depending which Doctor it is, sometimes I leave feeling dissatisfied. I don't want to be one of those people to tell a Doctor how to do their job (because that would be stupid) but for example, surely it's common sense not to give someone who has an eating disorder and a BMI of 36, tablets that increase appetite and make you gain weight. The pharmacy staff next door however, are good workers and are run off their feet. They get prescriptions handed out almost instantly. It's very rare that I hear other people complaining to the pharmacy staff but when they do, it's due to the Doctor not sending the information over fast enough. P.S. I agree with another comment also, it IS very embarrassing to get a call back from the Doctor and you have to talk about personal things in a public area. Furthermore, if you are only ill for a few days but need a Doctors note and can't get through to the receptionist, what the hell are you supposed to do? Eventually get an appointment and say "yeah I was ill last week and I need a Doctors note because I had time off work". It's ridiculous.

recent_reviews.author: Gavin Porter
recent_reviews.text: Many, many years ago you could never get through to make appointments. One time I even rang 40-50 times within a couple of hours and still didn't get through. However, I always found the Drs & Nursing staff great, and the reception team they have are fantastic too ! Then approx 4-5 years ago their new phone system and maybe other changes they implemented approx made it so much easier to get through. As you went into a phone queue instead of getting the engaged tone when the line was busy. Now they have an online portal which has made it even easier for most people to make appointments. You answer some well designed questions, list any concerns and can even upload photos. All in all, it's become a well run great practice.

recent_reviews.author: Polly Lara
recent_reviews.text: I moved 4 miles away to help a sick relative during covid, while still owning and often staying at my address in wythenshawe. When this was mentioned the receptionist told me I could no longer be part of the surgery, despite the fact my house is maybe 300m away and my legal residence. I explained this to her and assumed it would be alright as it wasnt mentioned again and since then I had several tests for an ongoing condition and was booked in for a phone appointment. No one called me for the phone appointment so I called to check in. I was informed they'd removed me as a patient, two and a half months after the initial conversation, without informing me. They refused to let me know the results of the tests, which I need to get a prescription. This has also interfered with my ability to book my second vaccine! I now have to wait to get registered at another surgery and have an initial appointment there before they can access my medical records and get me the medication I need. This is going to take 4 weeks. Completely unhelpful, gave me no notice this was happening, didn't even bother to tell me they wouldn't be making the phone appointment which I waited in for. Terrible service.

recent_reviews.text: Came into doctors today to have a canula taken out as I was discharged from A&E 3 days ago dues to chest pain and nurse false my notes saying it was taken out notes given to me and medication this is not true. I'm absolutely upset and appalled at the NHS DOCTORS POLICE AND SOCIAL SERVICES FOR NOT LOOKING AFTER MY HEALTH AND WELFAIR.

recent_reviews.author: Another one Bites the dust
recent_reviews.text: *Edited* There are some doctors here who I've had issues with but I asked to speak with the Practice Manager to complain about it and she was lovely, listened to all my concerns and has put it on my records that I don't want to be seen by those doctors again. I must say there are some great doctors here who do their job well and listen to you. Dr Greenslade and Dr Molyneux are the two I enjoy seeing. The male doctors have all been pleasant too. No issues with them at all. On the flip side... I (and friends who also attend this surgery) have found Dr Fazal didn't want to listen to concerns and wanted to get the appointment over as quick as possible. I found Dr Iram didn't listen and blamed my symptoms on my weight, telling me the symptoms will go when I've lost weight even though I have lost 50lbs and the symptoms have worsened since losing weight so her theory, I feel doesn't make sense. (It's important that I include this in the review because anyone who is overweight will know how upsetting/irritating it is when you find a doctor who just blames everything on your weight.) Overall the practice has some doctors who are great and some who I found just don't want to be there and will blame your symptoms on your weight. All I can suggest is remember who you see, if you like them take note of their name and ask for them again. If you don't, tell the reception desk to put it on your notes that you don't want to be seen by them again.

recent_reviews.author: The 5 Brothers Squad
recent_reviews.text: Benchill Medical Centre is no longer the practice it used to be. All the old doctors are gone, and what’s left is a team that seems to have no urgency, no compassion, and no sense of responsibility. My 12-year-old son developed a serious issue with his eye — it was clearly getting worse — and we spent over two weeks trying to get him seen. I called multiple times, explained that his condition was deteriorating, and still we were ignored. When they finally responded, they didn’t even book an appointment — they just sent us to a pharmacy, where we received no help at all. This isn’t just poor service — this is gross negligence. They failed to provide proper medical care for a child in pain, and they didn’t even follow up. The delay has made things worse, and we’ve had to seek help elsewhere. No examination, no urgency, no care. This practice has changed for the worse — it is now unsafe and unreliable. If you value your family’s health, especially your children’s, I strongly advise you to go elsewhere.

recent_reviews.author: Michelle Moores
recent_reviews.text: When lockdown started, Benchill Medical Practice was oneof the best, if not, the best practice in Wythenshawe (in my opinion) it was one of the only practices who still had face to face appointments for emergencies. Since then, it has become one of the worst for getting appointments. I rang a couple of weeks ago and was 24th in line on the phones. I waited one hour and thirty five minutes, for them to tell me they would send me a link to fill in a form which would be reviewed by a triage doctor and I would be contacted in two working days. That was on the Monday, they gave me an appointment for the Friday. Same happened today. Sent the form saying I had an allergic reaction to a new medication, they sent me an appointment for this Friday. I am still waiting for them to ring me with an appointment sooner because I rang saying I couldn't wait that long. What on earth has happened to this surgery? It has gone from being able to queue in a morning and seeing a doctor there and then, to having to wait four days to see a doctor Sometimes you can't even choose the doctor you want. Would no longer recommend BMP to anyone. System needs changing to get better reviews (in my opinion)

recent_reviews.author: amanda greenwood-oldham
recent_reviews.text: I've been a patient at the practice for 20+ years and mostly had very positive experience. The most difficult thing is getting through on the phone, but that's the issue with all GPs currently. Telephone appointments are satisfactory and if it requires to be seen then they usually try and squeeze you in. I believe this to be an outstanding GP practice. Receptionist included, they are often under a lot of pressure and are trying to fit everybody in, and let's be honest, not everyone that uses the gp or a&e needs to, often a trip to the pharmacy will be sufficient for some but they just don't do that.

recent_reviews.author: Dot Grindley
recent_reviews.text: Just over a year ago I had a bad productive cough. Thought it would go on its own but got worse. Book an online appt with Dr Patel and he rang me several days before the appointed time. Told me to go in. On examining me he told me I was very sick and didn't know how I was still standing. Have me a note for Wythenshawe. Also rang Wythenshawe himself. I was admitted with Pneumonia. Was on my intravenous antibiotics 5 days before my actual appointment was booked. Have seen him on a few occasions and so has my husband. He always calls back before the appointed time. I've never found the receptionists anything but courteous either. It really isn't their fault if appointments are booked for the day. That's why unless I feel I need to see someone that day I book a telephone appointment. If the doc feels the need to see me they tell me to call in.

recent_reviews.author: vishnu mohan
recent_reviews.text: Had very bad experience from customer service people in the center, including the so called manager - not from doctor and nurse . We were planning to migrate to another country and that place requested a form to be filled which gives details of Immunization status . It's a basic form most schools ask . Gp practise requested the kid to attend GP to give the form which we undertand, but unfortunately we were out of country for admission purpose and was not in a situation to attend in person. They also told i have to pay extra for that which we agreed to considering that form is important for kids school admission . We requested whether that can be done virtual which they usually give appointment for even when we call for severe illness, and this is just a statement form . They clearly rejected that request and was not even compassionate and accomodative. NHS stands for compassion which clearly is not the service we recieved form the administrative staff of Park medical center. My child couldn't go to school for few months because of this and finally got the statement from the new country GP after migration and registration which new GP here which obviously took some time . I wish the staff who were there would have been more professional and understanding. This happened months before and I am not posting this out of immediate response or anger . Still I am not able to forgive that response from that staff and manager , she was so adamant not to give the form and denied all possibilities apart from attending the practise in person which was not possible at that time . Ironically, all other friends who moved from UK and Ireland got their same form filled by respective GP practise without any concern. So it's not an NHS issue, it's purely that employee attitude and denial .

recent_reviews.text: My GP referred me to them for blood tests, they told me my GP didn’t send them the labels !!they didn’t even check my details. They asked me about my first name, nothing further !! So I went back to my GP and they confirmed that they already sent them !!! Really disappointed as I am really sick and I was waiting for a week , as well as I was fasting till 5 pm ! Very poor environment and communication and bad handling with patients…
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: maysaa Elhaj2 reviews2 months ago My GP referred me to them for blood tests, they told me my GP didn’t send them the labels !!they didn’t even check my details. They asked me about my first name, nothing further !! So I went back to my GP and they confirmed that they already sent them !!! Really disappointed as I am really sick and I was waiting for a week , as well as I was fasting till 5 pm ! Very poor environment and communication and bad handling with patients…Like Share Response from the owner 2 months agoDear Maysaa, Thank you for your feedback, and I’m very sorry to hear about your experience. After checking the system last night, the blood test request was not showing when the phlebotomist looked for it, which is why they were unable to proceed at the time. The Phlebotomist checks she has all the labels at the start of her clinic, and this is how reception knew the labels were not available. If your GP Practice added your blood test requests after you contacted them, they should have advised you to come back to the surgery to see if the phlebotomist would be able to see you. I completely understand how frustrating this must have been, especially as you had been waiting, were unwell, and had been fasting. It may also help to clarify that although the blood‑taking service is based at our practice, it is run by the Enhanced Hours Team. If you would like to make a formal complaint about the service you received, I can pass this directly to the Enhanced Hours management team so they can review what happened. Regarding fasting, we would not ask any of our patients to fast until 5pm. We offer morning appointments specifically for fasting blood tests. If you were advised to fast until that time, you will need to contact your own GP practice to discuss this further, as that advice would not have come from us. Thank you again for taking the time to share your experience — your feedback is important, and we want to ensure this is looked into properly. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact me on 0161 9985538. Best regards, Dan Hey Practice Manager

The support she offered in that short conversation was honestly staggering compared to what I’d experienced elsewhere. It made a huge difference at a moment when I really needed it. If this is the standard of care the practice offers before I’ve even joined, I feel very reassured about registering with them.

recent_reviews.raw_card_text: David Mchugh2 reviews3 months ago Almost impossible to get a appointment with a doctor. On line booking is a nightmare for us older people who are not good with technology.Like Share Response from the owner 3 months agoDear David, We’re disappointed to receive a 1‑star review, as we strive to make accessing care as smooth as possible. We understand that online booking can be difficult for some patients, which is why we provide several alternatives. You can call our reception team and they will complete the form on your behalf, or you can visit the practice to fill out a paper version. We accept appointment requests from 07:30 until 18:30, and all requests are triaged by a GP the same day, with patients receiving a response within 1 working day. Appointments are offered the same day for urgent requests, or within two weeks for non‑urgent requests. For some minor illnesses, you may be referred to the pharmacy under the national Pharmacy First scheme. We have worked hard to remove barriers for our patients while improving our appointment system, and we truly value feedback that helps us continue to refine it. I’d be happy to discuss this with you in more detail — please don’t hesitate to contact me. Dan Hey Practice Manager

recent_reviews.text: Used to love this practice, the doctors and staff were brilliant, but many have left now. The new appointment booking system is awful. Really not good if you work and/or have a chronic condition.

recent_reviews.author: Amrit Kaur Swalley
recent_reviews.text: During my call, I was advised by reception staff that I should take my mother to the dental hospital instead. This advice appeared to be a medical decision, which I found concerning, as reception staff are not clinically qualified to make such determinations. I later spoke with the reception manager, who confirmed that reception staff are permitted to make these decisions. This is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about patient safety and appropriate triage procedures. In addition, I do not feel that my complaint was handled effectively or taken seriously. There was no reassurance, clear explanation, or appropriate escalation of my concerns. I believe further training is required for reception staff, particularly regarding the limits of their role and the importance of not making or influencing medical decisions. As a patient, I expect clinical advice to be given by a qualified healthcare professional. This matter is particularly concerning given the Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements, which state that patients must be treated safely, appropriately, and with clear clinical oversight. I trust that this issue will be reviewed promptly to ensure patients are not placed at risk in the future. Thank you

recent_reviews.text: Doctors are a bit hit & miss, depending on who you get. I have seen a couple recently who are good, but if you are a woman around 50 years old, they want to slap you on HRT & say 'job done'. Nothing else has been considered for almost 2 years in my case. Am changing the star rating (was 3, but now I am annoyed again having to write a warning to others about the backdoor way patients are FORCED to load the NHS app, so am downgrading to 2 stars). Are we not in a country where we pride ourselves on having a choice? Come on, guys, too many people let stuff go, so people think that nobody cares. Make a small effort, everybody, and things can improve. Am now downgrading again to 1 star. Took a proxy voting form in to reception to ask if the doctor could sign it for my autistic son so he can vote. The whitish blonde haired receptionist immediately suggested to me that I should have taken it to my dentist. She was most unpleasant, unhelpful, and short with me. She should look up the definition of receptionist.

recent_reviews.author: Erandi Samaraweera
recent_reviews.text: ⚠️ Serious patient safety concerns – I strongly advise de-registering I am writing this review as both a medical doctor and a parent who has been genuinely fearful for their child’s safety while registered at Junction Surgery and Alkrington Surgery. Since registering in August 2025, I have experienced repeated safety and professionalism concerns. My child was once prescribed antibiotics without enough doses to complete the course and I was told that “missing a few doses won’t matter.” This is unsafe advice and only corrected after I insisted. My daughter had a persistent cough for several months and attended multiple times, yet no appropriate referral or timely investigations were arranged. When she later developed fever and blood-stained sputum, an out-of-hours GP was clearly concerned and requested urgent investigations. Despite this, our concerns were dismissed the following day, my child was not properly examined, and I was given incorrect medical information. False reassurance when a child is coughing up blood is unacceptable. When I later requested an urgent private ENT referral due to ongoing bleeding, I was asked to pay a fee during a highly distressing situation, despite previously being told such referrals were not chargeable. The supervising GP did not attend to assess my child in person. Overall, I felt unheard, disrespected, and unsafe. Based on my experience, I would strongly advise patients—especially parents of young children—to seriously consider de-registering and seeking care elsewhere. IF ANYONE NOT TRUSTING ME PLEASE READ THE REVIEWS IN OTHER WEBSITE AND CQC REPORT

recent_reviews.text: I recently had text messages in regards to an Annual Review which I'm not even entitled to, I further received a letter for a home visit to do the annual review a few days later. I never went to the first appointment since I assumed it was cancelled due to the letter I received. I spoke to the nurse today, she wasn't happy about me missing the appointment and when I refused to have Annual Reviews she stated that I may have to register with another GP, I couldn't be bothered arguing with her and just said "OK" to pretty much everything she was saying after that. I ended up ringing the GP in regards to why I have been given appointments for Annual Reviews when I'm not entitled to them as well as being concerned with numerous mistakes on my medical records which I've requested to have corrected but I need to speak with the Practice Manager in regards to that. I'm protecting myself from harm by refusing certain things until my medical records get corrected. One funny thing is that the nurse thinks I'm "House Bound" and she stated that it's on the system but reception stated it's not so the Nurse must have me mixed up with another patient. It'll be really funny if she turns up after I've already declined the Annual Review, she'd only be wasting her time and the practice is also wasting their time booking me in for Annual Reviews without my consent, any missed appointments will be them wasting their own time since I've stated numerous times that I'm not entitled to them and don't consent. This GP also failed to update my records after I sent them a psychological report confirming that I don't have Autism or a Learning Disability. Luckily my new GP know how to do their job and have amended my records.

recent_reviews.author: T
recent_reviews.text: Always had bad experiences with this surgery but this one took the cake. I’ve had a knee surgery recently so I’m not able to get to the surgery by myself, I’d noticed I hadn’t been prescribed enough medication upon leaving the hospital and was told to get more I must contact my GP and that there was an electronic message sent detailing the surgery to them. When I called they said there was nothing on the system and I’d have to call the hospital, so I did and the hospital said that the electronic message was already sent and there was nothing more they could do. The GP expected me to now travel to them with a printed off discharge note which I was not able to do alone and if it wasn’t for my mother I wouldn’t have been able to access my medication. This isn’t the first instance I’ve heard about the GP not receiving electronic copies but I’m starting to wonder if they actually bother even checking for them properly. This was a mess around for someone who needed the time to recover and desperately needed their medication before the weekend closed in.. as someone who is autistic it is already difficult to call asking for assistance with issues like this but the staff are completely unfriendly and bite your head off when asking for help.

Absolutely appalled at the service from this drs.

We want our surgery to provide the best possible care and service to patients and are trying to improve. recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Julian Smith1 review2 years ago I can never get through. And when I send an email they send an email back saying ring patch. Patch are as worse as junction surgery.Like Share Response from the owner 2 years agoThank you for your feedback. We are sorry that you have had issues getting through. We have ongoing problems with our phone system but are in the process of moving to a new provider and hope that this switch will improve things. With regards "ring patch". I think you have likely been asked to contact us via PATCHS which is an online consultation service which many patients have positive experience with (average rating 4.5 out of 5 stars). To use PATCHS go to https://patchs.ai/practice/junctionsurgery/ or follow the link on the appointment page of our website. We recommend PATCHS as our clinicians can access information on there quickly, and can file data straight to the patient record quickly and effectively. Many patients have their health issues reviewed directly with the GP via this online text consultation and have treatment or examinations directly arranged by the GP. For this reason it is preferable to email communication. Once again, we are sorry that you've had a bad experience trying to get through. If you would like us to specifically investigate an event, email the practice directly to complain so we can investigate further. If you continue struggling to get through and PATCHS isn't an option, another option would be to attend the surgery and our reception team will do whatever they can to help.

Kind regards, Junction Surgery

recent_reviews.author: naruichgo
recent_reviews.text: While many post issues regarding the receptionists or wait times, my primary issue with this GP is in fact, the doctors themselves. I suffer from some complex needs that this GP surgery clearly has no interesting in helping manage. I've essentially been told that despite medications and other health issues relating to some problems I've been having, that they are mine to solve and the GP will do nothing about it (despite NICE and the NHS website suggesting multiple actions GPs could take). I get told to do blood tests and then no follow up on next appointments. GPs don't bother to read previous history before talking to you. Had many times where flags have been raised during yearly review and then the GP/Doctor/Nurses gives not a single fig to actually escalate the issue further. There's no care here. The Doctors will watch you cry and then proceed to tell you what's happening is your fault. Will only act if you literally drag them and force them by having to repeat visits and be firm. Clearly out of their depth with so many issues, especially mental health. Do better. I'm moving else where to a different GP despite living literally a 5 minute walk away. That tells you everything.

recent_reviews.author: Chris “Chris” Le'Carpentier
recent_reviews.text: I have only been with this practice since moving into the area in March 2023. I have needed the services of the GP twice. The first time it took almost 2 weeks to get an appointment and the second time I am still waiting. The surgery cancelled the appointment over a week in advance, as the doctor was apparently not going to be available and the next date for an appointment is now in February 2024. Two and a half months for an appointment is outrageous and this despite blood test results identifying abnormalities. I suspect I will need to have fresh blood tests before I finally get to see the GP due to the time that will have elapsed but I feel one actually cares. I have not even had the courtesy of a phone call, as requested to explain the blood results. I just got told to read the results on the app. I personally have received a terrible service and am going to register with a different GP practice.

recent_reviews.author: Carl Eden
recent_reviews.text: The NHS in general is crumbling at present and this is very much how the practice feels. I don't blame them, they must be under enormous pressure, but it can be a 6 week wait for a none urgent appointment. Trying to get through on the day is just a cattle market and their can easily by 8 or 9 people in front of you in the phone queue. Again, I blame all this on 13 years of political mismanagement rather than the surgery itself. The doctors do their best, the practice manager is lovely and always willing to help with issues, and the majority of receptionists (with one notable exception) are very helpful and understanding. We always pray that we don't get that one particular receptionist when we call up as she can be rude, officious, confrontational, unhelpful, and sometimes gives the wrong information, hence the loss of 2 stars from our review. Frontline staff and their attitudes matter very much to a practice and I cannot for the life of me think why she is allowed to continue making the practice look bad as others have commented. Still, thanks must go to others on the team, some who probably work for a pittance, for keeping a cheery demeanour in such a difficult job.

recent_reviews.author: Paulina Jasowicz
recent_reviews.text: I can’t express how lucky I am to be a patient of Dr. Collett-White. I have been seeing him for a few years now, and he’s the best doctor I have come across. I had a couple of challenging years trying to sort out my physical and mental health, and he has been such a great support in both. He’s really thorough and takes the time to answer all my questions. He always explains things in a way that’s easy to understand and really remembers what’s been discussed in previous visits. He also asks about my other consultations at the hospital. He is genuine, kind, and supportive. He often comes up with several treatment options, so I can choose the most suitable one for me. This means so much to me, as I’ve encountered a few GPs in the past who had little to no empathy. Dr. White creates such a safe, nonjudgmental space, and he truly cares about his patients. The front desk staff are kind and helpful too, and the nurses are patient and caring. I can’t forget Dr. Brenchley, who’s just as great as Dr. White.

recent_reviews.author: SARAH H
recent_reviews.text: On this occasion I was pleased with the care I received for my 3yr old. I contacted surgery numerous of times at 8am (to be expected), I eventually got through to a very helpful lady at reception, provided her with my child’s symptoms and she asked me if I could go to the surgery now, I got there within 10 minutes. I was seen straight away by Dr Brady (a wonderful Dr of many years), he completed the necessary checks and gave me a prescription. I can honestly say I already have noticed a difference within 48hrs, my child is eating, interacting and back to their active self. The Dr’s at this surgery are superb! Best around. I moved GP when I moved out of the area and I was disappointed compared to Woodside Medical, moved back to the area and came back to Woodside Medical Centre. On this occasion I could not fault the reception desk service, it felt like old times, previously the reception desk team was patronising, rude and didn’t care for patients. Keep up the great work Woodside Medical Centre I noticed a difference.
