recent_reviews.author: B M
recent_reviews.text: I wouldn't recommend parking at this doctors. I have a disabled mother who relies on me to take her to her appointments, and the carpark is always full despite the doctors waiting room being empty. I input my registration everytime I take my mum, as she signs in with the doctor. I do this habitually everytime and have absolutely not forgot to do it. I then received a letter in the post for a £100.00 fine for parking in the carpark. I asked for a confirmation of appointment from the receptionist which she was good enough to give me, as well as a letter from the assistant manager requesting that the charge be dropped, and I appealed the fine. I then received an email from the carpark company saying my appeal has been rejected because I did not input my reg, and the fine still stands. This is a disgusting way to treat people who are trying to take their elderly disabled relatives to their doctors appointments. If I was using the carpark for its intended purposes, with a valid appointment, why am I STILL being charged by this company?! What purpose does this serve?! Even if somebody was to forget to input their reg, for arguments sake, mistakes happen, why would you fine people on their first strike for trying to use the facilities and then not accept their appeal when they have clear evidence of an appointment. Its just a sickening excuse to make money off people. Wouldn't surprise me if they do it on purpose!

recent_reviews.author: Ari Steinberger
recent_reviews.text: Dr. Deacon may have a title, but don’t be fooled—he is anything but a helpful doctor. Under his leadership, this so-called medical practice operates like a bad joke, with his team of clueless cronies openly Googling conditions right in front of desperate patients. But that’s not even the worst of it. When our 11-month-old baby needed urgent care, we were met with days of exhausting arguments just to secure a simple face-to-face appointment. Imagine the sheer negligence—precious time wasted while a helpless infant suffered. My advice? Stay far, far away. Dr. Deacon, Dr. Cohen, and their disgraceful team are nothing short of a danger to public health, in my opinion. If you value your well-being, trust Hatzolah or A&E instead. Your life—or your child’s—may depend on it.

recent_reviews.author: Sian Gizon
recent_reviews.text: Went in as I had a fever and difficulty swallowing with white spots on tonsils. I was checked in same time as a lady with a small child . We were both waiting over 40 mins while people with later appointments came and went. I asked if there was anywhere i could have a drink of water and was told to go shop round the corner as all fountains have been removed but i didnt want to miss the dr calling me in. We both asked if we'd be waiting much longer as the small child needed feeding and was getting tired waiting and it turns out we hadn't been checked in at all! After she and her child were finally seen to, I was called into the dr office. I was there for less than a minute and the dr asked me 2 questions took my temp checked my throat and said 'youve got a sore throat, come back Friday if it still hurts'. After feeling like an idiot wasting time i went home and threw up then went to bed shivering with a temperature of 38.6. My husband got me seen by a private dr through his work who diagnosed tonsillitis and gave antibiotics straight away. I dread to think what the experience would be for a more serious illness. Whole experience here was terrible.

recent_reviews.text: This surgery has gotten a lot if stick about waiting times and when to call but thats not really their fault, their hands are tied for a lot of things. recent_reviews.author: M C
recent_reviews.text: The service at this surgery is soooo poor. To get an appointment you have to ring up at 8am on the day you want it. It's crazy, so everyone who wants an appointment is on the phone persistently redialing from 8am onwards. It took 157 redials to get through - not to a human, but to their queuing call system. That being said, after 18 minutes it then connected - but to another message, saying that they are migrating their systems over and cannot offer any non urgent appointments or issue repeat prescriptions, but to hold for urgent enquiries. Why do their phone lines not give this information before 157 redials and 18 minutes on hold? Anyway, I decided to hold and after some more music and waiting I actually spoke to a receptionist (08:42 - 42 minutes after first starting to contact them), who asked if it could "wait until tomorrow since I'd already waited three weeks" before trying to get this appointment. I explained that I didn't want to come running to doctor after 2 minutes as I wanted to see if my problem resolved itself and after three weeks it was time to try and get treatment. I then explained that I had had to take time off work today just to try to get through to them as I couldn't commute in a car, constantly redialing, so I am now at home. I can't go through the same process again tomorrow, take time off work again and waste the morning trying to get through (to potentially not even get an appointment). But anyway through my persistence, I did secure an appointment. Be aware though, there are previous occasions that I have got through after hundreds of redials - to then get told that all appointments have now been taken - try again tomorrow please. This process needs a massive shake up, it is not fit for purpose. They used to have an online booking system (AskMyGP), which was fractionally better, but that you could only use it during certain working hours and was also hit and miss as whether you got an appointment. recent_reviews.text: I spent 4 hours in A and E yesterday eve , I was told to make an appointment with my GP as soon as possible . As I’ve been feeling really not well I rang this morning ... it took 123 phone calls to get through ... 30 mins on the phone ! Constantly engaged !!!! Obviously my hospital results have now gone through to The surgery .... so I’ve just received a text now saying due to recent results pls make an appointment at the surgery . I ring up and eloquently explain my reason for ringing and that I’d already attended this morning ! I ended up handed over to someone else to have to repeat it all .. to then be asked ... what do you want us to do ?! I also explained 123 phone calls is not acceptable !!! To which the reply was .... yes we’ve been busy .... I suggest the left hand doesn’t know what the right hand is doing ?! But the empathy I received at 123 phone calls was non existent !! I can only comment on the compassion and care Dr .Wookie has shown my dying Father and Stepmum ... however I myself can not praise the service I’ve received as it’s failed so many times !! Including an appointment I made that I sat 30 mins beyond .... queried it ... to be told you don’t have an appointment ... to ... can you come back in 45 mins ... which I did ... I sat another 20 mins beyond this ... to eventually got to see a Doctor who was uninterested and unhelpful ... I picked up my shopping and said I’ll leave shall I ... to which he responded ... let’s start again .... I’m very upset at my service so far .. in 5 years .... if it was a retail institution ... it would close down !!!! I avoid coming as much as possible ! Not great for good health !!!

recent_reviews.author: Paris Pinglaux
recent_reviews.text: I had a 6cm ovarian cyst burst, had internal bleeding, and needed a blood transfusion. I needed urgent surgery. I ended up in A&E - called the GP a day or so later relaying my very worrying symptoms and A&Es findings (projectile vomiting, diarrhoea, unable to keep food/water/tablets down, excruciating pelvic and full body pain, falling in and out of consciousness, blood in urine). A GP told me it was ‘nerves’, and gave no explanation as to why my symptoms suddenly increased tenfold. I was refused anti-sickness tablets many times while dealing with the unbearable nausea and vomiting, because they can become addictive apparently. The pain was unbelievable, I had to take the maximum dosage of cocodamol a day, and that barely touched the sides. Rather than showing concern for the severity of my pain, nausea, and other symptoms, conversations around pain medications became interrogations regarding addiction. I had a large cyst that needed to be removed urgently. They should have heard my symptoms and flagged them as concerning. They should have contacted my NHS surgeon with those concerns, urging them to bring the surgery date forward. They should have spotted the signs and symptoms of a ruptured cyst. Instead of trying to understand what could be happening to cause these very severe symptoms, they did nothing but minimise and ignore my concerns, while refusing me medications that were saving me from ending my life due to the constant, excruciating pain. What exactly are these doctors trained in? How could you be a trained doctor and miss the signs of an ovarian cyst rupture, especially considering my suspected endometriosis? I felt that something was seriously wrong despite this, so I pursued private surgery. If I did not have the means to do that, as many do not, I may not be here now. I could have gone into sepsis, I could have developed blood clots, and god knows what else. Not only that, I also had samples necessary for a referral to gastroenterology go missing three times in a row, which is just bloody odd. I am still in unbelievable amounts of pain, and have ongoing symptoms. I spoke to the practice manager yesterday. I wanted to try to explain how deeply traumatic all of this has been for me. According to her, I should have contacted my surgeon and asked for the surgery to be moved forward, not the GP. Like ???? I didn’t know I had a cyst! That is why I went to my GP for help, so that they could flag this as a potential emergency, justify my concerns, and potentially get my surgery moved forward or flagged as urgent. I am not a doctor, I went to my GP because I had no idea what was going on in my body, I was unbelievably ill, and scared. Is that not what you are supposed to do? However, my concerns were minimised, and I was made to feel dramatic. So, I just kept suffering until I could finally be booked in for a private laparoscopy. I explained that my dad (also at the same practice) has stage four cancer, and recently my brother passed away too, so my mental and physical health are very poor. She wouldn’t let me finish and responded very unprofessionally. I can’t remember her exact words, but it was something along the lines of ‘don’t start that’ or ‘don’t go there’ because her father passed away and she had been through a lot too. Honestly, I was gobsmacked, still am. I don’t understand why she thought it appropriate to respond like that. It is her job, that she is paid for, to be the practice manager. I hoped she would listen to my concerns and understand how negligent the practice had been, but I suppose that would be an admission of guilt. I am 24. I haven’t even managed to graduate university yet because of how much I have had to go through. All I want is to be healthy! I have been living a nightmare, and this practice has only made it harder. The doctors that work there traumatised me. If you do choose to join this practice, ask for doctor Nisha. She is truly lovely. The rest are incompetent.

recent_reviews.author: Kerry Hall
recent_reviews.text: I find the staff really friendly and helpful. However, I get frustrated at the medical team (drs, not senior health practitioners). They do not have enough time to assess you properly, ask you to make a follow up appointment, which is next to impossible as you ring on the day, and not guaranteed the same Dr. Then you have to go over why you are their again, and by the time time they have scanned your notes, times up. You can pre-book of course, but you could be dead by the time you get an appointment with Dr you want. I don't blame the surgery at all, it is a failing of the NHS. Which is a failing of our government. The Drs work incredibly hard. I do worry that diagnosis can be quick and patient dismissed, and follow ups don't happen.

recent_reviews.author: Richard Openshaw
recent_reviews.text: I only came on to find the closing time for the surgery and was completely shocked to see some of the reviews. I have been with this surgery for a very long time and sadly with some serious illnesses, it has meant many visits and phone calls etc. I am so sorry to disagree with most people's reviews, as my experience has been nothing short of professional, personal and caring. The reception/administrative staff are also in this category. I have no vested interest in the practice, so my opinions are my own and on experience and observing. The one thing I will say, this is Radcliffe Medical Practice within a primary care centre. The staff at the practice only deal with Radcliffe Medical Practice patients and no other practice or department in the building. You wouldn't go to a shopping centre and go to Next for a refund of something you purchased at WH Smith. I have seen lately a lot of people approaching reception staff and asking them to help with other departments within the building, but sadly they cannot help, as they only deal with that practices patients. Some people just don't like that and take it out of them, which is grossly unfair. I take my hat off to Lucy the other morning, as she had two such people and they were so nasty, whilst she was being so pleasant and explaining. Having a bad day, not feeling well? Don't take it out on the staff, they are there for your benefit, not your sounding board. Also, to the gentlemen who came in that morning to and made a right song and dance. He said he had been told by staff to get there for 8am to see if an appointment was available with a certain doctor, "for 8". Don't come in at 8.10 and expect there to be any left and then take it out on the receptionist. You had already told her you were to be there for 8, but you weren't. I know for a fact if you had been there "for" 8, you would have got an appointment. Shame on you.

recent_reviews.author: Mrs Robey
recent_reviews.text: I am sad to have to write this post but after several bad experiences I find I have no option, firstly the on line app, I have on many occasion got up early to be on for 7:00 , to find it not available or to say its now closed, trying to get through on the telephone is a feat in itself, on average it takes between 30 to 80 minutes to get through only to be given incorrect information or told there are no appointments and either ring 111 or try again tomorrow. The latest advice is walk into a pharmacy and get advice from them, on both occasions I have been told they should not be sending adults to pharmacists for the reason I had been sent, and that for many things they can only treat children up to the age of 17. The sad thing is there are good medical staff in the practise and without Janice the practise nurse and the other nurses, the whole place would fall down, I have not been able to see an actual gp at the practise for over 2 years. My advice is better training for the receptionist, as they are constantly giving out incorrect information, you CAN not go to emergency numbers when your own gp is open and you will be told to go back to your gp. The phones need to be manned better or the option to get a ring back rather than kept holding on line. People are genuinely suffering and when you are ill you don't want to be passed around, many people don't have transport to go to these sometimes faraway out of hours practise and if your ill having to go out to appointments late at night in the cold to bolton rochdale or Oldham is barbaric. There is a desperate need for change and maybe invite patients in for a forum to get a clear understanding of how it affects individual patients.

recent_reviews.author: Martin Godfrey
recent_reviews.text: Booking GP appointments at Redbank is done via the AskMyGP website starting at 7am each morning. By logging a request close to this start time i've never had much of a problem getting an appointment over the last four years since they introduced the website. I tend to ring the surgery outside key times (eg after 10am) when booking blood tests and so on. During the pandemic it took a very long time for the phone to be answered, but response times over the last six months have been much much better. It is true that trying to book an appointment over the phone at 8am can be an issue (AskMyGP is the solution to that), but given the number of patients registered at GP practises these days, if each one had 30 receptionists answering the phone at 8am it would likely not be enough. I'd like to thank all the staff for what they do - I've been a patient at the practise for about 10 years now - and have found them universally very helpful.

recent_reviews.text: If you see Dr. Flascher I would avoid him if I were you! My dad attended the surgery often, starting in August where my dad suffered pains in his chest. From August to December he seen Dr. Flasher (who isn't his doctor but stands in for him all the time) and over and over he tried to say that my dad had a chest infection and kept giving him various antibiotics. On one occasion when he went in he had seen a nurse who had done his blood and told him he needed to go to the hospital for an X-ray, 24 hours later Dr. Flasher tells my dad OVER THE PHONE he has cancer. My dad was told next month that he had less than 12 months to live, but actually passed away 3 months later. In my opinion Flasher should count his lucky stars my dad didn't take this further with the surgery, as even my dad's doctor said looking at his notes he wasn't happy with the care he received from the surgery. Flasher if you see this I would strongly recommend you should go on further training to look after the patients in your care as I really feel sorry for them!

recent_reviews.author: Danielle Birkett
recent_reviews.text: I had to leave rock healthcare after being a patient for 6 years. They never answer the phones, I find the staff rude and unempathic. I visited 3 times in 3 months - once for blood tests that were requested by a private practitioner for my thyroid, once for a smear test and once for my annual blood tests due to a genetic condition I have that causes an increased risk in cancer. On my third visit of which was the only one related to my genetic condition I was quite bluntly accused of being a hypocondriac. The nurses words were you need to stop letting this genetic condition get to your head and had I even been diagnosed with this condition' I was so disgusted and upset by this comment that I changed GPs immediately. I have been diagnosed and have to have several screenings due to the fact I'm at an 80% risk of cancer and at a young age. I try my best to manage this condition but the one thing I need is a gp surgery who will take me seriously when I have symptoms. The first time I had a bad experience was when I was repeatedly told by a nurse at rock healthcare that I'm far to young to get bowel cancer and it's highly unlikely. I had to argue with her for several minutes that this isn't the case with my gene, she kept pushing her argument when she didn't even know what my condition was when I first walked in. News flash my dad was only 36 and Stephen Sutton was 18 so unfortunately no it doesn't matter that I'm young. Absolute disgrace of a surgery and shows how detrimental private healthcare services are for our NHS. I'm writing this now as I have been trying to call for my husband's results from a stool sample he sent in over a week ago. I have been unable to get through for 1.5hrs now and we know he has an infection as I have the same one from food poisoning. My new gp surgery got my sample a day later than his and I've nearly finished my antibiotics. However he's still waiting due to the complete mess that is rock healthcare. He has now just handed in his forms to change to my gp who also answered the phone within 2mins this morning for me to get a sick note. So unfortunately rock healthcare can't blame 'a sign of the times' as other gp surgery's in bury have got it right.

recent_reviews.author: Val Greenhalgh
recent_reviews.text: Recently took my mum for a scan here. She is disabled and I dropped her at the door to sit and wait for me whilst I parked the car. Someone very efficiently came to collect her and escorted her to her scan. I went to the Star suite but was unsure where she was. I needed to find her as she has severe mobility issues so spoke to the receptionist. She very rudely refused to confirm or deny that my mother was being attended to, and would not even say whether I was in the right place. I understand data protection, but gave my mum's name, dob and address and explained I needed to find her to help her walk, but no help at all. The medical staff undertaking the scan were very good but the receptionist was rude, ignorant and had an appalling attitude with zero communication skills and zero customer service. As the receptionist is the first face to be seen on arrival, I suggest you review your recruitment criteria to ensure you employ people who are pleasant, articulate and approachable, rather than ignorant, unpleasant, jobsworths

recent_reviews.author: Helen Perlin
recent_reviews.text: I had a very distressing experience with Dr Tse Belmond and feel it is important to share this for transparency. I attended an appointment following a panic attack. As English is not my first language, I brought my partner for support. During the consultation, my partner was dismissed and interrupted, and I was pressured to speak despite being visibly distressed. I was prompted to discuss a traumatic experience, which caused me to become extremely upset. Throughout this, I was not offered reassurance or support, and the lack of empathy was noticeable. At a later appointment, I raised concerns about possible Autism and requested an assessment. This was met with a dismissive response, including laughing, and statements were made that Autism is rare in women and predominantly affects men. I found this response unprofessional and not in line with current understanding. I also have concerns about how suicidal thoughts I disclosed were recorded, as they were documented as “depressed mood – minor,” which did not reflect the seriousness of what was discussed. Overall, I left feeling unheard, belittled, and unsafe. I would not feel comfortable seeing this doctor again and would advise others to be cautious.

recent_reviews.text: very hit and miss. on this occasion a definite miss. I had fractured my foot and needed blood thinners, the consultant at Salford had not given me enough saying I needed to take for 4 weeks but giving us a script for 2. After a lot of help from Salford Royal we were emailed by The Sides and told the script would be sent to the pharmacy from The Sides to next door. We explained we were going on holiday and had only 1 days worth left when we arrived home. Arrived home went to the pharmacy only to be told the script could not be issued and had to be done by the consultant! More frantic calls to Salford this time asking can we pick up the script from Salford as we didnt want The Sides involved. The Sides said they had left a message on our home phone (little use when we had told them we were away) unsure why they couldnt have emailed or sent a text as my notes clearly state i cannot speak. Blood thinners are to prevent DVT when Im wearing a fracture boot so we consider this to be very poor service.

recent_reviews.author: Adam Birds
recent_reviews.text: This GP surgery has gone extremely downhill the last year. Previous to that you could ring and either get a telephone appointment the same or next day and then if you needed a face-to-face they always had appointments. You could also just message the GPs and send pictures and they could even prescribe stuff for basic things without a phone call. It was great. But now, you can't message a GP and either you have to ring at 8am (which not all people can) or you get offered an appointment for two months in advance and what good is that for. recent_reviews.text: My kids got eczema and can’t sleep well recently. First I called them on 27/12/2024 they told that they can only take emergency cases. I though it’s because of Christmas holiday period so I tried to call again on 30/12/2024. They thought this was not emergency case so they helped to book at Silverdale which I couldn’t understand so I missed the appointment. I called again on 31/12/2024 and they told that they are only handling emergency cases again. I questioned if it’s because of holidays but the lady on the phone told they have such arrangement for 2 years. The lady on the phone thought I only want to take the hydrocortisone cream repeatedly but the real situation is that my kids can’t sleep due to eczema. If the Lake GP has such arrangement, please make sure the staff has the ability to ask precise questions so that they can understand the real situation. Secondly, the emergency department in the hospitals is really for emergency. If GP only takes emergency cases so where is the place for handling normal cases?

recent_reviews.author: Orla Kelly
recent_reviews.text: I have been misdiagnosed and misinformed multiple times by 2 doctors and the first contact Physio at this practice. I have now decided to change to a practice where patients are listened to instead of spoken over. I initially went in with severe back pain in July and the doctor gave me Zapain which done nothing to relieve my symptoms. I ended up in a&e less than 2 weeks later. I then went back in and was told by doctor mason I had “chronic back pain” which was not true. I ended up paying £350 for a private mri which revealed multiple issues with my back (disc degenerative disease osteoarthritis a bulging disc and sciatica). I went to the first contact Physio who told me to continue with private physio and electrotherapy would be the way forward. Today I went back to the first contact Physio as I had a bad spasm in my back the other day which left me unable to move. He told me not to go to private physio as he didn’t think it was helping due to how stiff I was (this is connected to the spasm on Saturday not the physio I have had!) he also asked if the physio was just doing electrotherapy and when I said yes he said it wouldn’t work!!! This is what he initially recommended. I am living scared that my back could go any minute and the professionals at this practice do not care one bit. I am disgusted with the constant fobbing off I get and have chosen to leave this practice. I have never needed the doctors here before as I don’t suffer with my health but now that I do need them they have let me down massively. I would not recommend them to anyone

recent_reviews.author: ruth dawson
recent_reviews.text: After being a patient at Silver dale medical practice for over 30 years, I became very disalousiond having to wait 5weeks for a tel consultation regarding a letter for my recent cancer treatment. Also couldn't get a ref for Lympodema for over 3 weeks and surgery is always empty. Phoned up the Lakes medical centre and asked how long it takes to see a GP, also did I have a choice in Tel or face to face consultation. Receptionist was very informative and I resisted with them. This has been the best move I have made. Extremely happy with the service and care, even had the pharmacy Tel me today regarding my inhalers and giving me advice on rinsing my mouth after using them. The NHS really does get a lot of critism but I have to say changing my GP has been really good. Well done the Lakes medical centre.

recent_reviews.author: Sue G
recent_reviews.text: Surprised to see some poor reviews as I've never had an issue with the surgery. I've been a patient since 2015. Yes sometimes it can take a long time, and many calls, to get a same day appointment. But this is the same at all surgeries! Whenever I've needed an emergency appointment I've always been able to get one. I do recommend the Online Consult for none urgent appointments. Whenever I've completed this I've always had a response within 48 hours and either had follow up telephone consultations or face to face appointments. I have never found any member of staff to be rude, they have always been helpful. I do have a fair few medical conditions, and it has been one thing after another over recent years and all members of staff at the surgery couldn't have done any more to help me. The only issue at the surgery is car parking, they do only have a small car park, with additional parking available on nearby residential streets. Living only a few minutes walk away though I do try and walk to the surgery as much as possible.

recent_reviews.author: Kirsty Jackson
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient here for the last 2.5 years with my partner and our son. I am surprised to see the negative reviews as I cannot fault the GPs or getting an appointment. Yes it is a pain to phone up in the morning like all doctors, but you can generally get an appointment. Their online booking system is great, so now I just log in and make an appointment with whoever I wish to see, when I want to see them. You just need to get the online appointment form from reception - no longer call. In relation to GPs I have found them to be all very professional and well natured. The only negative about his practice is car parking! There are no parent and child bays (it's a small surgery car park), but I had to go in on one occasion as I couldn't get my car door open to put my baby in his car seat. That's the only thing that annoys me, but there is on street parking available too.

I have never been to a medical centre that so consistently demonstrates unprofessional, shambolic and uncaring attitude to their jobs and to the people they are supposed to serve. The nurse I am booked in with knows nothing about diabetes and so cannot see me. I was offered another appointment mid February but I refused. I will see the doctor later, always supposing they haven't made a mistake with this as well, and I will have 55 minutes of treatment/consultation in 15 mins. recent_reviews.author: Dawn Sunny
recent_reviews.text: Joined this practice Nov 2017, when my own GP of 45 years passed away. First impressions were that the reception area was dirty and smelly. Tired looking and in need of a good clean. Reception staff were unhelpful and i felt didn’t really want to be there. From registering onwards, I had a growing catalogue of errors from quiet simple admin tasks to more seriously getting results incorrect. No one answers the phone, prescriptions were lost, drs appts cancelled or changed without notifying me. Extremely unhelpful. I have never experienced anything like this. I have been a surgery Manager so I know what to look out for. I felt so sorry for patients who are already feeling unwell having to ask unfriendly and inexperienced staff to aid them. I have since found out that this surgery are in special measures. I can see why. It needs a really good shake up, employing happy caring professional and experienced staff, especially on the front desk, these are the representatives of your practice at the end of the day. Hopefully one day someone will take note of all the poor comments they receive. I have today re registered elsewhere.

OVERALL, from moving into the area from South Wales, the medical service, and The Lakes in comparison is very good. recent_reviews.author: Gaz W
recent_reviews.text: Lack of compassion. Lack of professionalism. Lack of empathy. Arrogance. Rudeness. Failing of DPA. Ignorance. This all starts at the reception area. The ladies normally treat their patients like dirt. Very unhelpful with a “tough*” kind of attitude. Every other practice seems to work fine and use common sense, not Silverdale. For some reason you can’t book an appt using the My GP app for Silverdale, but other practices... no problem. You can call after 9am at most practices and book an appt for a GP.... not Silverdale. The poor service then trickles down to the GPs. I feel rushed. I feel things are not explained clearly. I feel they are more interested in hitting targets than curing the sick. Of course it all depends on the GP. I feel some GPs don’t listen to your needs, ailments or feelings and make massive assumptions and with any reason can’t wait to fob you off to a physio or hospital. I have been visiting this practice ALL MY LIFE. It has declined steadily and then rapidly. So after ringing up to book an appt with my GP for a later date, I’ve now been told I need to ring at 8am tomorrow.... WHY??? What difference does it make? Not only was I told this, it’s the arrogance and unhelpful attitude from the jumped up receptionist that is making me seriously consider switch GP. I’d you’re not registered with a practice, don’t bother with this one. It’s very amateur from top to bottom and the care no longer exists towards patients. UPDATE: what a mess. They are changing their system now. I’m certain this joke of a practice is making it deliberately hard for patients to speak to someone or make an appt. They even send texts saying “you have an appt on 02/09 at 2pm, this could be a phone or face to face appt, please contact the surgery for clarification on which it is” - WHY NOT TELL US IN THE TEXT?!? My god, this surgery was better in the 80s before we had computers and apps. I don’t think I’ve seen my GP face to face for 5 years. Absolute joke. UPDATE: after being told Curtis the physio is off sick AGAIN, I was asked to call to rebook an appt. Rang up and said I can’t do the rest of today as going to work. The lady said the nurse will be informed and call me to make an alternate appt. I got the call “we have appointments free all day with a GP” she said, I explained that I’d already said I can’t do this. I did however say, I can make a u turn now and come and see you “oh, we are booked up till 10:30” - the lady literally just told me they had a full free day?!? I eventually settled on 12:30 the following day. My text comes through to say my appt is 4:30pm the following day?!? I’m now sat here at 5pm and still not been seen to. This practice is a farce. No doubt I will get the usual reply from the practice manager where she takes no accountability nor responsibility for how dreadful Silverdale has become.

Do the decent thing Silverdale .... if it wasn't for my mum's generation you wouldn't be where you are today .

recent_reviews.author: Chelsie Wright
recent_reviews.text: I rang around loads of clinics this morning complaining about struggling to breathe and everyone single one of them couldn't have cared less because I wasn't registered there. Luckily for me I found Silverdale where I explained to the receptionist and she went out of her way to get me on the system as an emergency and was seen too promptly. My Doctor was lovely, friendly and smiling and even though I went in there quite panicky I left feeling comforted and relaxed. I was told that I needed to have a blood test and upon booking at the counter a lovely nurse let us know that she was available to do it there and then if they just booked it in. I left after about 1 hour, a now registered patient there, bloods done, follow up appointment booked and prescription in hand. I think sometimes it's easy to get frustrated at our local practice because they always seem so busy, but at least at Silverdale they care and they try their hardest to help when needed.

recent_reviews.text: I am bit shocked to what the doctor has told me this morning which what I not expect for a doctor to say in general. My call was made before 8am even though the practice is open from 8am. I don’t mind getting a call in the morning but nobody has made me aware the calls are made in the morning from 7am to what the doctor has stated via telephone today . When I called to make an appointment I have mentioned to the receptionist that I am not sure whether I need a call or a face to face appointment and clearly have stated what my problem is. The doctor called and said that I would need to a face to face appointment to get examined. Which I felt that I have wasted my time because with the pain that I have I could have been seen today and maybe the doctor could see my problem because the pain that I have is not always there. Which means I am not sure when I will get face to face appointment as it’s Thursday today and to get a face to face appointment would be slightly longer (possibly next week) which means I am not sure if I will still be in pain at the time of when I get seen face to face. Also for the doctor to say that even if we do all investigation referrals ect I should expect for the problem not to be solved and that possibly I will be on long term painkiller depending on the specialists will say. Now from the time that I was registered at this doctors, until now I was actually thinking that this practice and doctors are very caring towards their patients, I don’t mean by just solving the problems and providing medicine . But I would definitely except for the doctor to be more caring of how they speak to the patients too , that is part of the care too. I defiantly wasn’t asking Dr Cheema about what I expected or about my expectations were, when I see the specialist . This is not what I expect from the doctor at all. We are all humans a despite I have this is an on going problem and still nothing is found and this is not a blame at the GP. recent_reviews.author: Veronika
recent_reviews.text: As a long-time patient of the practice, I wanted to take a moment to express my appreciation for the consistently positive and welcoming environment that all staff members, from reception to the nurses and GPs, have maintained over the years. I have been a patient at this practice since 2014 and have never encountered any issues. Even during the challenging times of the COVID-19 pandemic, the practice remained open and continued to assist to the best of its ability. It is unfair for individuals to damage the practice's reputation simply because they are unable to secure an immediate appointment. In my own experience, this issue is prevalent, if not worse, in other healthcare settings. Individuals need to address any concerns they may have directly with the staff at the practice, rather than resorting to negative online reviews. Some individuals don't understand that a single negative review can have a significant impact on a practice's reputation and it can be difficult to recover from such damage. I encourage everyone to communicate openly and constructively resolve any issues, rather than resorting to anonymously criticising the practice online. We should support the positive environment at the practice by addressing concerns directly and fostering open communication rather than hiding behind the keyboards...

recent_reviews.author: Skeet
recent_reviews.text: I have been with Orchard Medical Practice since the mid-1990’s. I came here because of dire medical consequences with my previous G.P. What a difference! I have always found that the reception staff, nurses and doctors who work here try and make my appointment as friendly and welcoming as they possibly can. Not all patients visiting may feel the same, due to their condition, but come on. They have a job to do and they do it very well. I feel like I’m treated as a person and not just a number, going through the motions. They haven’t, over the years, got everything 100% right, who hasn’t, yet when they do they have the decency to apologise and learn from it. The simplest way to book and cancel appointments and order repeat prescriptions is online via Patient Access (organised through the surgery) or through the ‘My GP’ app on your mobile. Appointments are readily available and if it’s urgent you may be able to pick up one that day by telephoning the surgery after 8.00 am for a five-minute appointment. With medication, it’s all laid out and everything just gets sent straight through to the pharmacist, waiting for pick up within 48hrs, maybe sooner. I feel that the doctors, nurses and associated health professionals attached to the surgery, are always looking after my best interests health-wise. I believe they put patients first. My family and I feel very fortunate to be patients here. This is a First Class surgery, make no mistake. Thank you so much, Howard.

recent_reviews.author: deborah browne
recent_reviews.text: Towards the end of last year, I witnessed what I can only describe as a master class in customer service. I was waiting to collect something, as I noted Michelle take over a phone call from a younger receptionist, it appeared to be a difficult phone call. I moved away and took a seat. I couldn’t hear the caller, but from the time it took, and response by Michelle, I could tell that it took a lot of patience and calmness. There was a lot of warmth and empathy, and when Michelle finished, she introduced me to the younger new receptionist. I said to her take it from me you are learning from one of the best, and from what i observed, that was a master class in customer service. I think we forget that the front line staff in any medical centre, whether it is on the phone or face to face, do an extremely good job, and are faced with a lot of difficulties along the way, and are blamed constantly for things that are beyond their control. I know the Limes staff well, and they are all really hardworking and caring individuals. Please remember they are all doing their jobs, to the best of their abilities, and going through the same pressures of everyday life, as every one of us.

recent_reviews.author: Finlay Hepburn
recent_reviews.text: I have been visiting walkden medical centre since a very young age, but after my recent appointment, I have been told I can no longer visit as I have changed addresses. I have moved addresses to across the road from my old home after moving out of my parents. But after being told I can no longer be registered here, after >10 years, is a massive let down. If they would have told me about this after all of my tests etc. then I wouldn’t have been too provoked but this has put me in an awkward position as I am (was) in the middle of appointments. My new address is actually closer to WMC than my previous address. Which I told the receptionist, but I am not in the new postcode limit apparently. I have been told I have 30 days to find a new GP. Which of course, it is hard to find a half decent one in this area, and this will probably make it 60 days before my next appointment. The Medical staff are very pleasant, understanding & informative. So for this I will give them 5 stars, in my review. But this new ‘postal code restriction’ is absolutely ludicrous & to put someone in this position whilst going through appointments is completely uncalled for and unnecessary.

recent_reviews.author: Bethy Mc
recent_reviews.text: My mum & myself would like to commend Walkden Medical Practice, in particular the reception staff. Their patience is exemplary in the face of an over whelmed patient list. For the past 9 months, I have spent a considerable amount of time on the phone to the Practice, so much so that I think they recognise my voice. They are knowledgeable, informative & professional, sign posting us to the appropriate health care professionals. They are not responsible for the lack of GPs nor for the booking system. They do their job and cannot create appointments that are not available. I would also like to commend the practice's Pharmacists, whose medication knowledge is outstanding. They have devised a medication care plan and followed it through with planned telephone appointments. The GPs have also been wonderful, both the locums and partners. We would like to say a massive THANKS to you all.

recent_reviews.author: Renee Tucker
recent_reviews.text: Initially I thought this GP was great. Appointments were made within two weeks, the GPs seemed concerned and attentive, that was 2 years ago. Now you are looking at appointment wait times of no less than a month. If you want to go to the morning Emergency clinics be prepared for the wait time to be at least 1hr 30 mins and the GPs are less attentive and thorough. One occasion my young daughter and I waited 3hrs 30min in the Emergency clinic for a rash in her head. We were told that we needed to go into a separate room when it comes to rashes. However, that room was simply a chair in the hallways behind the reception office with Dr's/ nurses walking through. It was a horrible experience with a young restless child. I truly believe they somehow forgot about us as I had to ask the reception who looked surprised we were still there. In regard to that rash, the GPs misdiagnosed my daughter (several times) without testing despite all of my consistent concerns which resulted in multiple Emergency clinic and phone calls, long wait times and the condition getting worse. My daughter was in agonising pain for months which resulted in in sleepless nights, loads of crying and the rash going from a 20p coin to the size of an orange which left a massive patch and multiple smaller ones! I dread having any heath issues because of the service of this place. I'm writing this currently waiting to be seen by the GP for 2hrs 30 mins from the time of arrival.

recent_reviews.author: Tracey Fowler
recent_reviews.text: I, and all my family have been lucky enough to be a patient at Elliott Street Surgery for over 44 years, and the level of care we receive has always been outstanding. It has never failed to be anything less than 100%. I want to express my deepest gratitude to Dr Shah and the team for the outstanding care and support provided lately especially to my Mum following her recent operation when she fell downstairs and broke her Femur bone. When Mum was finally discharged to bed rest at home, from Hospital after a new days, she was complaining that the feet were sore I thought she could be developing bed sores, I called the Surgery at 5.00pm, and the next day at 9.00am a Nurse called to examine Mum when she put us at ease and luckily, it was not bed sores! A week later I was worried about Mum again as her good leg swelled extremely fast at the foot and doubled in size - so I called the Surgery and I was called back within 5 minutes to say the Practice was closing in 30 minutes but Dr Shah would personally visit Mum on his way home and he did within 40 minutes, the door bell rang and Dr Shah was stood waiting to see Mum – I initially thought she had a blood clot in her leg, Dr Shah thoroughly examined her for over 10 minutes and explained things to us in great depth, he explained the swelling could be just because she has had the operation and was bed bound and not able to walk and be mobile, that was one scenario or, it could be water retention and a few other scenarios were discussed too. Dr Shah advised he would send a Nurse to collect Mums bloods the next day to see what the bloods revealed if anything. The next day, sure as his word a nurse attended to see Mum – bloods were taken and sent off. The next day we were called that evening by Dr Shah to say the results had not come back yet and he would call us the next day. That evening a Locum GP Called and said the bloods were elevated and we needed to go for a scan an appointment was made for 2 days later. That day, Dr Shah called to discuss Mums blood results, and I explained what had happened. Anyway, as a precautionary measure, a scan internally and Mum - no clot Dr Shah and all the staff, have always taken the time to listen carefully, explain everything clearly, and make sure we all felt reassured at every stage of Mums recovery. Nothing ever felt rushed and every concern — big or small — was treated with genuine care. It’s rare to find someone who combines medical expertise with such kindness and patience. Thanks to their guidance, my mum has felt safe, supported, and confident throughout her healing process. We are incredibly grateful for the dedication and humanity shown during what could have been a very stressful time. The team ALWAYS go above and beyond to make patients feel heard and supported and welcome, even during busy periods. They are exceedingly compassionate. The Practice is also great for reminding you that you need to see the nurses for check-ups and also medication reviews etc. Another point I wish to make is they have been great with Mum as she has smoked for 68 years, and the Practice now supports her with patches so to my amazement, she has not smoked for over 2 months The reception staff deserve special recognition too. Their kindness sets the tone from the moment you walk through the door. This review seems mainly to be about my Mums care at this difficult chapter in our lives but when I or any of family ever need to see the Doctors, everything is always made so easy with so much empathy. I have never in 44 years experienced anything negative from the Practice. Our Community Practice is a true example of what excellent healthcare should look like. Again, I’m incredibly grateful for the dedication and hard work of the entire team. I would 100% Highly recommended. My final thought… In a time when NHS services are under pressure, this practice stands out as a true asset to the area. I feel fortunate to have such exceptional care right on my doorstep. Thank you, Dr Shah and your Wonderful Team x,

recent_reviews.author: Neil Shepherd
recent_reviews.text: Avoid this practice if at all possible. I have been registered with the practice for 13 years and initially all was great. Currently, every time I have to deal with them, something goes wrong causing stress and anxiety when help is needed most. I was sent to get bloods elsewhere and when I attended the appointment I was told that the surgery should have given me some paperwork which they hadn't. I called in on my way home and was told "of course you need paperwork" as though it was my fault. The text they sent confirming the appointment stated I didn't need any paperwork. I wasn't even aware what the test was for as there was no other contact. They recently put me on medication for high blood pressure. Initially, the "GP" I saw put me on a drug which caused my ankles to swell so I asked if it could be changed. Their remote clinical pharmacist changed the drug but when I read the leaflet, it stated that it shouldn't be taken by anyone on anti-fungal medication, which I am. Another drug was prescribed and sent to a different pharmacy. When I went to the pharmacy stated, they said they hadn't got the prescription as it had been sent to another pharmacy which was closed, so I was without the medication for 3 days. I have been sent another appointment with the clinical pharmacist for next week. The times don't fit around my work so I called in to ask for a later call and was refused. Dr Archer agreed I could have a flu jab due my lung condition. An appointment was made for this on the same day I went for a kidney function blood test and I was told I could have it at the same time. The phlebotomist was about to take bloods for a test she had already done about 4 weeks ago until I told her it was a kidney function test and informed her that I had been told that I could have a flu jab at the same time. Her response wasn't good, but suffice to say she didn't do it stating that she was thinking of retiring due to the stress that the admin team were putting her under. I went to reception and was told "no, you can't have a flu jab as you're not old enough". I really do think that this practice has gone downhill which is a great shame as I used to sing the praises of all the staff. I hope Dr Archer reads this and takes some action as some of the staff are rude, ignorant, uncaring and more importantly following unsafe practices. Not what you want from a GP surgery. I am quite willing to discuss things further with him if he wishes to call me. I am currently looking for another practice hoping things will be better there. In the meantime, if I can be bothered I am seriously thinking about contacting CQC. Avoid Avoid Avoid

recent_reviews.author: PC Mumble
recent_reviews.text: I am updating my review because after speaking to various friends who visit other GP surgeries across Trafford, I appear to be quite lucky with Washway Road. My friends have awful problems getting someone to pick up a phone, they're always number 20+ in the queue, they can't get an appointment. I rarely have to wait to speak to a receptionist, they have some lovely ones who answer the phones these days, very helpful. I have had some very pleasant experiences and interactions with both admin staff and GPs over the last 6 months so I actually cannot complain. The AskMyGP system seems to work well now they have changed it to logging a request between 8 and 10, it's no longer a race to get your request in before it closes/gets full. The on site pharmacist is very good, he can resolve a lot of medication queries so you don't have to wait to see a GP. ******* GPs do not take women's pain seriously. Was ignored and told that 3 periods in a month was absolutely nothing to worry about and was offered a flu jab instead. Completely uninterested so had to go private and seek a second opinion. Currently recovering from a total hysterectomy inc. ovaries and removal of severe stage 4 endometriosis. I also had Adenomyosis. When I wrote to advise them of this, they couldn't even be bothered acknowledging me. This practice has gone totally downhill in the last year or so. Utter disgrace. Edit - it's worth noting this same review was rejected by the NHS website 'because it includes a serious complaint about a specific practice'. So do not trust their NHS review score.

recent_reviews.author: Abigail Awoyeye
recent_reviews.text: I had a very distressing experience at Medlock Medical Practice. I arrived on time for my blood test and waited as instructed, while several patients who arrived after me were seen first. After over 20 minutes, I calmly approached reception to ask for reassurance, as I was worried I had been forgotten. I am currently receiving treatment for anxiety and depression. Instead of reassurance, I was spoken to harshly and repeatedly called “rude” in front of other patients. English is not my first language, and I believe there was a misunderstanding, but my attempt to explain was dismissed. I was left feeling humiliated and extremely distressed and broke down in tears during my appointment. I would strongly encourage the practice to provide staff with additional training in compassionate communication, mental health awareness, and supporting patients with language barriers. Healthcare settings should feel safe and supportive, especially for vulnerable patients. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

recent_reviews.text: Made an appointment for 3.10pm yesterday (12th November 2025) arrived at 2.55pm in plenty of time which i always do. Spoke to the receptionist (not sure of her name) she advised me of what waiting room to go to. Half hour after my appointment. I'm still sitting there, watching people come in after me and being seen before me. I didn't want to leave the waiting are as I was on my own, just in case my name was called. 2 hours later (to which I think another patient may have informed the reception desk) I was still there. She asked me to the desk. To my knowledge I was booked in She told me I had been put down as a non attendee. Apologised, then said they had been having problems with the computer system. To which I said obviously not, its the person inputting/working the computer. As I had seen approximately 7-10 people arrive after me and go in before me. So to me that's not a computer error, its a human error. She said I would have to come back tomorrow. I said absolutely not as I work early mornings, and could the doctor see me now as he finishes his shift at 5pm (it was 4.50pm) absolute sham. Luckily, for them to basically save face, I imagine. The doctor said he would see me.

recent_reviews.author: Laura
recent_reviews.text: I would give less for the stress and anxiety the surgery caused me, but it doesn't seem to let me. If you need care, there is no point going here. The reception staff are lovely however the doctors, nurse practitioner don't seem to care whatsoever ever. In January after a visit to the GP I was given incorrect medication. After the issue was no better I went back, I was told by the GP the 1st GP was wrong. They gave me different medication. After 2 days and getting worse. I presented yo A&E and was kept on for 5nights. Being told each step of the way the GP was wrong. I should have been referred to podiatry on the first visit. The second I should have been sent to hospital... If I followed their guidance any further, I could have lost toes/feet. After hospital admission, I was sensitive to the medication so rang the GP to change it. They advised that technically I don't need medication anymore as I have had a course. Without even seeing me. But I did. That was my treatment plan from my discharge from hospital. This surgery completely exasperate medical conditions unnecessarily. It's almost like doctors don't care anymore.

recent_reviews.author: Anish
recent_reviews.text: I’ve recently joined New Islington Medical Practice as I started to take more responsibility for my health issues, which lingered over the years. I’ve had a 10/10 experience through every consultation and clinician I’ve encountered so far. The facilities are clean and modern, and the reception/back office staff have been very polite and prompt in responses. The new appointment booking system has been very efficient. Having many personal/professional experiences at other GP practices as a GP doctor myself - I have to say New Islington Medical Practice is by far one of the best that I’ve encountered within the region. The waiting times are optimal. I’ve had multiple health issues which have either been resolved or I am now receiving further support for. For sensitive issues, the clinicians are non-judgemental and empathetic in their approach which makes a huge difference. Kudos to Dee and management for their successes thus far and keep up the great work.

recent_reviews.author: Dannie J
recent_reviews.text: I've been here for my whole life, I used to give 1 star but I do believe some aspects of the surgery have changed in recent years which is why I changed to a 3. A lot of the doctors here are absolutely lovely and compassionate (especially with mental health) and I cannot fault them on how they have cared for me - for this I would like to give a special mention to Dr Graham and Dr Duncan (this could be due to how recent they qualified as a GP and there now being more awareness of mental health). For anything fertility related Dr Wareing is next to none also! Dr Heron I've struggled with for years due to past experiences and I will not see him, however in pregnancy he has been decent which shows he does take SOME things seriously and is willing to help. The prescription service is very fast and all of my repeats have normally been approved and sent within an hour of requesting. I thought the reception staff had improved over the last year or so however recently they have gone back downhill and are back to being the stereotypical NHS dragons on reception who refuse to help or even acknowledge you past 9.01am when the slots are full - I have even had a GP apologise for this! However it must be said that for me the real star of the show in primrose is Nurse Sharon! She is one of the most kind and compassionate people you could ever meet and I'm sure anyone who has ever crossed paths with her would agree!

recent_reviews.text: I contacted Primrose yesterday 19/11/2024, through askmygp. I told the surgery that I had strained my neck, shoulder and bicep carrying a TV box. I told them that I was in excruciating pain and that I was hardly getting any sleep and asked for help and that I needed to see a doctor and needed some sort of strong prescription medication. I got a call from there reception and told the caller that the pain I was experiencing was unbearable. She said she'd pass it on to 'the doctor' whoever that was supposed to be. Then I got a call back telling me that the 'doctor' wanted me to go for physio. I had politely stated how horrendous the pain was. Got told I'd get a call the following afternoon from their pharmacist. I couldn't go through another 24+ hours suffering this agony. So I went to TGH., walk- in clinic and was seen in & out within 1.5 hours, with strong pain killers and advised on three exercises to carry out. Primrose, in my opinion on this matter we're terrible. No empathy or help for my medical problem from primrose. Very dissatisfied on this occasion.

recent_reviews.author: Janet L
recent_reviews.text: Unacceptable and impersonal service especially when using the Ask My GP website. If these requests are not seen by clinicians how can patients be confident that the staff who are triaging them are sufficiently medically trained to judge whether a patient needs advice/help from a GP. I was advised by way of an impersonal on line response to an Ask My GP request to contact a pharmacy. When I did this I was then asked if I had contacted 111. How many hoops do patients have to jump through to be able to get help? Left in pain with a possible infection. It makes one wonder when you read media reports of patients who have ended up with sepsis or worse whether this is the right approach; I don't think so.

recent_reviews.author: Dan
recent_reviews.text: If I could give 0 stars if I could. I was born in Urmston and was at Urmston Group Practice til late teenage years, moved around and came back and signed back up. It's not the same doctors surgery that we used to know and love on Church Road. The receptionists need to go on a humility and compassion training course because their actions or there lack of are directly affecting peoples health and mental health. The receptionists also like to try and It seems to be a common theme that one or two of the receptionists (not all) do not seem to have any level of care or sympathy towards their patients. They forced me into crisis because I missed a phone appointment at 18:30 when my appointment was supposed to be 14:45. Apparently they tried to call me twice but number was dead. I know this to be untrue because not only did I not get any notifications that they tried to call but I also have a voicemail as well and they could have left a message. So when I call the next day )which was a friday) to find out what's happened and if I was going to have an appointment then rather than the one that didn't happen the day before. I was met with the usual "you've got to make an appointment, you'll have to call on monday" Despite the fact it was mental health tablets that I needed a review on, for them to use a poor excuse of "it didn't go through" when my phone is connected to wifi calls as well. I was so upset after it all I just told the woman if they aren't going to take me seriously I'll do something serious for them to take notice. No call back, no duty of care, no safeguarding, no making sure I wasn't going to do anything stupid. NOTHING. Then I received a very SNOTTY letter from the practice basically telling me off for saying what I said to the receptionist without even acknowledging that had they of cared or done their jobs, I wouldn't have been in meltdown mode and said what I said. So off the back of that, I have sent a complaint to them TWICE about the whole disgrace of a situation and I have yet to hear from them. Not even an acknowledgement. This review is my last hope that they see this and reply to me because if they don't then I'm going to go above their heads as it's becoming a joke at this point. Business are expected to acknowledge a complaint within 3 days and set out within that acknowledgement a time frame of when I should hear back from them. It's been months.

recent_reviews.author: vincent dean
recent_reviews.text: As someone with Autism, I don't enjoy Clarendon's surgery as a whole as I never feel like anyone actually cares, even the doctors, I'm just a ticket in a line to receive my pill, I've been trying to get an ADHD diagnosis, I've just completed the form and have spent 20 minutes going through my emails, looking on the website, which is just an organised mess, the contact us, doesn't even look like it has an email address, if I'm a low intelligence person fine, but the fact that your website is difficult to navigate to simply send an email is disgusting, I hope I'm just missing something simple, i can't even call in to book an appointment as it's done online, Clarendons is a prime example of how the NHS just makes it difficult to receive healthcare in the UK
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: vincent dean8 reviews2 months ago As someone with Autism, I don't enjoy Clarendon's surgery as a whole as I never feel like anyone actually cares, even the doctors, I'm just a ticket in a line to receive my pill, I've been trying to get an ADHD diagnosis, I've just completed the form and have spent 20 minutes going through my emails, looking on the website, which is just an organised mess, the contact us, doesn't even look like it has an email address, if I'm a low intelligence person fine, but the fact that your website is difficult to navigate to simply send an email is disgusting, I hope I'm just missing something simple, i can't even call in to book an appointment as it's done online, Clarendons is a prime example of how the NHS just makes it difficult to receive healthcare in the UKLike Share Response from the owner 2 months agoDear Mr Dean Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. We are genuinely sorry to hear how frustrating and upsetting your experience has felt. We recognise that navigating healthcare systems can be particularly challenging for patients who are neurodivergent, and feeling unheard or unsupported is never what we want for our patients. We are sorry if our website has been difficult to navigate. Our website is regularly reviewed by Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (GM ICB) to ensure it meets accessibility standards; however, we understand that “accessible” does not always mean easy to use for everyone. We are currently reviewing alternative website providers to see how we can further improve clarity, navigation, and ease of contact. All our Doctors appointment requests are triaged by a GP to ensure patients are directed to the most appropriate clinician based on clinical need. We encourage patients to use our online consultation forms where possible, as these go directly to the duty doctor and support timely responses. However, online access is not the only option. Patients who are unable to, or prefer not to, submit requests online can telephone the practice, where a receptionist will complete the form on their behalf, or attend the surgery in person to receive support face to face. Please note that our phone lines are extremely busy, and waiting times inevitably increase when reception staff are assisting patients with completing forms, but this support remains available. All triage requests are reviewed and responded to within 24 hours via the contact method chosen by the patient. With regard to ADHD referrals, the specialist service is unable to accept referrals without a completed screening questionnaire being returned, as this is a requirement of the service. There is usually an option to return the completed form via an available link included in the accompanying text message, (valid for five days). We do however, appreciate the difficulty you have described and have taken this feedback on board. Going forward, we will also ensure that a return email address is clearly included within the message to provide an alternative way of responding. If you need further help or would like to discuss your concerns in more detail, our Reception Manager would be happy to assist and can be contacted via the surgery. We also have a dedicated Care Coordinator who can also support patients who need additional help accessing our systems. We also have an active Patient Participation Group (PPG), which meet regularly to share feedback, discuss patient experiences, and explore ways we can improve our services. We would welcome your engagement, and the Reception Manager can provide further information or help you get involved if this is something you would like to pursue. Thank you again for taking the time to share your experience. Your feedback is important to us and helps us continue to improve the care we provide.

recent_reviews.author: Humairaa Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: Had an appointment today at 11:40 for an ultrasound scan which I had to have a full bladder for. I took a taxi to the place but as the taxi driver went the wrong way, by the time I got through to the centre was 11:43 and I explained to the receptionist that I’ll be 5 minutes. She said that was fine. I arrived at 11:50 and sat in the waiting area waiting for my ultrasound. When I arrived, was only 1 woman I saw go in and come out 10 minutes later. After that it was just me sitting there waiting. Nearly 20 minutes had gone by so I ask the receptionist. She said I am half an hour late and how I said I’ll be 5 minutes and that they won’t see me , even though I walked in passed reception at 11:50 to sit in the waiting area which was by the ultrasound scan room. I explained myself. Then she said okay just continue waiting. 25 minutes later the person at the ultrasound came out for me and explained how I’m too late and she can’t fit me in. Even though I’m the only one there and have been for the past 35 minutes. She said she’s been calling for me. No one called for me at all whilst I was there. Whatever I was telling her wasn’t going through to her at all. So after sitting there for nearly 45 minutes on a full bladder that I’ve had for 2 hours, I got sent home and a phone call after to re arrange. No thanks I would rather not have the scan anymore to find the issue of what’s making me ill rather than dealing with people like this. And bare in mind whilst I was waiting, one woman kept coming in and out of the room ‘checking around’ but never called my name or spoke to me. Wish I could give this place 0 stars

recent_reviews.text: This was my first visit to this GP clinic with my daughter, who was unwell. Unfortunately, the clinic has no parking, and nearby street parking is limited to 30 minutes. We had to park further away and ended up arriving 10 minutes late. Despite explaining the situation, they told us there was a strict 10-minute late policy and refused to see us. I had never heard of this rule before, and it was not communicated clearly beforehand. We were only referred to this clinic because our original GP had no availability, and the experience was extremely disappointing. I felt there was a lack of flexibility and compassion, especially towards a sick child. I would not recommend this clinic to parents or anyone who might require understanding and timely care.

The practice manager is never on site to raise a complaint to and told to put in writing which I have and never got a reply from Patrick neither. I am going to have to transfer out as the care we are receiving is very concerning if I can not get my monthly medication at time when requested in time frame. The Reception team seem to be new and need training on how to request a prescription or get competent staff. This is a shame because for the past many years I have always been cared for and not had many issues as I know mistakes do happen, but this surgery has gone down hill.

recent_reviews.author: Jeremiah Agenyi
recent_reviews.text: I am disappointed with the level of service I have received from Mocha Parade Medical Practice. I visited their center to get registered when I first arrived in the UK, and they promised to get back to me in a few days. However, I did not hear from them after two weeks, so I reached out to them. They said that they could not find my records and asked me to register again. I did so, but I still did not hear back from them after another two to three weeks. When I contacted them again, they said that my records had been misplaced. I then submitted my records online, but it has been almost three months and I have still not heard back from them. I am concerned about the level of care I will receive if I need medical attention from this practice. I am also disappointed with the lack of communication and the apparent negligence of the staff. I would not recommend this practice to anyone.

recent_reviews.text: Visited today for the first time for a small procedure with a District Nurse. The Doctors Surgery reception staff very politely redirected me to the correct area of the building and I was dealt with in a friendly and caring manner. The Nurse went above and beyond in caring for my needs and the District Nurse Receptionist could not have been more helpful in finding me another appropriate appointment. The building and waiting areas were very clean and tidy and the free Car Park next to the building , which isn't the case at many doctors, was a blessing in the rain, as was the easy to use tablet device to register your vehicle for the parking pass. I wouldn't want to judge some of the previous comments as everyone can have a bad day and ill health can affect perceptions, but I've been to a lot worse Surgeries, this was a pleasure to visit today.

Around 15 minutes later the doctor tried calling me but unfortunately my phone was in silent so I never heard the calls.. I thought the receptionist told me she had finished for the day?? I have no complaints at the doctor they are directed at the receptionist who was very rude and made it extremely difficult for me and has left me now with no appointment and I am very unimpressed and unhappy!

Please could AD contact the practice manager with specific details, - we do have a formal complaints process - then we can look into this properly. Many thanks. Dr Davis

recent_reviews.author: Eugene Friday
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely ridiculous experience. Unprofessional staff. Arrived 10 mins early for my appoitment which was supposed to be 10:40 am, only to discover that their free parking was completely full, forcing me to find a paid parking elsewhere. I paid for 30 mins until 11:05 am but I wasn't called in the given timeframe. Thus, I had to extend my parking. I immediately informed the receptionist and asked them to let the doctor know that I needed extra few minutes to extend my parking. But they dismissed my notice and informed the receptionist that they wouldn't wait and asked to book a new appointment. Instead of showing basic courtesy, they just refused to wait extra couple of minutes, despite the fact that they were 25 mins running behind. So somehow it's acceptable for them to be late but the patients get penalised for circumstances entirely out of their control. If you expect punctuality, maybe start by managing your schedule and facilities properly. I won't be returning and wouldn't recommend this medical practice to anyone.

recent_reviews.text: I would like to express my sincere thanks and appreciation to all the staff and respected doctors for their great effort and dedicated work. recent_reviews.text: I left my GP appointment feeling terrible, after seeing Dr Afsheen Aasma. I also received a message from the practice advising me to contact a doctor regarding my results which was the reason for this visit. I expected compassion and support, but instead felt judged and ignored. I walked out feeling worse than when I arrived — so disheartened that I don’t even want to go back. recent_reviews.author: khalil zeria
recent_reviews.text: I would like to share some positive feedback about my surgery. The doctors there are good but could do better with patient care and understanding. My go-to GP is Dr. Bukhari. He truly stands out to me—always welcoming with a smile, attentive, and genuinely focused on helping me improve my health and overall quality of life. While some doctors insist on addressing only one issue per appointment, they could take a leaf out of Dr. Bukhari's book—he's always willing to listen and help with multiple medical concerns, showing true dedication to patient care. The nurses working in the practice are genuinely compassionate and attentive, always showing kindness and care in their approach. The reception and phone staff are always friendly and helpful. They do their best to assist within the limits of what they’re able to do. The practice also benefits from having an in-house pharmacy, which is incredibly convenient and valuable for patients. Additionally, the surgery has expanded by opening a secondary site to accommodate the increasing number of patients. I see this as a thoughtful and proactive step to ensure continued quality care. Areas that need improvement. 1. Phone service needs changing. 2. More availability on appointments. 3. Rather than operating as two separate entities, the surgery and the pharmacy should work in closer partnership to better support patients and provide a more seamless, integrated level of care. 4. Parking issues, but I guess that's down to location. All in all, a big thumbs up to the surgery for their commitment and service.

Unfortunately this was the case for multiple patients that were booked into the GP yesterday. recent_reviews.text: Called at 8:00 for a doctors appointment, waited for 40 minutes and my call was not answered, just kept ringing. Poor services like these make healthcare inaccessible and make people less inclined to seek medical help. Other reviews highlight similar issues with waiting times after initiating the call well over 1 hour 30 minutes and still no answer. CQC should be informed, this service is under par and negligent.

recent_reviews.text: Extremely poor service. They said they’d book me a telephone appointment and called the completely wrong day that they told me, they don’t respond to prescription queries, the practice itself looks extremely run down. There’s a lack of efficiency and care from this practice and everyone I’ve spoken to about it has had similar or if not worse experience to mine. I personally would avoid if you can and try going elsewhere

It is disappointing to hear that you have said that you had to wait on hold for so long on the phone. I am not sure how this happened as the lines time out a lot sooner than that. We have more than the recommended staff required to answer the phones, however with a combined registered patient list of just under 17,000 patients, it is understandable that there will be some parts of the day that are more busy than others. If you feel this way again, please get the name of the person you are speaking to and record the time and date.
