recent_reviews.author: ENGLISH WITH SABBIR
recent_reviews.text: Terrible Experience at NHS GP Practice The Absolute Worst I am writing this review to express my extreme dissatisfaction with Dr. Parkin's NHS GP practice. This practice is, without a doubt, the worst healthcare experience I've ever had. Here's a list of my grievances: Unbelievably Long Wait Times: Getting an appointment is a nightmare. Even after securing one, expect to wait in the waiting room. Unprofessional Doctors: I've had appointments with various doctors , and none have instilled confidence. They seem unconcerned about my health problems. I would recommend looking for alternative GP practices in the area. There must be better options out there with qualified professionals who genuinely care about their patients' well-being. If you're looking for a GP experience that will leave you feeling more unwell than when you arrived, then NHS is the place for you! Buckle up, because this is a tale of woe. Getting There is an Odyssey: Firstly, reaching a human to book an appointment is an act of pure masochism. The phone lines are permanently engaged in a game of dial tone torture, and the online system is about as user-friendly as a medieval trebuchet. Finally, you're ushered into the office. Prepare for a five-minute consultation. Don't expect in-depth examinations or thoughtful diagnoses. Here, a generic prescription pad are your only companions. I understand that the NHS is under a lot of strain, but that doesn't excuse the unprofessional and unacceptable service.

recent_reviews.author: Amelia A
recent_reviews.text: I brought my daughter for an appointment and we were kept waiting 30 minutes past our scheduled time. When we were finally called in, we were then left to stand in silence for another 5 minutes while doctor Hassan typed notes from previous patients. While still typing and without making eye contact or examining my daughter, he asked why we were there. When I explained it was for a spot on her leg and that she’d had it for a few months, he immediately made a judgment and said it “must not be much of an issue” if we’d waited that long. He also commented that “they will ask why you haven’t brought her in for months” without explaining who “they” were, and before he had even looked at the spot. Only after making these remarks did he finally examine her leg and then told us it wasn’t serious and to return in two weeks with warm compresses. My concern isn’t the medical advice itself it’s the rude, dismissive, and judgmental manner, particularly when speaking to a parent about their child. Unfortunately, this is not an isolated experience. We have experienced similar rudeness from this doctor on multiple occasions. Between the repeated unprofessional behaviour, poor communication, and lack of respect for patients’ time, this is not a practice I feel comfortable bringing my children to, and I would not recommend it to other parents.

recent_reviews.author: L B
recent_reviews.text: GP's and Nurses are brilliant. Always friendly and easy to talk to. Both nurses I've seen there have been bubbly, happy and chatty and put me at ease, even when having a cervical screening :') One of the reception staff comes across very rude on the phone at times which isn't great when you're ringing up about mental health issues. She has at other times when I've physically been in the surgery been fantastic and extremely helpful. I can sympathise with them to an extent as they must get a lot of abuse but it shouldn't be pushed onto others. When you're physically in the building though they're all spot on. Struggle to get through and get appointments if you don't keep trying to ring at 08:00. They do seem to have introduced a phone queuing system which helps massively. With there only being a limited amount of appointments I think the reception staff need to be firmer in turning time wasters away and directing them to the correct place (pharmacy/a&e/self care). Also, they should tell people who repeatedly don't attend their appointments and dont have the decency to advise reception they will be struck off if they don't have a valid reason. Surgery is bright, airy and clean. Chairs could do with being spread out a bit more in my opinion but I'm claustrophobic so perhaps a bit biased. Overall, best doctors surgery I've been too in Heywood and I would recommend. All surgeries seem equally difficult to get appointments so can't hold that against them. As for the occasionally rude receptionist, this is just my experience and how I perceive something that's been said and that will differ from person to person. We all have bad days, we're only human :)

recent_reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed with the standard of care I have received from this surgery. I was issued a sick note and sent on my way .I left the appointment feeling worse than when I arrived. I was later referred for further care however, this referral was not completed for several months because the doctor was reportedly off sick and no alternative arrangements were made. I find this particularly concerning, as I received a message from the receptionist regarding the referral shortly after the initial appointment, yet no action followed. Overall, the lack of compassion, poor communication, and delays in care have been distressing. I would strongly advise anyone who needs medical support to consider a different practice. recent_reviews.author: Martha Beatriz Potter
recent_reviews.text: I'm writing this review as a frustrated patient who's had a shocking experience with this practice's service. I phoned at 8am and waited 25-30 minutes just to get an answer. I explained my situation - my consultant had asked them to prescribe more antibiotics for my lung disease, which makes any cold or flu linger and often leads to infections, making me cough uncontrollably and causing incontinence. It's a nightmare. The response seemed straightforward when I spoke to them, but then I got a call an hour later saying I needed to fill in an online form to be triaged. A nice lady helped me with this, but then... nothing. I phoned again at 2pm, was told they'd contact me, and... crickets. It's now 6:47pm. The worst part? This isn't the first time this has happened. I've ended up in A&E twice because their system is so appalling, and both times I've been told "this is something the GP deals with". I rarely use their service, but when I do, it's usually to be told to go to A&E or a walk-in centre. It's infuriating. To anyone considering using this practice, be warned: their system is broken, and it might end up costing you a trip to hospital. Not exactly what you want when you're already feeling well.

recent_reviews.author: Barry
recent_reviews.text: Having recently had a medical issue whilst abroad I was advised to contact my Medical Practice at home. I have been a patient at Greenbank since the 1960s fortunately I have not had to attend on a regular basis however I was pleased to be given a prompt appointment and saw a doctor who was most pleasant and professional and was able to fully interpret the advice I had received whilst abroad. She arranged for me to have an ECG which was done within a week at Greenbank by an equally pleasant and professional person. The results of the ECG were conveyed to me later that day by the the doctor who saw me initiallly and she organised for me to see a specialist at Oldham Hospital within days. I remember that a few years ago I read in the local paper a review of the Greenbank Practice which was rather poor, however after contacting Greenbank I was given the opportunity, a few weeks later, to meet with the leader of the group who had produced that report which illustrated how easy it is to criticise particularly over petty issues. The second follow up report a few months later recognised the true value of the Greenbank practice and the practice was marked up as Good. I have also had recent visits to see the physio at Greenbank with my slight hip problem and again I received prompt and professional help. My golf is just as bad however my hip is on the mend.

recent_reviews.author: John Gardner
recent_reviews.text: As I approach my 79th summer, I seem to pop more pills than a 1960’s Rolling Stones roadie. Which takes quite a bit of organising in terms of ordering them from my local surgery to keep the supply line flowing. When it comes to being business-like in such matters, on a scale of 1-10, one being chaotic and ten being hyper-efficient, I probably clock in at something like minus 5. That is in contrast to the present Mrs Gardner, who could probably re-organise Manchester United in the morning and the England cricket team in the afternoon. Anyway, the New Year being what it was, I thought I had ordered two sets of tablets from Leesbrook surgery at the dawn of 2026 when the evidence indicates that, in point of fact, I hadn’t. Doh! When this dawned on me earlier today, panic set in for I had consumed my very last Solifenacin tablet last night. We are warned to give plenty of notice when re-ordering prescriptions, particularly at this time of year when the whole NHS is so stretched. So imagine my surprise, delight and admiration when my hasty message to Leesbrook surgery was answered immediately. Together with the ever helpful staff at Well Pharmacy, they arranged for me to have the required medication in my hands this very afternoon. Thank you once again for your brilliant service. Happy New Year from John Gardner

recent_reviews.author: Stacey MacNaught
recent_reviews.text: I appreciate that GP services are incredibly stretched and it can be very difficult to balance offering in advance routine appointments with more urgent on the day appointments. I think this surgery, however, is striking the balance well. The last 3 times I’ve required fairly urgently assessing, I was seen on the same day and treated. Early on this year, after a bout of pneumonia, I suffered a follow up chest infection. I was seen the same day, prescribed antibiotics and the doctor sent a sample from my chest off for testing. I got a call a few days later saying the bacteria on my chest wasn’t the commonly found one and as such would not respond to the antibiotics I was given and he had sent a new prescription to the pharmacy. So instead of seeing me, prescribing something and leaving me to it, the Doctor has followed up, sought more information and then realised my treatment would need changing. Despite the huge time constraints they’re under, they’re still doing a thorough job. I was again recently seen the same day with another potentially urgent requirement. The surgery also now accepts appointment request forms - categorised as urgent and non urgent so you don’t have to wait on the phone. Trying to get through on the phones can be frustrating for sure. But this is, in my view, a Solid example of a clinic that does the best with the resources it has, despite huge patient loads. And doesn’t cut corners on healthcare just to save time. Thorough, understanding and incredibly hard working is my experience of the admin and medical staff I’ve encountered here.

recent_reviews.author: Michael Keating
recent_reviews.text: I felt that my health problems were dismissed and was disappointed and frustrated with the consultation overall. I had registered with the surgery for the GP to consider shared care protocol for ADHD medication prescribed and monitored by a private company I have paid for monthly since January 2025. I'd been advised by the receptionist prior to registering that this would at the least be considered. During my first consultation I was told indefinitely that the practice had a 'blanket rule' against prescribing in this manner. I would have accepted that, as I did with my previous practice, however I feel I was then delivered misinformation that was disheartening and upsetting. The GP told me that 'these private companies will give anybody a diagnosis of ADHD', something which I feel particularly upset and frustrated by. I know for a fact, as a specialist nurse for psychiatry working in primary care that there are many people referred for an ADHD assessment that are not diagnosed but offered alternatives and private companies will make recommendations based on valuable assessments that patients benefit from regardless. For a medical professional to deliver this false information can be especially damaging to somebody in my position, having waited years and paid excessively for support with. I, like many other service users have found relief and in the very least been validated by a diagnosis of ADHD which has answered a lot of questions and provided a pathway to improved wellbeing and hope for the future. The GP also stated that these private companies do not offer a true 'shared care' approach, and that if there are any problems with prescribing in primary care there is no support available from them. I know that this is also false as I have been instructed to remain under the care of the private company and pay for six monthly reviews from the specialists working alongside primary services to ensure safe prescribing and management of medications. The GP also attempted to misinform me that private companies prescribe medications without ensuring safe titration and effective physical health monitoring. Again, I know for a fact that I was sufficiently monitored in terms of bloods, ECG and regular blood pressure and weight reviews since being diagnosed with ADHD in January 2025. In summary, I feel Albion Medical Group have been negligent and failed to deliver individualised care based on service user need. Not only that, but many of the false statements assumed by the GP could have been particularly damaging to vulnerable people with a diagnosis of ADHD, further marginalising people like myself trying to seek support for this disability. If the surgery have a 'blanket rule' against considering shared care protocols for ADHD medication, they should at least ensure the GP's are better informed and work harder not to further dismiss and discredit patients already struggling to access safe support and guidance.

recent_reviews.author: Ali Channa
recent_reviews.text: I have never experienced such an unprofessional and shocking service from any GP practice in my life. Little Town Medical Practice is an absolute joke. We booked an appointment and had to wait three weeks just to be seen – that alone is ridiculous. When I finally arrived for my appointment, I signed in and waited 40–50 minutes past the scheduled time. I became impatient because the appointment time had clearly passed. I asked the receptionist, who told me to “wait another 5–10 minutes and the doctor will see you soon.” After waiting another 10 minutes, she then told me I needed to come back four hours later at 3:30pm. What a joke. I had children to pick up from school, so attending four hours later was impossible. I asked if I could be booked in for the following week instead, and I was told they had no availability at all for the next two weeks. Completely unacceptable and honestly disgusting. To make matters worse, while I was there another patient was arguing with staff because the doctor refused to see her child despite them having an appointment as well. That alone shows this GP treats multiple patients the same way. This is not the first bad experience either. On previous occasions the staff have been extremely rude. When complaining over the phone in the past, I was told things like: “Why don’t you change GP?” “Why don’t you move out of Oldham?” Disgusting attitude. Completely unprofessional. Shows clearly that this GP surgery does not care at all about its patients. Little Town Medical Practice needs serious improvement. People rely on their GP for their health and wellbeing, and this kind of treatment is shameful. I would not recommend this surgery to anyone.

Patients are not expecting special treatment — simply reasonable accessibility, particularly when prompted to make contact. I hope that moving forward the focus remains on improving accessibility rather than questioning patient expectations. Kind regards,Natasha

recent_reviews.author: Imthiyaz Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: I am slightly disheartened by the number of negative reviews for this GP. However, my experience is mainly positive. It is somewhat hard to get a hold of an appointment that is needed immediately, but that's the case everywhere. At my latest appointment just over a week ago, I called quite a lot of times over the span of 20 mins, but I could get an appointment for later that day at 3:30 pm. My other issue for that appointment is that the receptionist wasn't present, leaving me and another patient who was there prior to me for waiting for him for at least 5 mins while not attending to anyone in particular . For all my appointments over the past year (4 appointments, which is quite a lot for me), doctors and asthma nurse were respectful, professional, well-mannered, understanding, and informative about my conditions. Dr Butt even told me about the Manchester Access Programme, which was very helpful, and I'm currently part of 👍🏽. (I'd also be incredibly grateful if the practice allowed me to do work experience (shadowing) at the practice. However, the last time I checked, the receptionist told me they're not taking anyone 😭.)

recent_reviews.author: Ayanna
recent_reviews.text: I am writing to formally raise serious concerns about the continued poor standard of care and service I have experienced at your practice, which has now reached an unacceptable level. I had a telephone appointment scheduled for today at 10:00 AM to discuss blood test results I have been waiting over two weeks for. The doctor called but let the phone ring for barely a second—so briefly that my phone did not even make a sound before the call ended. This happened twice. By the time I looked at my screen, both calls had already disconnected. It appears these calls were made purely to be logged as “missed” without any genuine effort to reach me. This is not the first time this has happened. During my previous set of blood tests, I experienced the exact same issue with the same doctor. It is becoming a pattern, and I feel unfairly blamed for missing calls that I was never given a fair chance to answer. I contacted reception immediately after the missed calls and was told by one receptionist that the doctor would call me again by 3:00 PM. I waited all afternoon and received no call. When I followed up again, a different receptionist informed me that I would now need to wait until Monday to rebook the appointment. This lack of consistency and the conflicting information from staff is extremely frustrating and unprofessional. Had I been advised at the time of my first call this morning that it was unlikely I would receive a call back, I would have rescheduled immediately while appointments were still available. Instead, I have been left waiting all day, only to be told I now need to start the process again next week. This entire experience follows an already distressing and, frankly, concerning blood test appointment. During the test, the nurse attempted to draw blood from my left arm but was unsuccessful. She then inserted the same needle into my right arm, again unsuccessfully, and a third time into another site using the same needle. I was left with severe bruising due to how aggressive the procedure was. Afterwards, I looked into this and was shocked to learn that reusing the same needle for multiple injection sites is not in line with health and safety regulations. I find it deeply troubling that this occurred, and it has left me feeling not only physically hurt but also incredibly unsafe in your care. All of this is part of a larger issue I have faced at this practice: I have repeatedly had to fight to have my symptoms taken seriously, and even getting basic follow-up care feels like a battle. The reception staff regularly provide conflicting, inaccurate, or vague advice, which only adds to the confusion and stress. At this point, I feel neglected and disrespected as a patient. I will be looking into registering with another GP practice, as I feel the standard of care at this one has significantly declined during my time here. I hope this matter is taken seriously, as it relates not just to poor service, but to potential breaches in clinical safety and patient care standards

recent_reviews.text: I’ve had a consistently positive experience with this GP practice. Appointments and communication have been reliable, and the staff are professional and kind. I especially want to mention Dr Galvis, who is outstanding - compassionate, thorough, and someone who genuinely listens. I never feel rushed, and everything is explained clearly with a thoughtful plan moving forward. I’m really grateful for the care and would highly recommend this practice. Dr Galvis has honestly had such a positive impact on my life. I spent years struggling with my mental health and not feeling properly understood in the past, but Dr Galvis approaches care in a truly thoughtful and creative way. The first time she “prescribed” me a book to read I was sceptical, but it ended up meaning so much more to me than being given prescription tablets with little explanation or support. She’s also given me the confidence and tools to move forward - to the point that I’m now going back to university to train to become a dentist. Thank you, Dr Galvis.

recent_reviews.author: Jeanette Neilson
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this practice since moving to Gatley 28 years ago. Both my children , now adults were cared for at Gatley medical practice and the same for my husband and I. In our current climate of underfunding and lack of resources this practice continues to provide an excellent and exceptional service to its patients. I have always got through to the practice and have managed to get an appointment 99% of the time. Reception staff have been helpful and friendly. I have always been treated with courtesy and dignity having a long-term condition. I do think people should be realistic. Use the pharmacy or 111 for advice. Urgent problems go to ED. The practice is not a walk in and expectations that someone should get a same day appointment then get annoyed because they can't is unfair on an already over stretched service doing their best for the local community. Its a 10/10 from me. Thank you Gatley Medical Centre

recent_reviews.author: Helisa Bagheri
recent_reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed with the service at this GP practice. Over the years, both my children and I have been misdiagnosed multiple times, leading to serious consequences for our health. One particularly alarming experience involved a senior GP dismissing my concerns about perimenopausal symptoms. Despite expressing that I suspected I was entering perimenopause, she laughed and told me I was too young, completely disregarding that perimenopause can occur at various ages. She prescribed me the wrong medication, which worsened my symptoms to the point that I almost ended up in a mental health crisis.When I reported this to her, she casually offered antidepressants and didn’t even arrange a follow-up to check on my well-being. I had to take matters into my own hands and consult a private GP, who immediately confirmed I was perimenopausal and prescribed HRT. My symptoms improved almost instantly. This kind of negligence is unacceptable, and I have completely lost trust in this practice. I’ve even witnessed doctors Googling information in front of me, which makes me wonder—why bother going to the GP if I can just look things up myself? It seems they are only useful for minor issues like colds or flu. I would not recommend trusting them with anything beyond that.

recent_reviews.author: Sabina
recent_reviews.text: I went for a dermatology appointment at Handforth Health Centre. From the moment I entered the door, I found the personnel not very helpful. Then, I was taken by a very unpleasant nurse (of Asian origin, I think) to see my dermatologist. She was very moody and stayed with me during the appointment. I came with a mole I was worried about, so the dermatologist suggested checking all my other moles. However, I needed to take off my clothes in front of him without any separate curtains for privacy. The nurse was sitting on a chair next to the door in the meantime during all apointment. I felt really rushed taking my clothes off and throughout the entire appointment. Then, when the dermatologist finished the examination, I wanted to ask a few questions, but after my second question, the nurse opened the door to signal that the appointment was over and I had to leave. I have never experienced anything like that with the NHS or any medical organization anywhere in the world. It was an absolutely horrible experience.

recent_reviews.text: I had been told by a friend that St Johns was one of the very few surgeries that was doing something to find out if Statins would suit you. So I called them re this. Then at 7pm same day, Vanessa, the Practice Manager called me and said there had been a trial running that looked into this, and the trial was ending the next day. So she agreed to put me down for it and next day I took part in the trial. So its great that St Johns is taking part in such initiatives, and I was hugely grateful to Vanessa for calling me well outside normal surgery times and booking me onto the trial, that too in a Christmas Week. Very impressive and Well Done!

recent_reviews.author: Simon G
recent_reviews.text: Some good and bad experiences here. Was seen last year by a female doctor here who diagnosed me with anxiety and depression. I was referred for CBT treatment. The therapist, after many hours of talking therapy suggested that I may be suffering from a neurodiversity condition. I mentioned this to my GP on my next check in and was practically laughed at. The response was basically that we all experience these symptoms. I was embarrassed and didn’t raise the issue again. I was placed on a high dose of anti depressants and sent on my way. I’ve now stopped the medication abruptly as I am still experiencing the same problems - withdrawal is hell but I have no desire to return to this GP to revisit what was discussed with my therapist and have nowhere else to turn. Looking to transfer to a new GP to get the help I need

recent_reviews.author: Chuanjie Zhou
recent_reviews.text: I have great concerns about this medical centre, and I have no issue with doctors, but their reception team was very rude. You will never expect them to give you a smile. We have made an urgent appointment 9 am today for our granddaughter, who has had a bad cough with a running nose. We arrived at the medical centre 9:10am and at that time only one receptionist attended, but was continuously using the phone. We were waiting patiently for over five minutes until she finished her phone call. Then she told us that the appointment was invalid because we missed the appointment by over 15minutes. We tried to argue with her that we arrived at 9:10 am and the appointment should be valid. Suddenly, five receptionists appeared at the reception desk, showing a very aggressive manner, and one of the receptionists even threatened to call the police. I have to say, this reception team is arrogant, rude, and has a total lack of empathy for the patients. The management team should look into restructuring the reception team! I have checked all 53 Google reviews of this medical centre, and 26 out of 53 were one star, with an average score of 2.6. So far, this 2.6 score is the lowest within Greater Manchester that I have ever seen. 16 of 53 were complaints about their receptionists, which should tell you something!

I have always felt that they actually enjoyed their profession. My friends based in other surgeries can't believe the help I get from my doctors. The office manager is very capable; some of the receptionists can be a bit unpolished but generally, the service at the desk is very good. The building is clean and welcoming. Parking is not always easy but arriving a good 10 minutes before the appointment can help as people come but also vacate quite quickly.

recent_reviews.author: Kong Ng
recent_reviews.text: We have always been with this GP under our postcode area (WA14/15), but they changed their catchment area quietly without any notice. Suddenly, we were no longer within their coverage. When my wife needed to see a doctor, the NHS app still allowed her to book an appointment. However, when she arrived, instead of being asked about her symptoms, the first question was, “Why are you here at this GP?” As an organisation responsible for safeguarding the health of local residents, it is disappointing that they chose to turn away an unwell patient rather than provide care and then explain that her address is no longer within their service area.

recent_reviews.author: Jenny
recent_reviews.text: Monday, 27th October I spoke to Sara at 08:12 I said I would like to book an appointment for my husband Roger. He had difficulty breathing and his peakflow was very low, and a back cough.She said I can't book a telephone appointment. She said I had to book online which I did. I requested a telephone call after 12pm. I also requested that they phone Roger on his home landlines as he doesn't have a smart phone. I received a reminder message showing up on phone at 17:00 saying can Roger come in today to the surgery at 15:20 Luckily my husband phoned the surgery at 11:15 to remind them to use the landlines and luckily he found out the appointment was in person and he was able to go in good time. The fact that I had no knowledge of the appointment to 17:00 meant my husband would have missed his appointment had he not phoned the surgery at 11:15

recent_reviews.author: Kal Chudasama
recent_reviews.text: Patient Feedback I have been with the practice for around 36 years and have seen many changes over time, especially with staff turnover — particularly among receptionists, where there seems to be a high turnover and a lack of consistency. The doctors have also changed in recent years, but the current team is very good. I have spoken to and been seen by various GPs, and I appreciate that treatment options are always explained thoroughly, including both the pros and cons. It’s reassuring that I can always speak to a doctor over the phone when needed, and face-to-face or out-of-hours appointments are available upon request. However, I feel that out-of-hours appointments are not well-promoted, and more awareness should be raised around this service. Despite the many changes, the care and quality from the MSK team, doctors, and nurses remain consistently high. Prescription requests made via the app are handled promptly and sent quickly to my nominated pharmacy, which is very efficient. I have given 3 stars due to the attitude of some of the receptionists, which has impacted my overall experience. Suggestions and Areas for Improvement: 1. I would like the option to speak directly with a practice manager or someone in a managerial position in person to address any issues, without the need to email or raise a formal complaint. 2. Some reception staff could improve their communication and approach with patients. On one occasion, I went to collect my medical records and had a phone appointment booked to discuss results. The GP called during my work hours, and when I called the surgery back to explain, the receptionist was dismissive and defensive. I was told the receptionist who made the booking was in training, but the conversation lacked empathy and professionalism. This needs to be addressed to ensure better patient interactions. 3. I would like the ability to book appointments via the app again, as I was previously able to do. It would be great if the surgery could look into reinstating this feature. 4. Where possible, it would be helpful to have continuity by seeing or speaking to the same GP consistently. Lastly, I do appreciate the improved phone queue system — it’s a noticeable improvement compared to before.

recent_reviews.author: Kasper MB
recent_reviews.text: Consider the fact I booked a blood test because I had my own concerns about something. After my blood was taken I was told it would take 7 days for the results with a day I received two text message one telling me to book an appointment with a health improvement practitioner and not requesting me to book a second blood test. When I called the office the automated message ask me to call after 3pm for blood test results when I called after 3pm I was told I had to call at 8am to book a doctors appointment to speak about my blood test results. So the automated message was misinformation and what's more I still had not been told why I needed a second blood test. The reception insisted they didn't know why and I should speak to the doctor however they still expected me to book a second blood test I informed them several times I didn't have time for this yet they failed to understand why I was annoyed about being asked to do something without being informed why, especially as this is about my blood test, for which I already had concern is about and this was my time the fact I am the patient and have the right to be informed about my own health and what is happening with my blood seems to evaded this office. Furthermore I received a phone call hours later insisting I was to book a second blood test, totally ignoring my previous conversation, even more ride this was by way of phone call one a withheld number, why does the doctor need to hide its phone number? Ridiculous! It gets worse because all this was on Friday and Monday afternoon yes I received another call from doctors office on a withheld number telling me I must book another blood test once again without informing exactly why this was needed! Terrible treatment of patient and total lack of respect for what I previously explained, I was busy but that didn't matter just pestering me, so yes I spent 60 pounds in taxi to get to the doctors and have a second blood test still unaware of what happened to my first test. And when I asked what was happening with the second one I was told I had to book an appointment to speak to the doctor I'd that after 3pm or 8am? Why is it so difficult to gey an answer and be informed I went from being concerned to not wanting to know well atleast the doctors has satisfied thier curiosity about my blood and my health and I guess I'll to wait two weeks to discover why I need to speak to a health care improving specialist, Terrible experience.

recent_reviews.author: Stoobhoy MacanAba
recent_reviews.text: My experience of this surgery has been nothing but positive. Previously been healthy and rarely visited a doctors surgery, but due to a back injury a few years back I found my first port of call the Octagon Medical Centre and my Dr and Physio at the centre have been nothing short of a Godsend. Due to the nature of my injury and the waiting list for hospital appointments etc after Covid I was initially dreading the wait, but have been well looked after and was sent for a scan relatively quick after my initial appointment at the Octagon Medical Centre. A couple of surgical procedures later and one to one with pain management specialists have helped me come to terms with my ongoing injury and I feel positive about my recovery and the future. My medication and prescriptions have always been talked through and are always available when requested and I am now being talked through my next procedure with the specialists - all thanks to that initial meeting with my Doctor at the Octagon MC. All involved have been nothing but a credit to the NHS and if you’re unsure about your next step then my advice is make an appointment to discuss it with someone at the Octagon MC and I’m sure you won’t be disappointed and any worries will alleviate after that discussion. Thank you OMC!

recent_reviews.author: Vee Matt
recent_reviews.text: Worst possible GP Surgery. After months of being nervous and putting off my cervical screening, finally booked an appointment and went in today. First off, I was ignored by reception staff as they chatted and laughed while I stood there waiting. Eventually when I go in for my appointment with the Nurse Practitioner Nicola, she tells me that she thought I was someone else even though she clearly got my details from when I made the appointment. I know she only said that because I had come in for a cervical screening. She said she couldn't do screenings because (in her own words): "even though I'm a nurse, I am a nurse practitioner and I don't do those". She then walked out of the room, comes back a few mins later to tell me to go to reception and they will "deal with it". Reception staff were also rude and nonchalant with the woman smirking and rolling her eyes. She made it seem like it was my fault for booking an appointment with 'the great nurse practitioner' that was too good to perform cervical screenings. I was so frustrated with the way she was responding to me that I almost cried. At this point obviously other patients waiting in reception knew why I was there which was embarassing. I was so nervous prior to the test (as most women would be) and I had put it off for months. I finally got the courage to go today but was treated so badly. I said I will be making a complaint but she didn't care and told me to take a leaflet because I'm sure she knows that nothing would get done even if patients complain to the Practice Manager. I left there feeling so down and I want to change GPs as soon as possible now. This whole experience has really made me scared to get a cervical screening now even with another practice. I have now made a complaint with NHS England and will also be complaining to the Health Ombudsman as I believe this 'Practice' needs to be investigated.

recent_reviews.author: WAYNE LARGE
recent_reviews.text: Possibly one of the most disappointing experiences I’ve ever had with senior doctors. After being told by district nurses and undertakers that I could collect a death certificate to register my parent’s passing, I arrived at the practice only to be informed that the procedure had changed. Neither the nurses nor the detailed NHS leaflet I was given reflected this change, leading to unnecessary confusion at an already difficult time. When I asked to speak to the manager, I was instead met by her secretary, who I initially assumed was the manager until informed otherwise. Despite requesting the manager again and asking for the new procedure in writing, I was then redirected to a junior doctor. They asked me to fill out a form I had already completed with the district nurse, which then had to be emailed. To make matters worse, I later received a call from a senior doctor accusing me of upsetting and being rude to staff—a claim that was both unfounded and deeply upsetting. This same doctor, during a previous home visit, did not even know my parent’s name. On the phone, her tone was condescending and defensive when I questioned her. Over recent months, during an incredibly emotional period, I have consistently found this practice to be unhelpful, lacking in empathy, and frequently contradictory in their communication. Sensitive matters were often discussed in the crowded reception area, which felt completely inappropriate and disrespectful. This experience added unnecessary stress during bereavement, and I sincerely hope the practice takes steps to improve their procedures and communication in the future.

recent_reviews.author: vivienne boardman
recent_reviews.text: We moved to this practice a few months ago after our old Drs was really going downhill after merging with about four other practices. we are in or mid to late 70's, with a few ongoing problems, me with diabetes, which luckily doesnt give me any problems, but the osteo arthritis is a different story! that can stop me in my tracks when it gets bad, but my other half, he has dementia, COPD. and also bad pain in his leg as he had a plate put in years ago,, anyway when all the problems with covid started we lost most of the regular Drs, and the dr who we used to see retired, and trying to get an appointment even on the telephone was a non starter, and i was worried that if "him indoors" had a bad breathing attack i wouldnt be able to get in touch with anyone, so i decided to ask around like many other people from there and find another Drs who we could trust.. Luckily a few of my friends told me about "the Oaks" and thank god they did. this Drs has done more for us in the few months we've been here than our old Drs did in a few years,, and everybody has been so nice from the Drs, nurses, and the receptionists... because as you get older you just need the reassurance of knowing there is someone who will be there for you, even if its only for advice on the end of a phone, I know there are times when you have to call back because they are busy, but this happens everywhere, because its obvious other people need a Dr as well.. so I want to say THANKYOU, your very much appreciated Mrs V Boardman

recent_reviews.author: Flora Mousavi
recent_reviews.text: I am disappointed to write a negative review for Orient House Medical Centre based on my recent experience. I had a telehealth appointment to discuss concerning symptoms and was told photos I provided would be reviewed and I'd receive a call back later that day. Despite multiple attempts to follow up, I never received any response from my doctor. The lack of communication and follow-through are unacceptable when dealing with potential health issues. I made efforts on my end to send information ahead of time and arranging a call during work hours. But after assurance of follow-up from the doctor, I was left hanging without explanation or peace of mind. Worrying symptoms remain unaddressed, leading to unnecessary anxiety on my end as a patient. Clear communication should be a basic expectation from a healthcare provider. I cannot recommend a practice that fails at such a fundamental responsibility in caring for its patients. Unless major improvements are made, I will be taking my healthcare needs elsewhere. Patients deserve better.

recent_reviews.author: Jodie Leigh
recent_reviews.text: I’d be apprehensive to say this practice even deserves one star. I had been registered here for the past approximately 15 years and throughout attended this practice for multiple ongoing problems which I feel have been ignored and unseen to despite countless visits. The main problem is not the qualified healthcare staff but the overall system and management, I work in healthcare myself and understand that sometimes no matter how well patients are treated by staff they are still failed by the declining system of the NHS. Although I have felt ignored by some practitioners whose names I cannot remember, nurse Karen and mental health practitioner Ian have been great and have always listened to my health issues thoroughly. The reception staff answer calls with rude manner (I can’t say all as I have had kind receptionists previously but the majority of time not) and they appear uninterested in answering your queries and concerns. The appointment availability is unacceptable, attempting to arrange an on the day appointment at 8am often leaves you without one and trying to pre book an appointment leaves you with a 3-7 week wait and there is no acknowledgement of urgent symptoms. Sometimes they’ll tell you a GP will contact you over the phone on the day to assess your symptoms and then no one rings you all day from the practice. The final straw for me was when I rang last week describing tachycardia, feeling faint and CHEST PAIN and they told me they had no appointments for 4 weeks, neither did they advise me on what to do or where else to go for urgent medical attention. I have since changed practice and they have been a huge improvement.

recent_reviews.author: Diane Moss
recent_reviews.text: I took my twelve year old granddaughter to Hopwood medical centre yesterday (15th December) our appt was 11am, we finally got to see the dr at 11.50 ( I know they are busy). He said she had dry eyes and written on a piece of paper what to get from the chemist. I said she is 12 ( although she looks about 9) are you not going to give her a script, I asked him twice and he said no, you can buy over the counter, I said but she is 12. He said ' my supervisor will ask me why I gave a script out when it can be purchased OTC' , again I said she is 12. I went into the chemist, the lady said have they not given you a script, I said no and I told her my granddaughter was 12. £6.50 it was for these eye drops which I probably could have bought at Morrisons for less. My gripe is. If I as pensioner I was told to buy something OTC, even though though we are entitled, I would have paid it but a 12 year old. Disgusted with this practice if that is how they work. I think they need to look at who is entitled to what . End of gripe

recent_reviews.author: James Stridgen
recent_reviews.text: My son was advised by two separate locum doctors on two occasions at the surgery, to apply to ADHD 360 for an assessment for ADHD as the waiting list on the national health was 8 years. He was given the organisations name and address then contacted them for an assessment. We (his parents) borrowed the £1000 required fee and he was assessed for between 1 and 4 hours by ADHD 360. His results showed that he scored 99% symptoms on every test and was told that there were only 7% of the population with such scores. Obviously now having a diagnosis he made an appointment to see his GP at Yorkshire street where he was told that they could/would not prescribe the vital medication he needs to live a normal independent life and relieve his symptoms. He was told that because he went to a private company (as advised) then he had to pay for private prescriptions. As he is currently receiving statutory sick pay there is no way he can do this, nor as pensioners can we. What can we do next please ?

recent_reviews.author: Dominic Keefe
recent_reviews.text: Some of the doctors here are more thoughtful than others but overall they reflect institutional neglect. I'm dealing with a disabling and frightening chronic condition that has been poorly investigated and diagnosed by the NHS and this health center. Tests have always comeback within their very broad definition of 'normal' and they refuse to apply any further clinical consideration to a patients' actual clinical picture. I asked for my medical records and I still haven't received the requested information three months later. I've complained but received no response. One receptionist a month ago completely ignored me. Then she dealt with me as if it was an inconvenience. The online triage system is now a grim joke. It frequently suspends the option to make an appointment for a week or more, and then every alternative method of contact filters you back to it. The clinic is at the forefront of a modern dysfunctional NHS where compassion disappeared decades ago. The patient comes very last in its considerations and it merely a source of LHA funding. Addendum : I am now discovering that the causes that I suggested for my illness and was laughed out of the surgery with ('Dr' Yazicci actually laughed at them) are indeed the issue and I am now self medicating with considerbale success. The dimissal of my theories by this surgery has cost me years of my life as I didn't act on it. Any attempt to complain to them is water off a duck's back to them. I've since changed surgeries. When I mentioned I was going to this, this one became even less responsive and more dismissive.

recent_reviews.text: As of October 1st 2025 gov.uk made the announcement that patients in the UK, will be able to request appointments online throughout the day, rather than calling their surgery or visiting in person. Roisin the practice nurse is lovely and the most helpful member of staff at the surgery, and also seems to be the most overworked staff there too. The reception staff are generally as helpful as they can be but without actual doctors to see patients, the surgery would seem to be struggling.

recent_reviews.author: Vikrant Kalukhe
recent_reviews.text: I visited the practice for an in-person appointment to obtain a fit note while suffering from flu symptoms, including a high fever. I had made significant effort to attend despite feeling very unwell. Upon arrival, I was informed by the receptionist that the appointment was actually a telephone consultation, which was not indicated when the booking was made or confirmed. I politely pointed this out, explaining that it appeared to be an administrative error, and suggested it might help to flag this to prevent similar mix-ups for other patients in the future (e.g., someone travelling unnecessarily while ill). Unfortunately, instead of acknowledging the mistake or apologising, the receptionist repeated that I did not need to wait in the surgery for the call – raising her voice and speaking slowly and loudly on the second occasion. This felt highly patronising and dismissive, especially when I was already feeling extremely unwell and vulnerable. In the end, the journey was wasted, and I left without the consultation proceeding as expected. Clearer communication about appointment types and better handling of patient feedback when errors occur would greatly improve the experience here.

recent_reviews.author: Amanda Neville
recent_reviews.text: A masterclass in how not to run a GP surgery. Reception staff appear to have taken on the role of clinicians, routinely dismissing concerns, deciding what does and does not warrant medical attention, and frequently redirecting patients to A&E or out-of-hours services for minor or ongoing issues. One wonders when this became part of their job description. GP consultations offer little improvement. Complex medical conditions, mental health concerns, and written recommendations from specialists are met with indifference or ignored altogether. Listening appears optional; empathy entirely absent. Complaints are treated with the same enthusiasm as patient care — acknowledged, if at all, then quietly disregarded. Patients are spoken to in a patronising manner and left feeling foolish for seeking help. If you are looking for accessible, patient-centred care, this is not the place. If, however, you enjoy being dismissed, redirected elsewhere, and made to feel like an inconvenience, this surgery may be exactly what you’re looking for.

recent_reviews.author: John Neill
recent_reviews.text: Do not register at this practice. The worst treatment myself and my partner have ever received. The GP’s are utterly unequipped to deal with anything other than a cold. The receptionists are the rudest, most inept people I’ve ever had the displeasure to come across and should have their parole revoked (I’m assuming they’re on parole given the aggressive behaviour they show anytime you ring up). As for the administrative staff, they seem to be incapable of reading a clinical letter, ignorant of how their ineptitude affects patient care, or blatantly money-grubbers. The practices operate a “total-triage” system that is a choice given to them by the government to abandon patient care in favour of increased subsidies. I probably don’t need to explain at this point; they took the subsidies! They don’t care about patients, and If they ever did they were incapable of doing anything about it.

recent_reviews.author: Deborah Walton
recent_reviews.text: I have had a horrendous experience being registered with this group practice. I made a complaint about a senior admin worker who denied receiving 3 letters from my solicitor after waiting 12mths for a copy of my gp notes . Then my Gp notes were destroyed vindictivly I am amazed that the practice manager didn't know it was gross Misconduct and a criminal offence to tamper, alter or fix a patients notes. I know this by comments passed to me at a practice managers meeting. I had no option but to report this to the GMC who passed it to NHS England to investigate. My case was to serious for them to investigate as they should do because I named 2 Gp s who I had apts with and went in, sat down. The Gp looked at his screen and didn't speak when I told him my reason for going to see a Gp, he totally ignored me and after what felt like 30 mins of silence I got up and left his room. I had no idea Dr's behaved this way and happened twice with 2 Gp's. NHS England conducted a corrupt investigation without a single meeting with me. I found out 12mths later that the GMC worked with NHS England on this investigation, they don't work together. All this came to the senior Gp at the practice who was responsible for the surgery, I now know he took early retirement before the investigation got going. Ever since I have been treated very badly by every Gp I have seen at several practices. I am denied Healthcare, treatment and medication across the board even mental health services have been closed to me. I have been set up by mental health nurses who requested a urine sample under the order of a consultant. The drug test they did came up positive for every substance you can think of but my prescribed medication didn't show up on the drug test, codeine and pregabalin are both controlled drugs and medication I take every day. Think this proves it was all staged and a set up, you don't expect this from a mental health nurse. Had I taken any kind of class A drugs I wouldn't have given anyone a urine sample. I was left bent in half with horrific back pain the Gp practice I was registered with Mark Street Surgery refused to review my pain relief or increase it. I am now disabled for the rest of my life and under a spinal surgeon at Salford with a life curve of my spine. I could go on forever I am now registered in littleborough and denied any kind of Healthcare Treatment and medication. Just today I've been denied antibiotics for a chest infection and have COPD. They are trying to kill me off for daring to make a complaint. I am advising everyone not to make any complaints against any Gp's if you do your life will be turned into a living hell just as mine has. If you do you will get invented diagnoses, lies out and out lies all on your care summary and cannot be removed, only they do remove notes and letters and remove all names of Dr's and nurses from your Gp notes this is tampering again with my life. My whole life and the birth of my Boys has been wiped out how dare they do this to me ? I have a right to complain I cannot sit back and take being labeled a druggie, this is now one step to far I've been given no option but to go to the Nursing and Midwifery council and The royal college of nurses and midwives. I can't be punished anymore than I have been and still taking this off Gp's and bardoc Dr's, who put the cuff on to do my BP and don't inflate it they then walk out of my home without a word. A Gp at the practice I am registered with looked in my ear after earache for 2wks and bleeding from inside and said it was OK Really ?? I also had a swelling under my arm and lumps he failed to examine me and have a family history of breast cancer. He smirked at me in a very sick way, he's training to be a Gp. District Nurses refuse me compression bandages requested by my vascular surgeon but then go on to lie and document I couldn't tolerate them. I am totally disgusted with all of them I am now self managing leg ulcers because they refuse me home visits and dressings. Don't complain its not worth it.

recent_reviews.author: Sandeep Tandon
recent_reviews.text: I ordered my repeat prescription via the app several days ago. When I attended the pharmacy, I was told the prescription had not been authorised by the doctor. On Thursday, I attended the surgery and was informed by the receptionist that the particular doctor was “not in”. I explained the urgency and asked for the prescription to be pushed through. I was then assured that my medication would be ready to collect from the pharmacy on Saturday morning. Today (Saturday 17/01/26), I attended the pharmacy at 1pm, only to find that it was closed. Both the pharmacy and the GP surgery are now closed. As of today, I have completely run out of my prescribed medication, including Ramipril and Atorvastatin. I have disabilities and suffer from high blood pressure, and being without this medication places my health at risk. I am extremely concerned that the online prescription service is being promoted, yet it is ineffective if prescriptions are not authorised in a timely manner. The system only works if doctors take responsibility for approving patients’ medication. I would like this matter urgently reviewed, an explanation provided as to how this situation was allowed to occur, and assurances that this does not happen again. I also request immediate advice on how I can obtain my medication as soon as possible. I look forward to your prompt response. Yours faithfully, S

GP services are in high demand and one of the top comments we receive is that people are held in a queue for long periods of time in the mornings. Another way to access Dalefield Surgery is to visit www.online-consult.co.uk/org/dalefield-surgery and complete an online consultation form. You can also pre book an appointment. We have appointments up to 3 months in advance at 1-2 weeks notice.

recent_reviews.text: I've been a patient at the surgery for three years. In recent times I have been quite frustrated. I follow the protocol, which is to ring every morning at 8am to book an appointment. Everytime I ring it takes a while to actually get through to the phone. Always busy and beeping till at least 8.30am. When i do get through to their phone, I wait at least 30 to 45 minutes until I speak to a receptionist. Only then to be told that there are no appointments and to ring again the next morning. They always mention that they've not got enough reception staff to answer the calls on time and apologise. It's every day. I already have anxiety phoning in the doctors anyway, but to be told everytime there's no appointments it puts me off even more to go and see the doctor. I went in person today, to a quite surgery we're there was no patients in the waiting room. In hope that I would get an appointment finally. I was told again there were no appointments, would I like to book one for next week. I said yes please. She had a look for an appointment next week, to my disappointment there were no appointments available at all for next week. She then told me to ring out of hours or ring in next week at 8am. What's the point when I have been told there are no appointments and then to be on phone for over an hour to get the same treatment again. Sick to death of their being no appointments to see a doctor. If the number of patients is increasing get more doctors and receptionists! I will be changing my surgery.

recent_reviews.author: Royalty x Tehmeh
recent_reviews.text: I’m writing this as a patient who feels deeply let down by the GP system in Bolton. I developed what started as a cold burn, which has since turned into an open wound. It has still not healed and remains untreated properly despite me contacting my GP surgery on two separate occasions. During my first visit, I was prescribed antibiotics. What concerned me most was that the doctor appeared unsure about the condition and searched online during the appointment to understand what it was and how to treat it. Seeing a medical professional rely on an internet search in front of me made me feel unsafe and worried that they didn’t fully understand what they were dealing with. I was given antibiotics and sent home, but there was no proper wound care, cleaning or dressing provided. The wound has still not healed. I attended again on the 11 march because I was worried about infection and the lack of improvement. I waited for around an hour past my appointment time due to other issues at the practice, which I understand can happen when services are extremely busy. However, when I was finally seen, the appointment itself lasted only about two- three minutes. The doctor briefly looked at the wound and said I would be referred elsewhere. When I asked how long that would take, I was told “not long — around two weeks.” I left feeling shocked and frustrated and I’m not someone who is outspoken so I couldn’t even ask the questions I truly wanted to ask, especially when I feel rushed in an environment. I don’t understand why a GP service cannot provide basic wound care such as cleaning the injury and applying the correct dressing. Being told to wait weeks with an open wound feels unacceptable and distressing. I understand GP practices are under pressure and very busy and I am willing to put some delays down to how packed the surgery was. However, patients should still feel properly assessed, treated, and reassured especially when dealing with an open wound that risks 🥀infection🥀. This situation has left me asking some serious questions about our health care quality • What is the role of a GP if basic treatment isn’t provided? • Why are patients left waiting with untreated wounds? • What are we paying taxes for if essential frontline care isn’t accessible? My visit to this GP has shown me that quantity over quality is more valued. I understand the pressures on the National Health Service and that staff are often overstretched. However, patients should still feel safe, listened to and properly treated. Right now, I feel dismissed and let down by a system that is supposed to provide timely and 🥀competent care🥀.

recent_reviews.text: Very disappointing experience. I arrived at 4:00 pm for my 4:10 pm appointment while being 34 weeks pregnant. During the wait, I saw him talking with a member of staff inside the room. When I asked the receptionist at about 4:45 pm, I was first told the doctor was dealing with a patient on the phone. Later I was told he was speaking with the manager. I understand delays can happen, but waiting around 40 minutes in this situation was very difficult, especially while heavily pregnant and with two children after school. If the doctor needed time for a meeting, appointments should not be given at that time. Very disappointing service and poor time management.

recent_reviews.text: multiple bad experiences of this practice, it took more than 6 months to send my fertility referral off and i was advised on multiple occasions this has been done , i contacted one day and requested a copy of the referral letter to then be advised there wasn't one as the referral had been noted but nothing sent, if i hadn't of requested the proof i would still be waiting, the manger was great in resolving this but a shame the staff wrongly advised for so long. I went in today for an appointment at 9am for my Flu jab and whilst waiting 20 mints in reception I witnessed one side of a receptionist dealing with a difficult patient on the phone who wanted an appointment today and understandably the surgery didn't have any left to offer, the manor she was speaking to the difficult patient was disgusting and no where near the level of service a receptionist should be trained to, after this call ended the manor she then spoke to patients waiting at reception was beyond me, a witnessed her being abrupt and rude to at least 5 patients and this stemmed from her being annoyed with the previous call she had to deal with. In a customer focused job role you need to have the ability to stay calm and respect people around you and she clearly didn't have this ability, we sometimes have to deal with difficult people but the ability to bounce back and smile at the next person is a must for a doctors receptionist where people are already stressed due to being sick. I will certainly now be looking for an alternative doctors as witnessing what i did today was terribly upsetting.

recent_reviews.text: I am very disappointed with the care I received my experience with Dr. Jay was particularly troubling. Two weeks ago, I visited the clinic with an eye allergy. Dr. Jay refused to prescribe steroids, saying it would not be good for me in the future. Despite my insistence, he said no. The next day, I had a severe asthma attack, and only then prescribe the steroids I initially requested. This delay in proper treatment worsened my condition significantly. To make matters worse, I had an appointment today for allergy tests, but the clinic did not have any record of the specific tests I needed the Doctor who requested my blood test had forgotten to note which blood tests to perform. As a result, my appointment was rescheduled for next Friday, which is incredibly inconvenient and frustrating. This level of unprofessionalism and lack of care is unacceptable. It seems like the clinic does not prioritize their patients health and well-being. I hope this review brings attention to these issues so that future patients do not have to experience the same negligence.

recent_reviews.author: Vee Matt
recent_reviews.text: There are so many things that could be done better at Bolton General Practice but judging by the reviews, they have no intention of improving their services. Where do I start? From the very beginning they messed up my appointment. I had a telephone interview on the 7th of June but they couldn't even leave a message to let me know it was cancelled. Then randomly I received a call on the 11th of June instead when the nurse Gemma told me she had been sick. That's ok, it would have been nice to have been informed by the admin staff but it was fine. We then booked an appointment for today at 8am because I informed her that I start work at 8:30am. She (Gemma) assured me that she would be in the Practice from 8am anyways so not to worry. This is where it gets worse. I arrive before 8am but wait outside until 8am then make my way to reception. I inform them about my appointment. Now, it would have been great if the receptionists had told me at that point that Gemma wasn't actually in. I would have happily rearranged my appointment and left so I could make it to work on time. Instead, they let me sit there even though I asked a couple times if they could please check with her as I didn't want to be late. One receptionist told me she wasn't logged in so she couldn't check which was obviously not true as I realised later that Gemma hadn't arrived yet. Then at 8:07am, a lady strolls in and doesn't acknowledge me so I didn't know at this point that it was Gemma. She casually checks her schedule and talks with the receptionists briefly then goes into a consultation room. She comes out a couple times and goes back in without once acknowledging me, despite knowing that I had specifically booked an appointment with her for 8am. At 8:12am, one of the receptionist whispers to the other and I catch the name "Gemma". I guess at this point, even she realises that she should be proactive and do something. She then goes into the same consultation room the lady went in earlier. She comes out in a few seconds and tells me that Gemma won't be long. It's at this point I know that the lady was Gemma. Gemma never once acknowledged me. Surely, if you're late for an appointment you would apologise for being late especially as you knew I was waiting. It's funny because if a patient had been even 5mins late, their appointment would have been cancelled. At 8:15am, I'd had enough. I was going to be late for work and Gemma had yet to come out of the room. At what time was she going to begin? All I wanted was some travel vaccines! I then go to the reception and tell them I'm leaving as I had to go to work. I guess Gemma overhears the conversation through the open door of the consultation room because for the first time, she comes out and addresses me. I wasn't rude and never raised my voice. I just calmly informed them that I couldn't wait any longer as I was going to be late. Gemma then tells me that she getting the vaccines ready and was stuck in traffic which is why she was late, and that she was almost done. The thing is, she knew I was coming today. It's ok if you're late but at least address the patient waiting for you! Only when I was leaving did she come out and address me. Also, why didn't the receptionists just tell me she was running late as I specifically told them I had to be at work for 8:30am and I was there to see Gemma. In addition, there were other staff I'm assuming were doctors and nurses chatting and laughing just around the corner. One even walked back and forth, looking directly at me. Could none have asked to help? I guess this is another reason the NHS is going downhill. It is already nearly impossible to book an appointment so what do they do all day? Anyways, this was a long rant but I had to get it off my chest. I rarely go to the doctors, last time was probably over 2yrs ago and still they are incompetent. I now do not have enough time to find another GP, register and then book travel vaccines before I go away so I'm having to go without any travel vaccines. Thanks Bolton General Practice for nothing!

recent_reviews.author: Moo Roo
recent_reviews.text: If I could give zero stars I would. An appalling practice that puts profit over patient experience. I’ve been registered with this practice for around 15 years or more and hate having to go in for anything, primarily due to certain receptionist staff… curt and off putting to put it lightly.. I try not to use this practice as I find the human interaction there highly emotionally disturbing, yes I may be over sensitive to people’s attitudes I accept that but I only pick up on what people give out, not what I imagine, and so the animosity I feel from certain members of staff led me to take up private heath care some time ago. It’s unfortunate I had to make contact with them over a matter recently that just upheld the issues I have with them. The malignancy that I find pervades certain members staff is highly unpleasant and unwelcoming. Luckily Bupa now have a GP service so I use them, but a recent issue required I needed a form signing by the GP at this practice.. Firstly the older receptionist told me curtly that it would be a 4 week wait for the signature, was told these waits times were displayed on the entrance door.. they were not, and still are not at the time of writing this. It took over 4 weeks to ring me to tell me they had eventually been signed and was told it was £104!!!! I questioned this cost a few times over the next few weeks while I was trying to save for the money, I needed to see a consultant, I asked several times for a breakdown, wasn’t given it, was treated with contempt for asking on several occasions.. a £104!!!!!! In my eyes I’m saving this practice the money that they get for having my name on their register by using Bupa, you’d think they’d be more helpful that I was trying to save time for more needy patients. That said I had a medical need and my needs weren’t met by these people and I was treated with contempt by unqualified receptionists and ultimately by the practice manager. When I was able to save up enough to go and get the form I needed signing I was told they had destroyed it on my say so during a phone call, I had not, I had told them it was unaffordable, that they were creating a block to my healthcare in such a cost but I never said to destroy it or why would I go in to pay… Absolutely untrue and a vicious attempt to cover up their personal petulance in relation to myself. I am on the spectrum and dyslexic and so are other people who visit their business, for that’s what it is.. a business. I’ve tried to report them to the relevant trusts for this cost but they appear to be unaccountable to Bolton NHS trust and their appears no real avenue for complaint. Charlatans, they’ll reel you in for all the checks they like because they get paid per diagnosis of say things like blood pressure medication… but the community service and true medical care has given way to a corporate identity.. So be warned of unpublished costs and be warned that Heaton Medical Centre may make you feel sick.. it did me!

recent_reviews.author: Sarah Almond
recent_reviews.text: I've been with this practice for years and always had great care. I've been prompted to review today by the recent changes to the appointment booking system. Gone is ringing up at 8am. You now fill in the econsult form either on the NHS app or surgery website and your information is then reviewed by a Dr and an appointment made if necessary. I've had to use this system twice in the last month and both times I have been contacted in under 3 hours of submitting the request, with same day appointments available. I really can't ask for any more than this from my GP. The staff have always been brilliant here as well, but the change to the appointment system has really made a huge difference to me and made the GP service so much more accessible (and less awkward than having to explain all your symptoms over the phone!) EDIT: Just seen that someone else has reviewed the same system with a very different viewpoint! They might want to wait an hour or so and maybe they'll be surprised with a same day appointment... They definitely do exist!

recent_reviews.author: Jay Shepherd
recent_reviews.text: We joined this surgery during COVID, I assumed the poor service was to do with the pandemic, however it simply just hasn't got any better. Every time my wife goes to pick up her repeat prescription, it's NEVER ready. So she's started ringing in advance to check that it's going to be ready on the daythey say it is, that's also made no difference... Each time this happens, the chemist next door and the medical centre just blame each other. Hilarious. Last time I checked the 'My GP' app, there are no appointments made available by the surgery to book online. Ringing up at 8am for a same day appointment really just isn't good enough a system, me and our children all need to be 'where we need to be' by 8am, we can't simply wait at home in case we get lucky and get an appointment, which could be any time that day. Or worse, not get an appointment and us all be late for school and work for no reason, potentially doing this every day until we get lucky. There are lots of positives.

recent_reviews.author: Rosemary Shaw
recent_reviews.text: I am carer for 91 year old mother who has late stage dementia. She lives with me and my husband. Since her diagnosis in 2014 we have had no contact with a GP or advice. The only way I've found out what to expect is on the internet. We are asked to make an appointment every 6 months for her to have a basic check up. We have been shielding her since mid March. We had to call paramedics in August. They informed GP but there has been no follow up. Feeling abandoned. My husband rang for an appointment for himself and told to ring on Friday at 8.00am. All appointments had been taken. If you show your displeasure at their unfriendly, officious administration you are threatened with being taken off the register. Reading the Inspection report it seems inconceivable that GOOD was awarded for mental health services which included dementia! Seriously consider the communication strategies and appointment system They are both dysfunctional. This Practice is NOT full-filling it's role in caring for vulnerable or anxious and exhausted clients during this time. Unsatisfactory

recent_reviews.author: Jean Leader
recent_reviews.text: We joined this practice many years ago and we were quite happy with the doctors and the whole practice. As time went by and the doctors changed except for a couple who stayed. Things started to deteriorate. Each visit would always be a new doctor as there seemed to be a regular changeover, this meaning you never got to know a doctor or they you. To ring for an appointment could take forever being on hold. Too get an appointment well that could be weeks away ( my very last attempt was over 3 weeks !!!! ). That made my decision to leave this practice.My husband made this same decision for a different reason. He had a motor accident and the hospital told him to go to his doctors as soon as he could. This was fine he got in the next day ( a one off ) as it was a sort of emergency. He saw the doctor but the doctor would not take his blood pressure, he told him to do it himself in the waiting room. Myself and my husband tried this but the machine was broken, reception tried it and agreed it was broke. So reception rang the doctor and asked could my husband go back in ( no other patient had gone in or was waiting ) The doctor said NO make an appointment to see the nurse another day. One thought came to mind DISGUSTING. I myself was seeing the nurse a couple of days later and she said " tell your husband to come and see me after his work and i will wait for him if he struggles to get back to Bolton on time". What a difference we found the nurses are so helpful and caring. Also we would always be on time for our appointments but the wait sat in the waiting room could be anything from a good half hour to well over an hour. !!!! We have now changed to another surgery and we are so pleased with our choice. It may not be an updated modern surgery but it is so welcoming. The staff lovely and the doctors 1st class. I have had too visit more than normal so another reason I am glad we changed, as TWO days is the longest I have had to wait for an appointment and next day the other two appointment's. To close I can only say I am surprised Heaton Medical Center have managed just over one star in these reviews. Our opinion is that it has gone down so badly over the years and feel so relieved to have got away from Heaton Medical Center.
