recent_reviews.author: David Taylor
recent_reviews.text: *STAY AWAY* Absolutely useless GP Surgery. Receptionist seem to think they can diagnose your problems over the phone and they deem if you are able to see the actual doctor or not. This practice has let me down on many occasions, even after I left! On numerous occasions over the last few months they have informed me my prescription had been sent and it had either not in fact been sent or had been sent to the wrong place. I recently moved from Bolton to Bury and I was already being seen by this practice for a knee problem, I was constantly "told off" by the receptionist that I need to move to a new GP as I have moved address and they won't continue to send my prescriptions to Bury. I emailed the practice to order my repeat prescription before I decided to make an application to a join a new GP. I did this via email, I was emailed to confirm my medication had been sent. After going on public transport to collect my medication ( whilst struggling to walk) I arrive and to be told that nothing has been sent. I contacted the GP to see why this has not been sent and was met with a receptionist who insisted I am not a patient anymore as of Wednesday last week. I informed her I ordered this prior to moving to my new GP and was informed that this had been sent and I have the email as proof. She said leave it with her and if I don't hear anything back by 5pm to ring her back. I stressed that I needed my medication as I have ran out and I have come all the way to collect my prescription now. her response was nothing she can do. As I heard nothing back I had to call them back again I was met by a different woman on reception who was very rude to me. She said yes we have done it but you will have to come to Bolton to pick it up. This would take me hours on public transport and it was 5.30pm, I asked why could my prescription not be sent electronically or sent to my new GP which is 10min down the road from me as I need my medication today. The woman talked over me, wouldn't let me finish and said your prescription is here if you want it or contact you new GP and get them to assess you and go from there. I was shocked at how poorly this has been dealt with, I stressed at 12 o'clock that I have ran out of my medication and I need it. The GP hadn't even bothered to ring me back. Now I am awaiting for a manager to ring me back, which wont happen. I have spoken to my new GP and they haven't been informed that I am taking medication and would require me to see the doctor which is the earliest appointment is seven working days!

recent_reviews.author: Amy
recent_reviews.text: Only recently registered with them, first experience with the doctor (Dr. Ashraf) was positive but consequent visits have been pretty negative. A follow up appointment was running 10 minutes behind (I'd turned up at least 10 minutes early, for a 9am appointment and the waiting room had been empty). My "ten minute" appointment was about 4 minutes long and I was rushed out the room before I even got to discuss my symptoms, which I'm now very worried about. Instead of getting to discuss them in my appointment I've been made to feel like I'm not worth treating and I'm wasting their time, but looking on the NHS website (among multiple others) has suggested my symptoms are actually quite serious, I'm just too nervous to go to A&E because they're for "emergencies" like people who need stitches, etc. So I don't feel right taking up their time, especially after being rushed through my doctor's appointment like my symptoms don't matter. The receptionists here are very hit or miss (miss = rude and useless!) I had to phone to ask for the doctor to request images from my ultrasound scan (I couldn't request them from the company directly) and the receptionist acted like I was asking for them to do a handstand and sing the alphabet backwards. I called again a few weeks later to find out there wasn't even a note of it on the system. I also had to basically shout personal information over to a receptionist (in front of people in the waiting room) who kept interrupting me before I could properly get a word out because she "couldn't hear me, WHAT do (I) want?" (Bobbed brown hair, older middle aged woman). I have now just got off the phone asking a simple, non-medical question because I didn't want to waste the doctor's time (especially since doctors are being overworked and I was rushed out last time in under half my alloted appointment time). Her attitude was disgusting, she spoke down to me like I'm some sort of idiot and you could hear in her tone she thinks she's better than other people (she even did one of those "taken aback" sort of "throat tutts" if that makes sense). I have to book an appointment tomorrow to try and discuss my more worrying symptoms with a doctor (if I win the phone lotto, otherwise I'll be going to A&E) but now I have to add on another issue to discuss, which could have been done without my needing to have an appointment if the receptionist hadn't been such a stuck up her own a--e tw-t. I think she said she was called Pat or Pam.

recent_reviews.author: Professor J.
recent_reviews.text: I attended for an emergency appointment that the practice themselves scheduled, despite me explaining that traffic at that time is extremely heavy. I accepted because it was the only option given. On arrival, I was spoken to by the receptionist in a sarcastic, rude, and dismissive manner. When I explained that this was an emergency and asked to be seen, I was told I was not allowed to wait, despite the practice’s own policy stating that late patients may wait for the doctor’s discretion, not the receptionist’s. Most concerning was a racist and discriminatory comment made by the receptionist during the discussion: “You can’t argue with us because you’re not in Pakistan now.” This was shocking and completely unacceptable in a healthcare setting. I was also told there was only one doctor working and that they were “busy,” yet shortly afterwards, a doctor came out to call the only other patient, with no one having left the doctor’s room beforehand. This contradicted what I had been told. Patients deserve respect, honesty, and basic professionalism. That receptionist failed at all counts.

recent_reviews.author: Margaret Parrish
recent_reviews.text: My review of this GP Practice is long overdue. I have been a patient for almost 40 years, much of that time being under the leadership of Doctor Green and Dr Muhsin. In this current climate when people are often unable to see a doctor, I find that this is not the case at Burnside. I have had no problems obtaining telephone consultations and, when appropriate to my circumstances, a follow up face to face appointment at the surgery has been provided promptly. The senior doctors are both very experienced and genuinely interested in the wellbeing of their patients. The reception staff, nurses, doctors on placement and other health professionals are welcoming, knowledgeable and supportive. There is a warmth and understanding at Burnside that means a lot to people, especially when they are anxious about a diagnosis or injury. I am both lucky and proud to be a patient at this practice. Margaret Parrish April 2024

recent_reviews.author: David Spencer
recent_reviews.text: I transferred myself from the Egerton and Dunscar Health Centre to the Burnside Surgery some 3 months ago. The transfer was easy due to a very helpful receptionist who suggested I complete the necessary forms in the waiting area. This proved excellent as I was able to correct any mistakes by asking her questions there and then. The first thing that I want to highlight is that wonderfully there is no background music whilst waiting to see the doctor or nurse and this for me is a big plus. It was my perception at the Egerton and Dunscar Health Centre that events leading up to my heart attack some 5 years ago included stress whilst waiting to consult the doctor.I actually felt worse having seen the doctor than when I walked in at the front door. This is no longer a problem at Burnside and I am grateful. Dr Gillooly is my local practitioner and is very patient. He makes me feel confident in his advices and takes great interest in any problems I have. He is great! Lastly I just love the TV screen where you can alert the practice of my arrival simply by typing in my surname and date of birth etc. So easy.

recent_reviews.text: Absolutely appalling service and dismissive attitude. Avoid this practice if you value your time and dignity. I submitted a consultation request on 23 April and was told I’d hear back by 29 April. That deadline passed with no response, when I chased they told me I wasn’t to expect such a quick response. I was called 9 April and to tell me they had no appointments and they will call me by the end of the day. I was then called today to 16 MAY When I questioned the delay, the person on the phone said, “Do you want an appointment or not? ,” in a rushed and dismissive tone. When I asked for their name, they refused to give it. The lack of professionalism and accountability is staggering. I also spoke to Heidi today. While this interaction was fine, I have had very poor experiences with her in the past, as I see others have mentioned in their reviews as well. This isn’t just poor service, it shows a clear disregard for patient wellbeing. Delayed communication, broken promises, and an unhelpful, even hostile attitude toward perfectly reasonable concerns. People deserve better than this. I’ll be formally reporting the interaction and encourage others to do the same. Patients are not just numbers. We deserve respect and timely care. Please take a moment to consider the 5-star reviews on here. Many of them sound completely false and do not reflect the reality of this practice’s service.

recent_reviews.author: Amy
recent_reviews.text: UPDATE 2: The Practice Manager (Sophie Whitehead) took the time to speak to me and my partner in person. She addressed our concerns and has assured me that steps will be taken to minimise potential issues in future. After taking good & friendly treatment from a few members of staff into consideration, I've changed my rating from a 0/1 to a 4. UPDATE: The situation has gotten worse, I ended up on the phone for around 2 hours trying to get my appointment, was given an after hours appointment 12 days later. I had the appointment but because it was after hours, couldn't book in for bloods. So I was told to come in the next day in person to book in with daytime reception, which I tried to do (after waiting at least 20 mins in queue). I had to collect sample pots, book in for a blood test, a GP appointment for a referral and to hand in a urine sample I'd been given at my GP appointment the day before. The receptionist told me they "didn't have the authority to give (me) sample pots", they "couldn't accept (my) sample because there wasn't a form" and that they couldn't book any appointments for me. They said they couldn't see my notes, even though I'd watched the GP typing them up and she explained they would be available on all 6 practice systems (although I was in Harwood for the appointment anyway). The receptionist said I would have to speak to the Practice Manager, they would call me in the morning - I explained wouldn't be available in the morning and my phone blocks private numbers automatically so they said I needed to call in, I asked when and they said I could come in person, I tried to clarify whether she meant I had to phone in first or could just come in and she wouldn't give me a clear answer, just kept repeating that she couldn't do anything and I should call in and everything would be sorted tomorrow. So I went in today to talk to the Practice Manager as I'd been told I needed to do, but receptionists had no idea about any of the previous. I was in there at least 30 minutes (I was the only person waiting for around 10 minutes). The receptionists ended up printing off the forms and giving me sample pots with no issues and booked me in for the appointments I needed. Other than confusion over blood tests (because I already have a separate blood test related appointment) - the receptionists were able to do everything I had been told *couldn't* be done without talking to the Practice Manager. So once again I have had my treatment/appointments delayed because of a receptionist. I CAN NOT EMPHASISE ENOUGH, AVOID THE HARWOOD MEDICAL GROUP PRACTICES. Original Review: I don't know where to start. GPs who don't listen and deny urgent appointments and blood tests (until A&E step in) causing unnecessary and potentially harmful delays in treatment, last minute cancellations of appointments because they decide patients "aren't eligible" (with no evidence to back it up, for arbitrary reasons), gaslighting from GPs, gatekeeping by receptionists, online services which don't work, and now I've spent the last few days waiting to make an appointment (I was told to wait until today for appointments to be available) only to spend over an hour on the phone on hold (with multiple attempts where I couldn't even get through) only to go through a queue of 7 people, get to position 1 to be hung up on, then a queue of 8 people, position 2, hung up on, now I'm waiting again (currently over 23 minutes to get to position 6 from 8). Absolute nightmare.

They said they couldn't see my notes, even though I'd watched the GP typing them up and she explained they would be available on all 6 practice systems (although I was in Harwood for the appointment anyway). The receptionist said I would have to speak to the Practice Manager, they would call me in the morning - I explained wouldn't be available in the morning and my phone blocks private numbers automatically so they said I needed to call in, I asked when and they said I could come in person, I tried to clarify whether she meant I had to phone in first or could just come in and she wouldn't give me a clear answer, just kept repeating that she couldn't do anything and I should call in and everything would be sorted tomorrow. So I went in today to talk to the Practice Manager as I'd been told I needed to do, but receptionists had no idea about any of the previous. I was in there at least 30 minutes (I was the only person waiting for around 10 minutes). The receptionists ended up printing off the forms and giving me sample pots with no issues and booked me in for the appointments I needed. Other than confusion over blood tests (because I already have a separate blood test related appointment) - the receptionists were able to do everything I had been told *couldn't* be done without talking to the Practice Manager. So once again I have had my treatment/appointments delayed because of a receptionist. I CAN NOT EMPHASISE ENOUGH, AVOID THE HARWOOD MEDICAL GROUP PRACTICES. Original Review: I don't know where to start. GPs who don't listen and deny urgent appointments and blood tests (until A&E step in) causing unnecessary and potentially harmful delays in treatment, last minute cancellations of appointments because they decide patients "aren't eligible" (with no evidence to back it up, for arbitrary reasons), gaslighting from GPs, gatekeeping by receptionists, online services which don't work, and now I've spent the last few days waiting to make an appointment (I was told to wait until today for appointments to be available) only to spend over an hour on the phone on hold (with multiple attempts where I couldn't even get through) only to go through a queue of 7 people, get to position 1 to be hung up on, then a queue of 8 people, position 2, hung up on, now I'm waiting again (currently over 23 minutes to get to position 6 from 8). recent_reviews.author: Ren Ashi
recent_reviews.text: Well what can I say, what a lovely caring practice this is!!!! I am from Merseyside but my grandmother Mary Anderson-W is a patient here who has been very poorly for months, in and out of hospital & at the moment residing in a nursing home temporarily to have rehabilitation. During her stay in hospital her hearing aid was lost & she has been struggling for months with no hearing due to the lost hearing aid! I telephoned this surgery desperate for any help/support for nan with this issue & was given a telephone appt with nans GP Dr Leach who telephoned me & listened to my queries etc about everything re: Nans hearing loss and other well being such as flu jab/covid booster etc! What a lovely doctor and what lovely admin/reception team you have here!!!! I felt really supported and that nan is cared about and to top all that Dr Leach acted immediately to process 'urgent referral' to the audiology department for an up to date hearing test/hearing aid for nan & the very next day I heard back from the admin team with all the details for me to arrange appointment for nan next week!!! She is thrilled & so am I & all the family at this result! Just had to write a warm review to express this! I couldn't be more grateful 🙏 honestly! My nan is '87 yrs old & it means the world to me to know she is in safe hands at this wonderful surgery especially as I live out of town!! Many Many Thanks To You All 🙏 😊🌈 God bless our NHS we are so so lucky!
